  We verify the hypotheses and determine recurrence-transience regimes for symmetric and anisotropic stable processes, symmetric uniformly elliptic diffusions, generalized squared-Bessel products on $[0,\infty)^d$, and symmetric bilateral Bessel-type diffusions on $R^d$ and their nonsingular linear images. Finally, we derive quantitative sufficient conditions for survival of total mass in semilinear equations with absorption, including time-dependent diffusion rates. Here survival means that the limiting total mass is strictly positive. For a hyperbolic diffusion, this holds for every $\beta>0$ in the absorption term $-v^{1+\beta}$.

papers.title: Quenched large deviation estimates for skew product systems with the almost-sure fiber specification property
papers.authors: Xue Liu, Xiaomin Zhou, Xiaoyao Zhou
papers.abstract: We establish quenched level-2 large deviation estimates for empirical measures of measurable skew products with compact metric fibers over an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation on a Polish space. Our hypotheses are formulated through lower and upper energy functions, which describe the exponential decay of conditional measures of fiber Bowen balls. Under almost-sure fiber specification, we prove lower bounds for open sets. Upper bounds for closed convex sets require only the upper energy condition, and upper semicontinuity of fiber entropy removes the convexity restriction. When these hypotheses hold with a common energy function \(T\), we obtain a quenched level-2 large deviation principle with a good rate function \(I_T(\rho)=\int T\,d\rho-h_\rho(F)\) on invariant measures with the prescribed base marginal, and \(+\infty\) otherwise. We also derive quenched level-1 large deviation principles for bounded continuous observables and a quenched Laplace principle. As an application, we consider skew products that are Anosov and topologically mixing on fibers. For Gibbs equilibrium states associated with random potentials $f$ having integrable two-sided Bowen variation, we construct bounded strictly positive common energy functions by coboundary corrections. This construction identifies the large deviation rate on invariant measures as \(\pi_F(f)-h_\rho(F)-\int f\,d\rho\), where \(\pi_F(f)\) denotes the fiber topological pressure.

papers.title: Divide-and-Conquer is Tail- and Anomaly-Robust: Factor Model Estimation Without Moment Constraints
papers.authors: Zetai Cen, Han Yan, Haeran Cho
papers.abstract: We study robust estimation of elliptical factor models with abnormal observations and without requiring the existence of any positive moments. In particular, a divide-and-conquer (DC) estimator averages orthogonal projectors onto the full column spaces of small data blocks, and we rigorously establish its probability bound that allows weak and heterogeneous factors. The derived convergence rate is comparable to that of classical principal component estimators, up to the proportion of anomalies. Building on our DC estimator, we propose a split-sample tail- and anomaly-robust (STAR) estimator for the factor number using sample medians of successive projected coordinate ratios, which is shown consistent under mild conditions. Subsequent factor and common component estimation is also discussed, with the rates of convergence spelled out. Remarkably, given an upper bound on the true factor number, our suite of procedures are free from tuning, require no tail-dependent truncation threshold nor solving an optimization problem, admit parallel block computations, and hence has the same computational complexity as the classical principal component methods. Extensive experiments corroborate our theoretical findings, where DC and STAR are comparable and often outperform state-of-the-art competitors. We also illustrate our methods on a portfolio return dataset.

papers.title: How good are spline spaces for the Kolmogorov $n$-width of a Sobolev ball?
papers.abstract: This paper studies the approximation power of polynomial splines on a uniform one-dimensional mesh. The quality of the best approximation of the unit ball of $H^{s}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace, measured in the $L^{2}$ norm, is quantified by the sup-inf of that space: for each function in the Sobolev ball, take its minimal approximation error over the space, and then take the supremum of these errors over the ball. The infimum of this sup-inf over all $n$-dimensional spaces is the well-known Kolmogorov $n$-width $d_{n}$. Choosing the $n$-dimensional subspace to be the piecewise polynomial space of degree $k$ with smoothness $C^{\mu}$ ($-1\le\mu\le k-1$) gives our sup-inf $E$. The approximation accuracy of spline spaces is then examined by comparing $d_{n}$ and $E$. The two quantities are determined by two eigenvalue problems, through which we obtain a lower bound for $d_{n}$ and an upper bound for $E$. Under the restriction $k\ge s-1$, the upper bound for the error of the maximally smooth spline space ($\mu=k-1$) is asymptotically equal to the lower bound for $d_n$, showing that uniform $B$-splines are asymptotically optimal among all $n$-dimensional spaces. For $\mu<k-1$, we prove that $E/d_n$ is bounded below by a constant strictly larger than $1$, except when $k>s-1$ and $\mu=k-2$ hold simultaneously. This reveals the superiority of $B$-splines in the sense of $n$-widths. Numerical experiments corroborate these bounds and, in some cases (e.g. the exception above), show that they are sharp.

papers.title: Polynomial conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov maps derived from train track representatives
papers.abstract: We investigate two kinds of polynomials associated with pseudo-Anosov maps. Each kind consists of three polynomials that are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes and these polynomials contain more information than pseudo-Anosov stretch factors. The first kind is defined by the train track representatives. The second kind is obtained from the first kind by incorporating additional data that encode the transitions among the unpunctured singularities of the invariant foliations. The Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials coincide with those of the second kind. As an application, we prove that the Birman-Brinkmann-Kawamuro polynomials are conjugacy invariants of pseudo-Anosov mapping classes which is also proved by Dodge-Kawamuro, independently.

papers.title: Generalized near-group tensor categories
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a finite tensor category with exactly one isomorphism class of simple objects which are non-invertible.
  Semisimple tensor categories $\mathcal{D}$ with this property are called near-group categories, and have been studied by Evans, Gannon, Siehler and others. In this paper, we study such categories in the non-semisimple setting, with the additional assumption that the non-invertible simple object is projective. Specifically, we consider the case when $\mathcal{D}$ admits a fiber functor and has a unique semisimple abelian block (in the general case that $\D$ is not semisimple). We describe the structure of such categories and their corresponding Hopf algebras, and construct examples of such categories with a cyclic Picard group. We obtain additional results when the Frobenius-Perron dimension of the unique non-invertible simple object is a prime number.

papers.title: Weighted Logarithm Laws in non-commutative Probability
papers.abstract: We prove analogues of weighted laws of iterated logarithm and laws of logarithm for non-commutative martingales and independent random variables respectively. First we obtain a weighted LIL for non-commutative martingales, extending the sharp unweighted result of arXiv:2509.22037v2 to the case for polynomial weights, then by approximation to a broader class of functions. Then we proved a weighted law of logarithm for triangular array of weights and replacing the coefficient in the denominator by regularly varying functions with index $\alpha$. We show that the normalised sums converge to 0 for $\alpha> 1/2$ and for the case $\alpha=1/2$, we obtain the sharp upper bound with constant $\sqrt{2}$.

papers.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
papers.abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.

papers.title: Discrete-Time Zero-Sum Markov Games with Control, Stopping, and State-Dependent Discounting
papers.abstract: We study a discrete-time two-player zero-sum stochastic game with control and stopping, where both players can stop the game, the discount factors depends on the states, and the running and terminal rewards may be unbounded. A contraction argument for the constrained Shapley equation establishes the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium consisting of stationary controls and stopping times. We further provides algorithms for approximating the value and computing an $\varepsilon$-Nash equilibrium. A numerical example with state-dependent discount factors illustrates the results.

papers.title: Basis selection, universal sampling discretization, and sampling recovery
papers.authors: Feng Dai, Jiashu Ran, Vladimir N. Temlyakov
papers.abstract: For every real $N$-dimensional subspace of $L_2$, we construct one orthonormal basis such that, for every $1\le v\le N$, at most $Cv\log(eN/v)$ positively weighted samples discretize the squared $L_2$ norm of all $v$-term combinations. Random rotations also give simultaneous weighted $L_p$ estimates and a sharp $C\log(eN)$ bound for the squared $L_2$ norm of the pointwise maximum. For prescribed coefficient classes, a change of measure yields sampling recovery estimates from $Cv\log^3(2v)$ samples under a lower Riesz inequality and a common square-integrable pointwise bound.

papers.title: Directional Ergodic Theorems, Ergodicity, and Weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions
papers.authors: Chunlin Liu, Kairan Liu, Tao Yu
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study Birkhoff and von Neumann type ergodic theorems for $\mathbb Z^2$-measure preserving systems along irrational directions. This leads us to a further investigation of directional ergodicity and weak mixing. Additionally, we show that our framework (dynamical definitions) is equivalent to the spectral definitions of directional ergodicity and weak mixing introduced by Robinson, Rosenblatt and \c{S}ahin \cite{RRS2023} for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions.
  We note that in their recent paper \cite{RS2026}, Robinson and \c{S}ahin established the equivalence between dynamical and spectral directional weak mixing for $\mathbb Z^2$-actions using an approach fundamentally different from the one employed in the present paper.

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.authors: Kenneth Ascher, Kristin DeVleming, Hongyu Luo, Yuchen Liu, Junyan Zhao
papers.abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Nonexistence of positive solutions stable outside a compact set for the Lane--Emden system in a half-space
papers.authors: Zetao Cheng, Long-Han Huang, Wenming Zou
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension and for all positive exponents, the Lane--Emden system in a half-space with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions admits no positive classical solution stable outside a compact set.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
papers.authors: Jayan Mukherjee, with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.

papers.title: High-order long-time stable methods for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations
papers.authors: Fukeng Huang, Jie Shen, Xiaoming Wang
papers.abstract: We present in this paper two scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) correction steps for constructing long-time stable schemes for the forced incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with no-slip boundary conditions. A main feature is that the same correction steps apply to any linear predictor satisfying the order and spatial regularity requirements in Assumption~P. Their construction and stability analysis are independent of the particular form of the predictor and require no energy estimate for it. The first correction uses a damped, shifted kinetic-energy variable to obtain a uniform-in-time $L^2$ bound in two and three dimensions, together with a weighted dissipation estimate. In two dimensions, the second correction combines a higher-energy auxiliary variable with a scalar relaxation to yield a uniform-in-time $H^1$ bound. Under the stated assumptions, these estimates hold on arbitrary positive time grids, without restrictions on step sizes or adjacent step ratios. We also derive eventual absorbing bounds; for the two-SAV scheme, these apply to the admissible initial class associated with fixed parameters. The generalized BDF schemes require one constant-coefficient Helmholtz solve per velocity component and one pressure Poisson solve per step; the second correction adds no field solve. Numerical experiments exhibit second-, third-, and fourth-order convergence for the tested BDF schemes and illustrate the long-time stability and efficiency of adaptive time stepping.

papers.title: Bulgarian solitaire with distinguishable cells
papers.abstract: Classical Bulgarian solitaire tracks only the sizes of the stacks. We ask how the lengths of its periodic orbits change when individual cards are distinguished. To study this question, we introduce four actions $T_1,T_2,T_3,T_4$ on partitions with labeled cells. The actions differ in whether the top or bottom cell is removed from each column and in the order in which the removed cells are arranged to form a new column. We determine the exact sizes of the periodic orbits for all four actions. The main work lies in the analysis of $T_2$, for which we develop a coloring algorithm on Ferrers diagrams. The coloring encodes the cycle structure of the permutation of the labels induced by one full period of the underlying partition.

papers.title: An introduction to discrete dynamics in condensed sets: orbits, periodic loci, and arithmetic examples
papers.abstract: We formulate discrete dynamics internally in the topos Cond of condensed sets. For an endomorphism $f\colon X\to X$, we construct orbit quotients, backward histories, preimage trees, and periodic loci as objects evaluated on profinite parameter spaces. The framework recovers global-section dynamics, fully faithfully embeds compact Hausdorff systems, characterizes the invertible extension, and is compatible with inverse limits. It organizes $p$-adic congruence towers and shows, for a Cantor-type non-Archimedean Julia set, that classical periodic points can be dense although the internal periodic locus is not isomorphic to the compact condensed Julia set.

papers.title: Uniqueness and stability of Appleton's solitons
papers.abstract: We prove that Appleton's noncollapsed steady gradient Ricci solitons on complex line bundles over positive K\"ahler--Einstein manifolds are the unique such solitons arising from his metric ansatz. We then show that the four-dimensional examples on $O_{\mathbb{CP}^1}(-k)$, $k \geq 3$, are strictly linearly stable. By a result of Deruelle, this implies dynamical stability under the Ricci flow.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $\eta>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(\eta^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincar\'e inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

papers.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
papers.abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.

papers.title: GEAR: A GPU-Accelerated Global Solver for Bounded Continuous Nonlinear Programs via Linear Bound Propagation
papers.authors: Duo Zhou, Hesun Chen, Xiangru Zhong, Grani A. Hanasusanto, Huan Zhang
papers.abstract: We present a novel GPU-accelerated global solver for constrained nonlinear programming (NLP) inspired by the efficient linear bound propagation framework in neural network (NN) verification. Existing work on NN verification, a problem that can be cast as feasibility detection for a nonlinear objective, demonstrated orders-of-magnitude speedups with the linear bound propagation-based framework when compared to traditional solvers. Extending this paradigm to global nonlinear programming requires addressing many challenges: a global constrained NLP solver must effectively exploit all, possibly unstructured, nonlinear constraints to improve the objective, whereas NN verification typically handles simple input box constraints over a well-structured NN and does not directly optimize an objective function. We address these challenges by fully exploiting the linear bounds produced by bound propagation: these linear bounds can be viewed as relaxations of nonlinear constraints and used to provide lower bounds, check infeasibility, and guide the search for a primal solution. In addition, we propose tighter linear relaxations for bilinear, quotient, and other commonly used nonlinear functions in NLP problems, and a projected augmented Lagrangian method tightly coupled to our dual solving procedure to produce primal solutions. Our method solves 421 of 505 bounded and continuous NLP problems in the GAMS and MINLPLib benchmarks under a 180-second limit, more than each of the six global solvers we compare with, including Gurobi and BARON (commercial), and SCIP (open-source). Sixteen of these problems are certified by none of the six global solvers; all of them contain exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric terms, which are often challenging for traditional approaches. Project webpage is at https://verified-intelligence.github.io/GEAR.

papers.title: Local vanishing density of order $1$ and Divisor moments
papers.abstract: We establish a general framework relating local vanishing densities of order $1$ to logarithmic growth of divisor moments on regular arithmetic curves. As applications, we recover classical divisor moment estimates for polynomial values and establish their function field analogue. Furthermore, under GRH, we obtain a result on divisor moments for polynomials in the Fourier coefficients of non-CM cuspidal eigenforms with trivial nebentypus and trivial inner twist. The Fourier coefficients need not be integers, and the polynomials need not be squarefree. Under additional analytic hypotheses, we also allow a Sato--Tate angle restriction.

papers.title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
papers.authors: An Ping, Zhichao Peng, Pengliang Yang
papers.abstract: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.

papers.title: A Zero-Free Sum of Cauchy Kernels with Positive Coefficients
papers.abstract:
We construct a zero-free meromorphic function \[
  f(z)=\sum_n\frac{c_n}{z-a_n},\qquad
  c_n>0,\qquad |a_n|\to\infty,\qquad
  \sum_{a_n\ne0}\frac{c_n}{|a_n|}<\infty, \] thereby disproving the Clunie--Eremenko--Rossi conjecture. The construction starts from a product of two rotated Airy functions. The zeros of this product are shifted simultaneously so that all residues of $f$ are positive. The poles lie on the rays $e^{\pm i\pi/3}[0,\infty)$. The resulting function has order and lower order $3/2$, and the sum of its residues in the disc $|z|\le r$ is asymptotic to $\frac{4}{3\pi}r^{3/4}$.

papers.title: Geometric Stochastic Dynamics and Fokker-Planck Equation on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$
papers.abstract: This paper develops a geometric (coordinate-free) stochastic model of a controlled point mass evolving on the unit two-sphere $\mathbb S^2$, together with the Fokker-Planck equation governing the probability density of the resulting stochastic process. The state manifold is the tangent bundle $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. The Levi-Civita connection of the round metric is used to construct the horizontal-vertical splitting of $\mathsf{T}(\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2)$ and to convert the intrinsic second-order dynamics of the system into a first-order controlled vector field on $\mathsf{T}\mathbb S^2$. Endowing the tangent bundle with the Sasaki metric then permits stochastic perturbations to be introduced intrinsically and independently in horizontal, i.e., position, and vertical, i.e., velocity, directions. The corresponding infinitesimal generator is obtained in horizontal-vertical Hessian form. The probability density is defined with respect to the Sasaki Riemannian volume measure. The Fokker-Planck equation is derived intrinsically in both Stratonovich and It\^o forms. In the It\^o representation, a globally defined horizontal-vertical diffusion tensor yields a compact double-divergence Fokker-Planck PDE. No coordinates or embedded Euclidean representation of the sphere dynamics are used in the development. Numerical simulations illustrate the stochastic motion of a controlled particle ensemble on $\mathbb S^2$ toward an antipodal target configuration.

papers.title: Multivariate Pellarin $L$-values on algebraic curves
papers.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu
papers.abstract: We establish a generating trace formula for multicharacter ideal-type $L$-values associated with rank-one Drinfeld modules. For a sign-normalized Hayes module with free period lattice, the formula realizes the $L$-values at weights $n\equiv s\pmod{q^{\deg_\infty}-1}$ as a trace over the ordinary Hilbert class field. We further characterize the polynomials in the exponential variable $X$ arising in multicharacter lattice generating identities over arbitrary function rings. Their coefficients are given explicitly via the shtuka basis, which gives concrete control over their supports and degrees. This completely settles an open problem of Pellarin and Perkins: these polynomials are all constant if and only if $s<2q$. The results on coefficients apply to curves of arbitrary genus, infinite places of arbitrary degree, and nonprincipal period lattices.

papers.title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for the Unitary M\"obius Function
papers.abstract: Let $g(n)=(-1)^{\omega(n)}$, where $\omega(n)$ denotes the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. We prove that, for every sufficiently large integer $N$, each ordered additive sign pattern $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$ occurs at least $N/(128(\log N)^3)$ times. We also prove that, for every $N\ge18$ and every $s,t\in\sgnset$, there is at least one integer $1\le a<N$ such that $(g(a),g(N-a))=(s,t)$. In addition, we establish a one-quarter asymptotic formula for almost all target integers. Finally, we discuss Goldbach-type problems for the ordinary M\"obius function and formulate related questions.

papers.title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
papers.abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.

papers.title: Error Estimates and Convergence Analysis for Learning Mechanism--AI Coupled Dynamical Systems
papers.authors: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Yuan Lou, Shuangshuang Yin
papers.abstract: Mechanism--AI coupled dynamical systems retain known mechanisms while learning unknown dynamics from data. We study how neural approximation, numerical integration, finite observations, and optimization jointly affect the accuracy of this learning process. For time-dependent learned terms in a fixed compact admissible class, we derive a four-component objective error bound within an optimal control formulation. Explicit estimates are obtained for constrained ReLU approximation and Euler integration, with deterministic quadrature and random sampling treated separately. Under joint refinement, we establish $\Gamma$-convergence of the approximate objectives and show that approximate minimizers approach the continuous optimal set when the global optimization gaps vanish. We also derive conditional stability estimates for state-dependent learned terms. Numerical experiments with a susceptible--infected--recovered (SIR) model illustrate the analysis and show how solver resolution affects continuous-trajectory accuracy even when training losses are similar.

papers.title: Geometric classification of Noether invariants of the Time-Dependent damped Duffing Oscillator
papers.authors: Michael Tsamparlis, and Aniekan Magnus Ukpong
papers.abstract: We present a systematic geometric classification of the Noether point symmetries of time-dependent conformal Lagrangians of the form $L = A(t)\left(\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}\dot{x}^{i}\dot{x}^{j} - V(x)\right)$, whose Euler--Lagrange equations describe dynamical systems with time-dependent linear damping. The classification is carried out by coupling the temporal parameters of the conformal factor $A(t)$ with the homothetic algebra of the kinetic metric $g_{ij}$ through a set of compatibility and integrability conditions. The central result is a main theorem which determines the Noether generators, the associated gauge functions and the resulting invariants. The theorem splits naturally into two cases according to whether the quantity $D - 2\psi$ is non-zero or zero, with further subcases depending on whether the homothetic vectors are gradient or non-gradient. The theorem imposes no restrictions on $A(t)$, $g_{ij}$ or $V(x)$, and is therefore fully general and covariant. We apply the theorem to the time-dependent damped Duffing oscillator (DDO) in Euclidean space $E^{3}$ with $A(t) = e^{\gamma t}$ and potential $V = \frac{1}{2}a\,r^{2} + \frac{% \lambda}{4}r^{4}$. For the damped harmonic oscillator ($\lambda = 0$) the theorem reproduces the classical Bateman invariant as a special case. For the anharmonic case we obtain a new exact time-dependent quadratic invariant, valid when the linear stiffness satisfies $a = 2\gamma^{2}/9$. Each invariant is verified explicitly by direct differentiation along the equations of motion. The new invariant provides a rare example of a global conservation law for a fully nonlinear dissipative system, and can be used for the integration and quantization of the DDO.

papers.title: On the structural aspects of Convex Subhyperlattices under different orders
papers.authors: N Aishwarya Nayak, Bhargava K, Pallavi Panjarike, Kuncham Syam Prasad, Tapatee Sahoo, Harikrishnan Panackal
papers.abstract: Nayak et al. (2025) introduced the concept of convex subhyperlattices of a strong join hyperlattice $\mathfrak{L}$ and demonstrated that the collection of all convex subhyperlattices, $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$, together with empty set, forms a lattice. In particular, for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices, they obtained a unique representation of convex subhyperlattices in terms of hyperideals and hyperfilters. In the present work, we extend these studies by proving that $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L}) \cup \{\emptyset\}$, under set inclusion, forms an algebraic lattice. Moreover, we introduce two new orders on $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$ and examine their properties, including conditions for equivalence of these orders. In the class of $P$-hyperlattices, we characterize convex subhyperlattices in terms of initial and final segments, providing a structural insight into their formation. When convexity is extended to arbitrary join hyperlattices, many results known for $P$-hyperlattices and Nakano hyperlattices fail to hold. To address these limitations of convexity in arbitrary hyperlattices, we introduce the notion of strongly convex sets, denoted $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$, which naturally generalizes the concept while preserving its fundamental properties and extends the applicability of results to a wider setting. We establish several results for $\operatorname{SC}(\mathfrak{L})$ that do not hold for $\operatorname{CS}(\mathfrak{L})$.

papers.title: An exact K\"ahler form on $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ without a global SYZ fibration
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit exact K\"ahler form on \((\mathbb C^*)^2\) admitting no almost-toric fibration and hence no smooth Lagrangian torus fibration. For the logarithmic holomorphic volume form, we also rule out any special Lagrangian fibrations with compact fibers and dense regular locus, even when arbitrary compact connected singular fibers are allowed. For higher dimensions, taking products also yields explicit exact K\"ahler forms on \((\mathbb C^*)^n\), for every \(n\ge2\), admitting no smooth proper Lagrangian torus fibration.

papers.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on all smooth 13-spheres
papers.authors: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Junna Ni
papers.abstract: Every smooth homotopy $13$-sphere admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive sectional curvature. We construct a special $S^3$--$S^3$ bundle over $S^{13}$ whose star quotient represents the nonzero class $\pm\alpha_1\beta_1\in\Theta_{13}\cong\mathbb Z/3$. The defining equivariant map factors through the Blakers--Massey map by a smooth Hopf construction representing an unstable $J$-generator. This factorisation retains the prescribed base representation and makes Schultz's plumbing composition formula applicable; a normal-invariant computation in smoothing theory then identifies the smooth structure. On the quotient we implement the compatible-disk strategy with complete curvature estimates on arbitrary two-planes, matching boundary metrics, and a strictly positive sum of outward second fundamental forms. A direct smoothing argument completes the metric construction. Orientation reversal gives the remaining nonzero class in $\Theta_{13}$.

papers.title: Formal Proof of an Anisotropic Calder\'on Uniqueness Theorem
papers.abstract: We announce a Lean~4 formal proof of a special case of the smooth anisotropic Calder\'on uniqueness theorem released by OpenAI on October 6, 2026. We consider smooth Riemannian metrics on the three-dimensional unit ball, with full boundary measurements and Euclidean extensions outside the ball. OpenAI's release did not include a Lean proof of their uniqueness result. Our formalization uses results from Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it is given as a solution to a Lean comparator challenge whose check permits only the standard axioms of Lean. The Lean proof is not a line-by-line translation of the OpenAI manuscript.

papers.title: On the domain of attraction of source--type solutions of the porous medium equations
papers.abstract: We study the rate of convergence to Barenblatt profiles of the solutions to porous medium equations in $\R^n, n \ge 1$, by means of a certain class of Energy distances, a class of discrepancies between probability measures which have been recently widely used in problems related to AI, in particular for tasks related to machine learning. If $n \ge 3$, it is shown both that the rate of decay in Energy distance is improved with respect to known results which are based on the decay of relative entropy, and that, with respect to this distance, any initial value of bounded mass belongs to the domain of attraction of the source--type solution. Similar results are shown to hold for the fast diffusion case.

papers.title: Removing the floor from Hoeffding and Bernstein inequalities for finite-population U-statistics
papers.authors: Jianhang Ai, Yiming Chen, Ond\v{r}ej Ku\v{z}elka, Yuyi Wang
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a uniformly sampled $n$-element subset of a finite population $D$ of size $N$, and let $U_C$ be the complete U-statistic of order $k$ built from a bounded kernel on the $k$-subsets of $D$. We prove a product inequality for the uniform distribution on $\binom{D}{n}$ and deduce from it the comparison $ \log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\theta(U_C-\mathbb{E}U_C)}\right] \le \frac{n}{k}\log \mathbb{E}\left[e^{\frac{k\theta}{n}(Y-\mathbb{E}Y)}\right]$, where $Y$ is a single kernel value taken at a uniformly sampled $k$-subset of $D$. This yields Hoeffding, Bennett and Bernstein inequalities for $U_C$ with effective sample size $n/k$ in place of the $\lfloor n/k\rfloor$ available so far. The gain is negligible when $n$ is much larger than $k$, but it approaches a factor of two in the exponent when $k$ is close to $n$.

papers.title: The cofinite regularity spectrum of $F$-irregular graphs
papers.abstract: For a connected graph $F$, a graph $G$ is $F$-irregular if the numbers of copies of $F$ containing its vertices are pairwise distinct. We characterize which connected patterns admit regular $F$-irregular hosts of every sufficiently large degree. Stars admit no regular $F$-irregular host; for every other $F$, every sufficiently large integer $r$ is realized by a connected $r$-regular $F$-irregular graph of diameter two and order $r+o(r)$, optimal to first order. For triangles, and equivalently four-vertex paths in regular graphs, we construct such hosts of order less than $r+73r^{\log29/\log58}$ above an explicit threshold, with the constant reduced to $44$ for even $r$. Lexicographic words encode distinct rooted subgraph counts, while layered connections allow the common degree to be prescribed. Rooted-homomorphism expansions and spectral amplification establish separation for general patterns; an exact uniform-increment identity gives the quantitative triangle construction. The finite seed graphs are explicitly constructed, and their required rooted-count distinctions are verified by exact-arithmetic certificates.

papers.title: On Relative Greedy Weights
papers.abstract: Relative greedy weights were introduced by Li and Liu in [19] as a measure of information leakage in coordinated two-party wire-tap channels of type II when the adversary follows a greedy strategy. Their definition can be viewed as a relative version of the CEZ greedy weights, which are only locally greedy. In this paper, we revisit the concept of greediness and relative greediness introducing new measures, and we discuss other perhaps more relevant applications of relative greedy weights than the coordinated two-party wire-tap channel of type II. We pay special attention to bottom-up greedy weights, which correspond to an adversary with an ultimate greedy approach, and we present families of nested codes for which such weights are larger than the relative CEZ greedy weights.

papers.title: Learning-Assisted Beamforming Optimization for Hybrid XL-RIS-Aided Communication
papers.abstract: Hybrid active-passive extremely large-scale reconfigurable intelligent surface (XL-RIS) architectures mitigate the double-hop path loss of passive RIS while enabling near-field spatial energy focusing, but impose a computationally intensive mixed discrete-continuous beamforming design problem under strict radio-frequency (RF) power constraints. This paper investigates a hybrid XL-RIS-assisted downlink multi-user multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) system in the near-field regime. The joint optimization of the base station (BS) precoder, discrete XL-RIS phase shifts, and active-element amplification gains is addressed via a discrete coordinate ascent (DCA)-based alternating optimization (AO) framework, in which discrete variables are updated through local index-domain searches and the BS precoder is derived in closed form via a noise-aware minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. To reduce the per-sample computational cost for XL-RIS apertures, a deep unfolding (DU) framework is proposed as a low-complexity alternative, unrolling a fixed number of Riemannian gradient ascent steps on the sum-rate objective and recovering the discrete phase configuration via quantized phasor projection, with one learnable step size per layer trained in a self-supervised manner. Numerical results under near-field spherical-wave channel models confirm that the DU framework achieves sum-rate performance close to the AO scheme with substantially lower and nearly constant runtime, and that both schemes consistently outperform manifold optimization under discrete hardware constraints.

papers.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$
papers.abstract: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

papers.title: From many-body Schr\"odinger dynamics to magnetic Vlasov equation
papers.abstract: We analyse the combined mean-field and semiclassical limit from the time-dependent Schr\"odinger dynamics of $N$ spinless fermions in a non-constant magnetic field to the magnetic Vlasov equation with scaling $\hbar = N^{-1/3}$. With the velocity-shifted coherent states and the induced magnetic Husimi measure, we derive an exact BBGKY hierarchy with a remainder of order $\hbar^{1/2-}$. The main result is the weak $L^1$ convergence of the $k$-particle magnetic Husimi measures to the $k$-copies of the solution to the magnetic Vlasov equation. Furthermore, the convergence holds in the Wasserstein distance $\mathbb{W}_2$ when the second moment of initial Husimi measure correspondingly converges.

papers.title: Strong relaxed dynamics in stochastic control
papers.abstract:
We characterize relaxed dynamics for which any finite family of strong state solutions, together with their relaxed inputs, can be approximated by the prescribed controlled dynamics, ground-stably in law.
  Relaxed inputs include parametrizations of relaxed controls over the unit interval. Unlike relaxed controls, these parametrizations determine action couplings. The proposed relaxed dynamics is driven by a single cylindrical Brownian motion in a Hilbert space. For each relaxed input, its state is the unique strong solution of the corresponding equation. The collection of these states, over all relaxed inputs, satisfies the approximation requirement.
  Conversely, suppose one assigns to each relaxed input a continuous adapted state process on a fixed probability space. Pairwise approximation forces the assignment to be the strong solution map of the same dynamics, for a unique cylindrical Brownian driver. In fact, even for a state map indexed by (non-parametrized) relaxed controls, the relevant relaxed control class admits coherent parametrizations under separability and finite-family approximation assumptions, and the same type of dynamics is recovered again.

papers.title: Curvature estimates for stable hypersurfaces of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional
papers.authors: Hongbin Cui, Xiaowei Xu, Shoulan Yi
papers.abstract: A hypersurface $\Sigma \subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is called EDH-stable if it is a critical point of the Euler-Dierkes-Huisken functional $\mathcal{E}_\alpha(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma|x|^\alpha\, d\mathcal{H}^n$ with nonnegative second variation, which was introduced by Dierkes and Huisken in \cite{[DH-24]}. In this paper, we first establish a Bellettini-type $\epsilon$-regularity theorem and use it, together with tangent cone analysis, to derive curvature estimates for EDH-stable hypersurfaces with $2\leq n \leq 6$.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.

papers.title: Mean Field Limit Towards Kinetic Equation with Repulsive Dirac-Delta Potential
papers.authors: Jos\'{e} A. Carrillo, Li Chen, Paul Nikolaev
papers.abstract: A one-particle effective kinetic equation with repulsive Dirac-Delta potential in one dimension is rigorously derived from a moderate interacting second order particle system. It is proved that the Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure and the solution of Vlasov equation converges to zero. A convergence rate is obtained by a combination of the estimates for particle trajectory and a smoothed version of modulated energy.

papers.title: On the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers
papers.authors: Bingxin Jia, Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Wei Xiong
papers.abstract: Combining the frameworks of Chamizo--Iwaniec and Chamizo--Ubis with the recent character-sum and exponential-sum estimates of Bellotti and Kerr, we improve the error term in Gauss's mean value formulas for class numbers of binary quadratic forms from $O(N^{21/32+\eps})$ to $O(N^{55/84+\eps})$. If no Dirichlet $L$-function vanishes in $\mathrm{Re}\,s>7/8$, the exponent becomes $2274811/3487744$; under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions, it becomes $118/181$.

papers.title: Analytic criteria for criticality of subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operators
papers.abstract: For a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator, we introduce a quantity that plays a role analogous to the bottom of the spectrum of a Schr\"{o}dinger operator, and establish analytic criteria for subcriticality, criticality and supercriticality of a subordinated Schr\"{o}dinger operator.

papers.title: Remarks on spectral gaps on Gaussian path space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the relationship between spectral gaps of Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/$L^2$ operators on Gaussian path space and the underlying Volterra kernel $F$. This framework includes fractional Brownian motion $B^H$ with Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. For the fractional Wiener measure $\mu_H$, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with respect to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Dirichlet form holds for $H\geq\frac12$, whereas the corresponding weak Poincar\'e inequality fails for $0<H<\frac12$. The damped/$L^2$ Dirichlet forms satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for every $H\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: Total Variation Regularized Barycenters in Wasserstein Space
papers.abstract: We study total variation regularization of Wasserstein barycenters on bounded connected Lipschitz domains. We prove existence for arbitrary prescribed probability measures and uniqueness when at least one is absolutely continuous. Our main results are attained dual formulations in terms of relative perimeters and vector fields with zero normal trace. These yield necessary and sufficient optimality conditions and a variational characterization of superlevel sets. We also establish a maximum principle on convex domains, stability of minimizers, and an exact reduction to a single TV-JKO step in one dimension. The existence, uniqueness, and perimeter duality results extend to costs $|x-y|^p$, $p>1$, under the same assumptions.

papers.title: Iteration-Clock Selection for Euler Schemes of Degenerate Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study Euler--Maruyama approximation of the driftless one-dimensional SDE $dX_t=\sigma(X_t)\,dW_t$ when $\sigma$ vanishes at the origin and weak uniqueness fails because solutions may remain at zero for an arbitrary time. The central object is the logarithmic coefficient profile $q(Q)=-\log\sigma(e^{-Q})$. Under a two-sided logarithmic increment condition, with both indices in $(0,1/2)$, we show that weak-solution selection is governed by a deterministic iteration clock: if $N_q(Q)$ is the number of iterates of $q$ needed to reach a fixed reference depth and $hN_q(\log(1/|x_h|))\to d$, then the Euler scheme started from $x_h$ converges to the fundamental zero-sojourn diffusion delayed by $d$. This single theorem yields the common-index generalized-power law $d=\theta/|\log\alpha|$ when $h\log\log(1/|x_h|)\to\theta$, an effective translation-number formula for periodically modulated logarithmic profiles, a two-index delay window, and a sharpness construction in which, for one coefficient and one initialization family, the cluster set is the entire delay window. Thus the macroscopic selection mechanism is the iteration count of the logarithmic coefficient profile; the explicit double-logarithmic law of the homogeneous power case is its common-index closed form.

papers.title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.

papers.title: A Lie-theoretic approach to the type $C_n^{(1)}$ partitions of Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc
papers.abstract: Capparelli, Meurman, Primc and Primc (CMPP) extended the frequency conditions in Gordon's partition theorem to paths in coloured arrays. Their conjecture for type $C_n^{(1)}$ identifies the generating function of admissible arrays with a principally specialized character. We prove this conjecture for arbitrary boundary data by constructing an ordered Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt (PBW) basis of the corresponding integrable highest weight module. A decomposition of the admissible arrays and a tensor product argument establish linear independence of the corresponding monomial vectors. To prove spanning, we use relations from annihilating fields and PBW bases for modules over finite Levi subalgebras. Principal specialization then yields the conjectured product. The same basis identifies the number of parts with the degree in the associated graded module for the PBW filtration.

papers.title: Sharp Constants and First-Order Asymptotics in a Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu Formula for Riesz Potentials
papers.abstract: We investigate sharp constants and asymptotic properties of a pointwise inequality of Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu type in dimension \(n\geq2\), involving Riesz potentials and Spector's nonlinear fractional differential operator \(\mathcal D^\alpha\) of order \(0<\alpha<1\). For every \(n\geq3\) and \(0<\alpha<1\), we determine the optimal constant without symmetry restrictions and prove that it is attained by smooth radially monotone functions centered at the evaluation point. The proof combines geodesic-flow invariance, kernel monotonicity, and circular rearrangement. In dimension two, we establish the leading-order asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant and derive an explicit formula in the radial class. We further refine the pointwise limit established by A. Claros and C. P\'erez [Bourgain--Brezis--Mironescu formula for Riesz potentials, Adv. Math. 503 (2026), Art. 111226] by obtaining an explicit first-order correction with a quadratic remainder uniform in the spatial variable. Finally, we strengthen their convergence-in-measure result on compact subsets for functions in \(W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)\) by establishing almost-everywhere convergence as \(\alpha\to1^-\), without passing to a subsequence.

papers.title: Trivial solutions in Generalized Fermat equations
papers.authors: Pedro-Jos\'e Cazorla Garc\'ia, Ariel Pacetti, Lucas Villagra-Torcomian
papers.abstract: The modular method is a powerful tool to study generalized Fermat equations. Trivial solutions often become an obstruction to the method. While using hypergeometric motives to construct Galois representations, some of these solutions give rise to newforms with complex multiplication. In the present article, assuming a standard conjecture in Darmon's program, we prove that asymptotically any newform with complex multiplication cannot be related to a non-trivial primitive solution. This allows to discard all such newforms, including those associated to trivial solutions.

papers.title: Restricted Quantum unique ergodicity under Generalized Lindel\"of conjecture
papers.abstract: Assume the generalized Lindel\"of hypothesis. Let $u$ be an even Hecke--Maass cusp form on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})\backslash\mathbb{H}$, normalized in $L^2$ with respect to hyperbolic area, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. For every fixed $\psi\in C_c((0,\infty);\mathbb{C})$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that \[ \int_0^\infty \psi(y)|u(i y)|^2\frac{d y}{y} =\frac{6}{\pi}\int_0^\infty \psi(y)\frac{d y}{y} +O_{\psi,\varepsilon}(T^{-1/4+\varepsilon}) \] as $T\to\infty$, uniformly in $u$. In particular, the restriction mass equidistributes on every fixed compact segment of the imaginary axis in $\mathbb{H}$.

papers.title: Marginal Congruences and Elements for Two Commutator Words in Completely Regular Semigroups
papers.abstract: Motivated by Problem 13 posed by Ara\'ujo, Ara\'ujo and Kinyon \cite{Araujo2025} concerning marginal elements, subsemigroups and marginal equivalences associated with commutator words in completely regular semigroups, in this paper we investigate the two commutator words $ \omega_1(x,y)=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ and $ \omega_2(x,y)=(yx)^{-1}xy$ on completely regular semigroups. We prove that their marginal equivalences $\sim_{\omega_r}$ ($r=1,2$) coincide and are congruences. More precisely, for a completely regular semigroup $S$, we show that $a\sim_{\omega_r}b$ ($r=1,2$) if and only if $a^0=b^0=p$ and $b^{-1}a\in Z(pSp)$, where $Z(pSp)$ is the center of the monoid $pSp$, and so both words have the same set of marginal elements: \[ M_{\omega}(S) =\bigcup_{p\in E(S)} \bigl(Z(pSp)\cap H_p\bigr), \] where $E(S)$ is the set of idempotents in $S$. We also characterize when this set is a subsemigroup and establish alternative descriptions of the common marginal congruence and marginal elements.

papers.title: Zero extension for the Dirichlet problem on graphs
papers.authors: Yanglan Ou, Xuechao Yao, Guang Zhang
papers.abstract: Solutions of the Dirichlet problem on a finite part of a weighted graph are extended by zero, together with their source, to a larger connected part. A necessary and sufficient condition is proved for the extended function to remain a solution of the corresponding Dirichlet problem on the enlarged domain: at every newly included vertex adjacent to the original part, the weighted sum of the solution over its neighbors in that part must vanish. The admissible sources are characterized as the orthogonal complement of the harmonic extensions from the enlarged domain to the original part, their space has dimension equal to the number of vertices of the original part minus the rank of the interface coupling, and an exact energy identity for the extension error follows from a Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. The same reduction covers other boundary conditions, including the Neumann problem, and extends to higher powers of the Laplacian, where the boundary data must be compatible with the lower-order interface traces. The discrete criterion is compared with its continuous counterpart, and no result in this form has been reported on Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: Port-Hamiltonian Systems Beyond Joules: A Review of Unexpected Application Domains
papers.abstract: The port-Hamiltonian framework was built for mechanical and electrical systems, where the Hamiltonian is stored energy and the ports carry power. Over the past fifteen years it has spread to chemistry, cell biology, fusion plasmas, musical instruments, district heating, electricity markets, macroeconomics, predator-prey ecology, optimization algorithms and neural-network training. This review maps that spread. We classify each application by what its Hamiltonian really is: physical energy, a thermodynamic potential such as free energy or exergy, or an abstract storage function with no energetic meaning. The review keeps only sources whose bibliographic record we checked against Crossref. The picture that emerges is a continuum. Where a genuine thermodynamic potential exists, the theory is deep and constructive. Where the energy is borrowed, the framework still pays off through compositional interconnection and dissipation inequalities, but the work is younger and scattered. We close with a set of deliberately speculative research directions, including open port-Hamiltonian models of epidemics, opinion dynamics and supply chains, and learned port-Hamiltonian digital twins for structural health monitoring.

papers.title: Optimal rational spherical designs on the circle
papers.authors: Zhuo Cheng, Yeyao Hu, Deyu Yu
papers.abstract: The minimum numbers of points in rational equal-weight spherical designs on the circle are $2304$, $4608$, $9216$, and $9216$ at strengths $4$, $5$, $6$, and $7$, respectively. We construct two nonisometric optimal designs at each strength. At arbitrary strength $t$, we obtain an explicit cardinality divisor $D_t$ with $\log D_t=(1/2+o(1))t\log t$. Applied to the antipodal pairs of a $4608$-point design, Gromov's torus construction gives a flat minimal immersion of $\mathbb{T}^2$ into $S^{4607}$ with $2304$ distinct integral frequencies, attaining Petrunin's sharp Euclidean normal-curvature bound.

papers.title: Nonlocal bilinear differential operators induced by a third order hypermetric in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.authors: Hugo Aimar, An\'ibal Chicco Ruiz, Ivana G\'omez, Joaqu\'in Toledo
papers.abstract: The third order hypermetric $\rho(x,y,z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is given by the Euclidean distance of the point $(x,y,z)\in(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$ to the diagonal $\Delta^{(3)}=\{(x,x,x):x\in\mathbb{R}^n\}$ of $(\mathbb{R}^n)^3$. In this paper, we consider local and nonlocal fractional versions of bilinear differential operators generated by the geometry induced by $\rho(x,y,z)=\rho(0,x-y,x-z)$ instead of the usual $|(x-y,x-z)|$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$. In doing so, we obtain a fractional nonlocal version $\mathbb{D}^s(f,g)$, $0<s<1$, of the Dirichlet bilinear operator $\nabla f(x)\cdot\nabla g(x)$ which converges to this classical form when the fractional parameter approaches its endpoint $s=1$. We consider both the kernel approach and the Fourier multiplier version.

papers.title: Optimal orders for Hilbert-valued Littlewood--Paley functions of symmetric semigroups
papers.authors: Xudong Lai, Bo Li, Ji Li

papers.title: The $\nu$-core label order and noncrossing partitions
papers.abstract: We prove that the poset of $s$-noncrossing partitions is isomorphic to the core label order of the $\nu$-Tamari lattice introduced by Pr\'eville-Ratelle and Viennot.

papers.title: A quantitative two-interval criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: We aim to study whether the Weil form can detect a zero of the Riemann zeta function away from the critical line using two functions with increasingly narrow, widely separated supports. We prove that the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality on every such pair at all sufficiently large separations, provided the component widths decrease subexponentially. A zero to the right of the critical line forces the normalized cross term to exceed an exponential at arbitrarily large separations, with any exponent smaller than the horizontal displacement of that zero. In particular, reciprocal-width intervals suffice. Our proof combines a short-support positivity estimate, a smooth partition of fixed test functions and a pole obstruction for a one-sided Laplace transform. We also express the cross term through prime powers in a moving multiplicative interval. The resulting criterion specifies a uniform arithmetic inequality whose proof would establish the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives
papers.abstract: This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Analytical investigations, including equilibrium analysis and stability criteria, are conducted across varying fractional orders. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. The integration of fractional calculus with circuit analogies offers novel insights into tumor--immune dynamics and supports the design of memory-aware therapeutic interventions.

papers.title: A 43-vertex 4-chromatic unit-distance graph in the plane with girth 5
papers.abstract: We exhibit a set of 43 points in the Euclidean plane whose unit-distance graph has 83 edges, girth 5 and chromatic number 4. The smallest previously known 4-chromatic unit-distance graph of girth 5, due to Hochberg and O'Donnell (1996), has 45 vertices. The new graph is 4-critical, has trivial automorphism group, and has exactly 2n-3 edges; it is a Laman graph and its unit-distance realisation is infinitesimally rigid. The coordinates are algebraic numbers, specified as the unique real solution of an explicit system of 82 quadratic equations inside an explicit rational box. Every claim is certified by exact computation: existence and uniqueness of the realisation by a rational contraction-mapping certificate (independently re-checked with interval Krawczyk arithmetic), and non-3-colourability both by exhaustive search and by a DRAT proof verified with drat-trim.

papers.title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $\Gamma_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $\Gamma_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes \Gamma_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.

papers.title: Performance Analysis of Entanglement Swapping DV-QKD over MIMO FSO Channels
papers.authors: Sushil Kumar, Soumya P. Dash, George C. Alexandropoulos
papers.abstract: This paper studies multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) free-space optical (FSO) quantum communication systems employing polarization-encoded discrete-variable quantum key distribution (DV-QKD), based on entanglement swapping, with the goal of extending secure communications beyond the reach of a direct link. The FSO channels are subject to atmospheric absorption, diffraction, beam wander, pointing errors, and turbulence-induced fading, while background noise and detector imperfections degrade the performance. An eavesdropper controlling the channels and the relay is also considered. To analyze the performance of the considered system, both hops MIMO channels are decomposed into parallel spatial eigenchannels via singular value decomposition (SVD), photon loss is modeled using Kraus operators, and a threshold-detector model is developed for the relay. Based on these models, closed-form per-eigenchannel expressions for the relay gain are derived, which are then used to obtain expressions for the quantum bit error rate (QBER) and the secret key rate (SKR). Numerical results demonstrate that entanglement swapping maintains a low QBER over longer distances than direct transmission, extending the communication range beyond the noise-limited cutoff of the direct link, at the cost of a lower SKR at short distances. The crossover distance beyond which entanglement swapping prevails is determined mainly by the background noise and the detector technology, and it is demonstrated to increase with MIMO configurations. Moreover, the reach gain is shown to be maximized for a midpoint relay. Finally, since each swapping event requires a single-pair emission from both sources, a near-deterministic entangled-photon source is required, which spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources do not provide at practical key rates, whereas MIMO substantially relaxes this requirement.

papers.title: Rigid Lie Algebras from Semisimple Lie Algebras and Their Symplectic Modules
papers.abstract:
We consider two extensions associated with a nonzero finite-dimensional symplectic module $V$ over a complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{s}$, and study their rigidity. The toral extension adjoins a derivation acting as the identity on $V$ and trivially on $\mathfrak{s}$; the Heisenberg extension uses the invariant symplectic form on $V$ to define a central bracket.
  For the toral extension, we compute the first and second adjoint cohomology groups in terms of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak{s}}(V)$, and obtain rigidity precisely when $V$ is irreducible. These results hold for arbitrary nonzero finite-dimensional modules. For the Heisenberg extension, we express the second adjoint cohomology as the kernel of a map combining the symplectic centralizer with an equivariant Jacobi map. A Killing-form argument shows that every multiplicity-free sum of irreducible symplectic modules gives an algebraically rigid Heisenberg extension. We also treat constructions with independent toral generators or Heisenberg centers. Repeated summands lead to explicit nonrigid examples, including a deformation to $\mathfrak{sl}_3$. The proofs use invariant cochains and recover several previously studied families.

papers.title: Nonlinear stability and time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.authors: Renjun Duan, Feimin Huang, Rui Li, Lingda Xu
papers.abstract: We prove the global-in-time nonlinear stability and establish explicit algebraic time-decay rates of planar rarefaction waves for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system of an ideal polytropic gas in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Given a smooth initial rarefaction profile of small wave strength \(\delta>0\), we first construct the corresponding global one-dimensional Navier-Stokes-Fourier solution \(U_b(t,x_1)\) and show that it converges toward the self-similar Euler rarefaction fan in \(L^\infty(\mathbb{R})\) at rate \((1+t)^{-12/25}\). For the three-dimensional Cauchy problem under small weighted $H^3(\mathbb{R}^3)$ perturbations with zero integral of mass, momentum, and total energy, we prove that there exists a unique global strong solution $U(t,x)$ converging toward $U_b(t,x_1)$ in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$, with $\nabla(U-U_b)$ decaying in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ at rate $(1+t)^{-11/25}$.

papers.title: Embeddings for Orlicz potential spaces with applications to mixed local-nonlocal problems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide further insight into potential spaces within the nonstandard framework of Orlicz functions. More precisely, we establish continuous and compact embeddings of potential spaces in $\mathbb{R}^n$ into both unweighted and weighted Orlicz spaces. Special attention is devoted to the radial setting, for which compactness results are obtained through Strauss- and Ni-type inequalities. As an application, we prove the existence of positive radial solutions to a class of Henon-type problems involving both local and nonlocal contributions in the Orlicz framework.

papers.title: A Bayesian oriented exploration and reinforcement learning in continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization
papers.authors: Kexin Chen, Xiang Yu, Shanshan Zhao
papers.abstract: We propose a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization with unknown market parameters. To better reflect the impact of improved information of the unknown drift on the degree of exploration, we consider a novel randomization based on continuous-time stochastic filtering. Specifically, we construct a continuous-time analog to Thompson Sampling by treating the unknown drift as a random draw from a generalized sampling distribution parameterized by the filter's posterior mean and variance. The new learning objective measures the tradeoff between the wealth performance and the weighted KL divergence between the policy and the true Bayesian posterior, which transforms the classical feedback control into an information guided stochastic policy. As a result, the degree of exploration endogenously depends on the Reward-Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation that decays with the shrinking filter's variance. This allows us to devise an efficient model-based learning algorithm in the mean-variance portfolio optimization with theoretical guarantee and superior learning performance.

papers.title: Directional weak mixing and directional Kronecker for $\Z^2$-actions
papers.authors: E. Arthur Robinson, Jr., Ay\c{s}e A. \c{S}ahin
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a measure preserving $\Z^2$-action on a Lebesgue probability space $(X,\mu)$ and let $L\subseteq\R^2$ be a $1$-dimensional subspace. For a rational subspace $L$, direction $L$ weak mixing corresponds to weak mixing for the measure preserving transformation $T^{\vv_0}$, where $\vv_0$ is a primitive vector in $\Z^2$ generating $L$. For an irrational direction $L$, we study two different definitions of direction $L$ weak mixing, and show that they are the same: ``Dynamical'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined to be the absence of any direction $L$ Kronecker factors. These factors are defined in terms of almost periodicity along a finite width direction $L$ strip in $\Z^2$. ``Spectral'' direction $L$ weak mixing is defined as the absence of any direction $L^\perp$ line segments $I\subseteq\T^2$ with positive spectral measure. We also give a spectral characterization of the directional Kronecker property defined in \cite{liuxu}, and provide examples of $\Z^2$-actions $K$ that are direction $L$ Kronecker.

papers.title: Integral Compensation for Discrete-time Bearing-only Target Localization and Circumnavigation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the discrete-time control problem of driving an agent to localize and circumnavigate an unknown target at a prescribed radius using bearing measurements. Discretizing existing continuous-time circumnavigation controllers can introduce steady-state orbit bias, even at sampling rates that preserve stability. To eliminate the sampling-induced orbit bias, we propose an adaptive compensator for a circumnavigation controller formulated directly in discrete time. Driven by the estimated agent-to-target distance, the proposed compensator dynamically learns the geometric correction required to achieve the desired circumnavigation radius. Unlike existing static correction methods, neither the proposed controller nor the compensator update explicitly uses the sampling interval. Exponential convergence is rigorously established using Lyapunov-based analysis. Simulation results illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms.

papers.title: Local turnpike property for a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model
papers.abstract: We study a three-component mean field game system arising from a resource harvesting model. It couples Hamilton--Jacobi and Fokker--Planck equations for the harvesters with a reaction-diffusion equation for the resource. The coupling is nonlocal in space and time. For standard second-order mean field game systems, exponential turnpike estimates are known under assumptions such as monotonicity of the coupling. For the present system, Kobeissi, Mazari-Fouquer, and Ruiz-Balet proved algebraic convergence to a stationary solution in a space--time averaged sense, but no exponential turnpike estimate has been obtained. We prove such an estimate near a stationary solution with strictly positive density components. Inspired by the relative entropy method, we add the relative entropy of the resource density to the standard energy for local turnpike estimates. In the time derivative of this modified energy, the nonlocal coupling terms cancel. The two key assumptions are coercivity of a quadratic form determined by the stationary resource density and smallness of the relative density perturbations in $L^\infty$. Under these assumptions, we bound the absolute value of the modified energy by two terms that decay exponentially away from the initial and terminal times. We derive weighted $L^2$ exponential turnpike estimates for the harvester density, the resource density, and the gradient of the value function. We give sufficient conditions for coercivity. For each fixed $T>0$, classical solutions satisfying these assumptions exist for initial and terminal data sufficiently close to the stationary solution. We extend the modified energy estimate to a more general reaction term under the corresponding assumptions.

papers.title: New Classes of CCZ-Inequivalent APN Functions with Boomerang Uniformity One in Odd Characteristic: Differential and Boomerang Spectra
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^n>3$ be an odd prime power and let $g:\F_q\to\F_q$ be an even perfect nonlinear (PN) function with $g(0)=0$. We construct almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions $G_{\lambda,M}(x)=g(x)+M(x)+\lambda(x^{q-1}-1)$, where $\lambda\in\F_q^*$, $-\lambda\notin g(\F_q)$, and $M$ is an $\F_p$-linearized permutation polynomial. These one-point modifications of $g+M$ have boomerang uniformity one, the smallest possible value for APN functions in odd characteristic. We give complete differential and boomerang spectrum formulas and obtain closed-form evaluations for selected constructions based on Coulter--Matthews monomials and Dembowski--Ostrom polynomials. For $q>7$, comparison of differential spectra establishes CCZ-inequivalence to all APN monomial families listed in the paper and every APN binomial in the original Ness--Helleseth family or its extension by Zeng et al. We characterize CCZ-equivalence within our construction, showing that any two linearly inequivalent even PN functions over the same field yield CCZ-inequivalent APN functions. We obtain three pairwise CCZ-inequivalent APN functions with boomerang uniformity one over $\F_{p^{15\ell}}$ for every $\ell\ge1$, six over $\F_{p^{120r}}$ for every $r\ge1$, and unbounded numbers of such classes in characteristic three. We further prove that CCZ-equivalence and EA-equivalence coincide for functions at Hamming distance at most $m$ from a PN function, provided that $m(m+1)<q-q/p$.
