As an application of our results, we obtain an effective refinement of a theorem of Corvaja and Zannier: Let $(F_n)_n$ and $(G_n)_n$ be two linear recurrence sequences and $\mathcal{N}$ be the set of positive integers $n$ such that $F_n/G_n$ is an integer. Hadamard quotient theorem, conjectured by Pisot and proven by Van der Poorten states that if the set $\mathcal{N}$ coincides with $\mathbb{N}$ then $\left(F_n/G_n\right)_n$ is itself linear recurrence sequence. Corvaja-Zannier proved that if $\mathcal{N}$ is infinite set, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $P(X)$ such that $\left( P(n)F_n/G_n\right)_n$ agrees with a linear recurrence sequence for all $n$ in a suitable arithmetic progression. We give an explicit bound $C$, depending explicitly on the parameters of the recurrence sequences such that, the conclusion holds if $\mathcal{N}$ contains at least $C$ elements.

papers.title: Extremal graphs for Alon's graph coupon-collector conjecture
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices. Starting with every vertex uncovered, at each step sample a vertex uniformly and independently and cover one of its uncovered neighbors, chosen uniformly, if any. Let \(\cc(G)\) denote the expected number of steps required to cover all vertices. Alon conjectured that disjoint unions of \(K_{d+1}\) maximize \(\cc(G)\) among \(d\)-regular graphs of a prescribed order whenever such unions exist. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture for every fixed \(d\ge2\) and give a complete characterization of the extremal graphs for \(d=2\) at every order \(n\ge3\). In particular, all but at most six vertices of any such extremal graph lie in four-cycle components.

papers.title: Financial Connectedness: Heavy Tails andResponse Attribution
papers.authors: Zhu Yuzhao, Shao Jiahui, Liu Dongqi, Li Dan, Hu Xiaoxiao
papers.abstract: A financial market can appear mainly dependent on its own shocks under a variance account and mainly dependent on external shocks under a cumulative-response account. We establish how these opposite diagnoses arise from the same propagation system. For a given cumulative magnitude, squaring gives greater weight to responses concentrated across sources and time. Source priorities can therefore reverse even in stable Gaussian systems with known parameters. Heavy tails raise a separate question: whether the reported shares have a fixed population basis. One innovation with an infinite second moment removes the full network's finite covariance input. We characterize when normalized shares nevertheless stabilize and construct rank-amplitude connectedness, a cumulative-deviation target without finite first or second moments. It can be consistently estimated under local dependence and identification conditions. With fitted dynamics and rank scatter fixed, changing attribution replaces 3.14 names in the daily Top 10 of forty stocks, selecting recipients with greater external persistence relative to their own adjustment. In five futures contracts, mean external share rises from 28.0% to 55.9%, and 70.9% of recipient-dates switch from own to external dominance.

papers.title: Zero forcing is not unimodal
papers.abstract: The zero forcing polynomial of a graph counts the number of distinct zero forcing sets of every possible size. In 2018, Boyer et al. asked whether the zero forcing polynomial is always unimodal, and provided some evidence that it is. We answer this question by constructing an infinite family of graphs whose zero forcing polynomials are not unimodal. Our construction also shows that the graph polynomials associated with connected forcing and total forcing are also not unimodal in general.

papers.title: An Adaptive Short-Step Variant of BroxGD with Linear Convergence under Quadratic Growth
papers.abstract: Broximal Gradient Descent (BroxGD), recently analyzed by Richt\'arik et al. (arXiv:2605.08850v1), is a projection-free sister method to Projected Gradient Descent (ProjGD) for solving $\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)$, where $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ and $\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ is nonempty, closed and convex. The method performs local linear minimization over the feasible set intersected with a Euclidean ball and carefully prescribed radius. Like ProjGD, BroxGD enjoys linear convergence in the smooth strongly convex setting, with the same condition-number dependence. However, the known radius rule leading to linear convergence requires unavailable information and is therefore impractical. We develop an adaptive short-step variant of BroxGD which converges linearly for smooth convex functions under quadratic growth (generalizing strong convexity), without requiring unavailable information. We use $$z_k\in\arg\min_{z\in\mathcal X\cap\mathbb B(x_k,t_k)}\langle\nabla f(x_k),z\rangle,\quad x_{k+1}=\mathrm{Proj}_{S_k}(x_k-\nabla f(x_k)/L),$$ where $L$ is the smoothness constant of $f$, $\mathbb B(x,t)$ is the Euclidean ball centered at $x$ of radius $t$, and $S_k$ is the line segment connecting $x_k$ and $z_k$. The radius is updated by $t_{k+1}=\max\{\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|,t_k/2\}$. Projection onto $S_k$ requires only scalar clipping. Assuming an exact local linear minimization oracle, each update uses one oracle call. For any positive initial radius, we bound all oracle calls to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ and obtain $O((L/\alpha)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ for fixed initialization, where $\alpha=\min\{\alpha_0,L\}$ and $\alpha_0>0$ is the quadratic-growth constant.

papers.title: A divisorial domain with non-Pr\"ufer normalization
papers.abstract: We answer a 1968 question of Heinzer by constructing a two-dimensional local divisorial domain whose normalization is not Pr\"ufer.

papers.title: Persistence landscape velocity: Closed formulas and a topological probe of quantum criticality
papers.abstract:
We introduce the landscape velocity $\xi$, a scalar measure of variation of a parameter-dependent persistence landscape. For families of finite barcodes whose bars are all born at the fixed filtration value $0$, we show that $\xi$ is the $L^2$ speed of the landscape curve where the sorted death times are differentiable and derive an exact closed formula that requires no persistence landscape at all: the death times of the barcodes, as functions of the parameter, suffice. For the velocity of the empirical mean of several landscapes we also prove a closed formula which, again, strikingly requires neither the empirical mean landscape nor any of the individual landscapes, only the individual barcodes.
  As an application, we revisit Olsthoorn's persistent homology analysis of the transverse-field Ising chain. Whereas his approach uses different homology degrees and summaries depending on the boundary conditions, ours uses $H_0$ only and a single rule: the position of the maximum of $\xi$. This rule locates the quantum critical point for both periodic and open boundary conditions, and for both mutual-information and correlator-based dissimilarities. The position of the maximum converges to the critical point faster than all the estimators we can extract from Olsthoorn's work. In the 4 scenarios considered (different boundary conditions and different dissimilarity matrices), the peak of the normalized velocity becomes increasingly pronounced with system size, with observed logarithmic growth. This logarithmic growth is proved for periodic boundaries with correlator dissimilarity under stated hypotheses, identifying landscape velocity as a singular topological response to quantum criticality.

papers.title: Uniqueness of Axisymmetric Vortices in the Magnetic Ginzburg-Landau Equations
papers.abstract: We study vortex solutions of the magnetic Ginzburg-Landau model (or the Abelian-Higgs model). We establish uniqueness of axisymmetric vortex solutions for every winding number $n\geq1$ and coupling constant $\lambda>0$. Our proof uses a lattice inequality and constrained minimization to construct a positive radial solution lying above any two given radial solutions. A comparison argument based on the virial identity then establishes uniqueness. We further prove that the unique radial solution depends real analytically on $\lambda$ and that both radial profiles are strictly increasing with respect to $\lambda$.

papers.title: Uncertainty principle on $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: This paper establishes an uncertainty principle on the mixed space $\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ for $n \ge 2$. Leveraging the paraboloid restriction theorem on $\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ derived from Barron's global-in-time Strichartz estimates for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation, we construct measurable sets $S \subset \mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ and $A(R,\delta) \subset \mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n$ that form a strong $L^2$ annihilating pair, satisfying the uniform inequality $\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)} \le 3(\|f\|_{L^2((\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus S)} + \|\widehat{f}\|_{L^2((\mathbb{Z}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)\setminus A(R,\delta))})$ for all $f \in L^2(\mathbb{T}^m \times \mathbb{R}^n)$, where the measures of $S$ and $A(R,\delta)$ can be made arbitrarily large while the constant 3 remains unchanged. As an application, we derive a two-time observability inequality for the semi-periodic Schrodinger equation under a support condition on the phase-modified solution at the first observation time.

papers.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
papers.abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.

papers.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $\Omega$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/\mu_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/\mu_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.

papers.title: Tiling of Hyperbolic Surface by Maximal Number of Tiles
papers.authors: Chunlin Li, Erxiao Wang, Jie Wu, Min Yan
papers.abstract: Tilings of a closed hyperbolic surface by congruent $n$-gons with $n\ge 7$ is a finite problem. One extreme of the finite problem is that the number of tiles is maximal. The problem is related to edge-to-edge tilings of the Poincar\'e disk ${\bb H}^2$ by congruent $n$-gons, such that all vertices have degree 3 and the vertex sets satisfy certain balance condition. For the special case $n=7$, we show that the heptagon in any such tiling belongs to one of the four families, and tilings of ${\bb H}^2$ by generic heptagons in each family is unique. As a consequence, for any closed hyperbolic surface of Euler characteristic $\chi$, we may classify all tilings of the surface by maximal number $-6\chi$ of congruent generic heptagons in the four families.

papers.title: Nonlinear Stability of Planar Shock Waves for the Navier-Stokes-Fourier Equations in R^3
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the global nonlinear stability and large-time decay rates of small-amplitude planar viscous shock waves for the three-dimensional (3-D) full compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier equations in the whole space $\R^3$. {We prove that if the initial perturbation is sufficiently small in $H^3(\R^3)\cap\Hm(\R^3)$, then the Cauchy problem admits a unique global strong solution that converges to the planar shock profile without any phase shift. In the moving shock frame, both the conservative and primitive perturbations decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/4}$ in $H^3(\R^3)$. Their time and transverse spatial derivatives decay at the rate $(1+t)^{-1/2}$, measured in $\Hm(\R^3)$ for the conservative perturbation and in $H^1(\R^3)$ for the primitive perturbation.} No zero-mass condition or spectral stability assumption is imposed. On the whole space $\R^3$, the main analytical difficulties stem from the continuous transverse low frequencies, the opposite signs of shock compression in $L^2(\R^3)$ and unweighted $\Hm(\R^3)$, and the absence of density dissipation in the continuity equation coupled with temperature variations. To overcome these difficulties, we introduce a density-weighted $\Hm(\R^3)$ multiplier built from the inverse entropy Hessian and a modified curl operator. Through entropy symmetrization and the curl projection, all second-order acoustic derivatives of the potential cancel out and the transverse acoustic modes are controlled, so that the normal Euler drift is governed by the compressive derivative of the characteristic speed. Combined with an effective momentum variable and a momentum--density cross estimate, this negative-order energy absorbs the unfavorable compression term in the $L^2$ energy and closes the $H^3(\R^3)$ a priori estimates without loss of derivatives.

papers.title: Hausdorff Dimension of Escaping Sets of Transcendental Entire Functions in the Speiser Class
papers.abstract: For every $d\in[1,2]$, we construct a transcendental entire function $f$ whose finite singular value is contained in $\{-1,0,1\}$ and whose escaping set has Hausdorff dimension $d$. For $d<2$, the construction combines spiral corridors with quasiconformal folding. A narrowing Archimedean spiral gives dimension one, while a logarithmic spiral with adjustable width gives intermediate dimensions. The endpoint $d=2$ is realized by the exponential map. This gives an affirmative answer to a question of Bishop posed in 2018.

papers.title: Uniform inference for $U$-statistics of exchangeable arrays under degeneracy
papers.abstract: Many $U$-statistics of row-column exchangeable arrays become degenerate at natural null hypotheses: their convergence rates change and their limiting laws may or may not remain Gaussian. We establish conditions under which inference based on the classical unbiased variance estimator is uniformly valid across these changes, without knowledge of the degeneracy order. It is known that $U$-statistics can be decomposed into orthogonal projections indexed by bipartite graphs. Under uniform fourth-moment assumptions, we establish that the standardized statistic is asymptotically Gaussian and the classical unbiased variance estimator is ratio-consistent, as long as a certain measure of concentration for projections indexed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. Under compactness of the normalized projections, both properties hold if and only if the proportion of variance contributed by disconnected graphs tends to zero. The necessity of this condition follows from a general limit theorem for these $U$-statistics, in which each graph contributes to a Wiener chaos of order equal to its number of connected components. We note that the row-column jackknife variance estimator, although nonnegative, does not generally give a studentized statistic with a standard normal limit in degenerate regimes. We illustrate our theory with an application to estimation and testing based on a distance from product form, exhibiting Gaussian and non-Gaussian limits at various rates depending on the model. We also propose a conservative inference procedure that does not require a Gaussian limit, valid under additional moment and projection conditions.

papers.title: Smooth approximations to character sums and zeta sums
papers.authors: Zikang Dong, Shengbo Zhao, Guang-Liang Zhou
papers.abstract: We study smooth approximations to Dirichlet character sums and zeta sums. The uniform upper-bound consequence of the Granville--Soundararajan conjecture, when imposed on all nonprincipal characters including imprimitive ones, implies the Riemann hypothesis for every primitive nonprincipal Dirichlet \(L\)-function. The proof uses characters induced to moduli divisible by all small primes. In the other direction, assuming the Riemann hypothesis for \(L(s,\chi)\), we establish the conjectured approximation uniformly for \(q^a\le x\le q\), where \(0<a\le1\) is fixed, with \(y=(\log q+(\log x)^2)(\log\log q)^C\) for every fixed \(C>6\). In this range both the character sum and its smooth restriction, and hence their difference, are exponentially small relative to the number of \(y\)-smooth integers coprime to \(q\). We establish the corresponding approximation for \(\sum_{n\le x}n^{-it}\) under the Riemann hypothesis for the zeta function, uniformly for \(T^a\le x\le T\) and \(2T\le t\le5T\). We also show that the full zeta-sum smooth-approximation conjecture implies the Lindel\"of hypothesis.

papers.title: Quantitative Homogenization and Global Lipschitz Estimates for Elasticity with Periodic Rigid Inclusions
papers.abstract: We consider the pure traction problem for linear elasticity in a bounded domain containing an $\varepsilon$-periodic array of perfectly rigid inclusions. For compatible $L^2$ boundary tractions on a Lipschitz domain, we prove an $O(\varepsilon^{1/2})$ error estimate in $H^1$ for a smoothed first-order two-scale expansion. If the exterior and inclusion boundaries are $C^{2,\beta}$, we also obtain a global Lipschitz estimate, uniform in $\varepsilon$, for compatible $C^{0,\sigma}$ tractions, where $0<\sigma<\beta$. The displacement is normalized modulo rigid motions, and the estimate controls the full gradient in the matrix and the inclusions. The boundary argument uses a local Neumann comparison estimate whose constant is independent of the choice of inclusions retained in cells cut by an artificial localization boundary. We prove this estimate by combining cellwise rigidification, divergence-free stress extensions, and duality, and then apply a boundary Campanato iteration and local estimates at the microscopic scale.

papers.title: Inverse problem in difference Galois theory
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $K=C(x)$ with $\sigma(x)=x+1$. We show that every closed subgroup $G\subseteq\GL_n(C)$ with cyclic component group $G/G^\circ$ can be realized as the \PV{} group of a system $\sigma Y=A(x)Y$. Here $G^\circ$ denotes the identity component of $G$. Moreover, we can choose the coefficient matrix to have the formal expansion $A(x)=h+O(x^{-2})$ at infinity, where $h\in G(C)$ is semisimple. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture of van der Put and Singer in their monograph \emph{Galois Theory of Difference Equations} (Lecture Notes in Mathematics, vol.~1666). The original results in this paper were entirely generated by ChatGPT 6 and the MechMath Agent Team (MMAT) developed by the Key Laboratory of Mathematics Mechanization, AMSS, CAS. The author reviewed and simplified the initial proofs and verified the correctness of the results.

papers.title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
papers.abstract: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_\epsilon$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $\epsilon$. As $\epsilon \to 0$, $T_\epsilon = \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/\epsilon)+O(1)$. As $\epsilon \to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.

papers.title: The bilinear Hilbert transforms are not of restricted weak type $(1,1,1/2)$
papers.abstract:
For every real $\alpha\neq0,1$, we show that the bilinear Hilbert transform \[
  H_\alpha(f_1,f_2)(x)
  =\text{p.v.}\int_{\mathbb{R}} f_1(x-\alpha y)\,f_2(x-y)\,\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{y} \] fails to map $L^1(\mathbb{R})\times L^1(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^{1/2,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ when restricted to characteristic functions of sets of positive finite measure. The counterexample is quantitative and can be realized by sets that are finite unions of intervals of a common arbitrarily small length.

papers.title: A note on two functional inequalities
papers.abstract: Motivated by some recent works on the following composite functional equation: $$f(x^2+yf(z)) = xf(x)+zf(y), \quad x, y, z \in \R,$$ we solve two related functional inequalities. In each case the solutions are only the constant zero function and the identity on $\R$.

papers.title: Revisiting the conjectures of Shapiro and Schanuel
papers.abstract:
We tackle Shapiro's conjecture for exponential polynomials where the coefficients are polynomials, and show that it follows from Schanuel's conjecture.
  More concretely, given exponential polynomials $f$ and $g$ with infinitely many common zeros, we show that Schanuel's conjecture implies that there is an exponential polynomial $h$ vanishing precisely at all the common zeros of $f$ and $g$.

papers.title: Snowflake $q$-Flipping
papers.abstract: We prove a weighted extension of Byun's snowflake-flipping theorem for cored hexagons with unit triangular holes along three crossing lines. The ratio of the tiling generating functions of two regions related by a snowflake flip is given by an explicit product. The result recovers Byun's theorem when all lozenge weights are 1 and resolves an open problem posed by the author in 2024. Our proof uses shuffling identities for semihexagons with dents on two sides.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: Rate of convergence for the Wiener--It\^o chaos in $W_p$ for $1\leq p<\infty$
papers.abstract: Inspired by previous work of Nualart, Ledoux, Peccati, Nourdin, and others, we establish quantitative fourth moment theorems for random variables in a fixed Wiener--It\^o chaos and for sums of two Wiener--It\^o chaoses in the $W_p$-Wasserstein distance for $1\leq p<\infty$.

papers.title: Elliptic $L^p$ Carleman estimates near the boundary, quantitative unique continuation, and applications to controllability and stabilization
papers.abstract: This article deals with quantitative unique continuation results up to and from the boundary for second-order elliptic equations with variable coefficients via $L^p$ Carleman estimates. The coefficients in the leading part are assumed to be Lipschitz continuous, and the potentials in the lower order term are allowed to belong to almost scale-invariant $L^q$ spaces. As applications, following the method of Lebeau and Robbiano, we obtain a spectral estimate which yields the interior null controllability of the associated parabolic equation, with an explicit dependence of the control cost on the potential. We also prove the logarithmic decay of the energy for damped wave equations with unbounded dampings and potentials.

papers.title: Joint Design of Communication and Control in Center-Fed Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.authors: Xu Gan, Yuanwei Liu, Hyundong Shin
papers.abstract: An analytical and optimization framework for the joint design of communication and control (JDCC) in a center-fed pinching-antenna system (C-PASS) is proposed. Within this framework, the mathematical coupling between data throughput and closed-loop control cost is characterized for JDCC. The analysis captures the mutual interference between concurrently transmitted data and control streams during uplink state uploading and downlink command delivery. Based on this coupling, an achievable communication-control performance region is established for C-PASS. Accordingly, a throughput maximization problem is formulated to jointly optimize digital and pinching beamforming subject to control-cost constraints. To address this problem, an alternating optimization algorithm is developed based on constraint reformulation and resource decomposition. The proposed framework reveals how control requirements shape achievable data throughput, guiding the joint beamforming design. Numerical results demonstrate that 1) the proposed C-PASS design achieves 110.2\% higher frame-average throughput than conventional PASS, and 2) the proposed concurrent data-control transmission protocol increases frame-average throughput by up to 66.7\% over separated transmission.

papers.title: 2-Selmer in arithmetic progressions
papers.abstract: We prove uniform asymptotics for the 2-Selmer cardinality in the congruent number family $y^2=x^3-D^2x$ with twisting parameter $D$ restricted to long arithmetic progressions.

papers.title: The strong cylinder conjecture and R\'edei's factorization conjecture in three dimensions
papers.authors: Haihua Deng, Weicong Li, Weiye Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the strong cylinder conjecture, that is, for every prime $p$, a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathbb F_p^3$ that meets every affine plane in a multiple of $p$ points is a union of $p$ distinct parallel affine lines. We use this result to resolve R\'edei's 1970 factorization conjecture in three dimensions: if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ contain zero and every vector in $\mathbb F_p^3$ has a unique expression $a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$, then one of the two sets is contained in a plane through zero.

papers.title: Fourth-Moment Theorems for Sums of Multiple Wigner Integrals
papers.abstract: We derive quantitative free fourth-moment bounds for sums of two Wigner chaoses of opposite parity under mirror symmetry. The bound contains an explicit remainder consisting of internal contractions of the two kernels. In particular, vanishing of this remainder together with the fourth free cumulant implies convergence to the standard semicircular law. If the higher-order kernel is cyclically symmetric, the internal contractions can be moved to an endpoint and we obtain an explicit fourth-root bound without a remainder. For fully symmetric kernels we obtain a square-root bound under the $W_2$-Wasserstein distance. Using the operator-norm support estimate for Wigner integrals, we also extend these bounds to every $W_p$-Wasserstein distance , where $1\le p<\infty$.

papers.title: Differences Between Quantum Symmetries of Graphs and Graph $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We establish several characteristic differences between the quantum symmetry groups of directed graphs and their associated graph $C^*$-algebras in the frameworks of Banica and Joardar-Mandal, respectively, considering the family of finite directed graphs without isolated vertices and without multiple edges.

papers.title: Monotonicity of Erd\H{o}s sums
papers.abstract: For $k \geq 1$ let $f_k = \sum_{\Omega(n)=k} 1/(n\log n)$, where $\Omega$ counts prime factors with multiplicity, and let $g_k$ be the same sum restricted to odd $n$. Lichtman showed that $f_k \to 1$, with a global minimum at $k=6$, and Gorodetsky, Lichtman and Wong that $f_k = 1 - 2^{-k}(a_1 k^2 + O(k \log(k+1)))$. We prove that $f_k < f_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 6$, and that $g_k > g_{k+1}$ for every $k \geq 1$. The two statements come from one analytic distinction. Writing $\sum_k P_k(s) z^k = \zeta(s)^z H(s,z)$, at $s=1$ the point $z=2$ lies on the first singular circle of $H$, and strictly inside the first singular circle of the product with the prime $2$ removed. We show that this distinction decides the direction in general. If the complement of a set of primes $\mathcal{P}$ is thin and its least element is at least $3$, the corresponding sums eventually decrease, so the second theorem is one case of a general phenomenon. The inequalities used at the last step of the first theorem are certified by interval arithmetic.

papers.title: Solution Size Growth as an Obstacle to Iterative Refinement for Linear Optimization
papers.abstract: Iterative refinement is a technique used to exponentially boost the precision of the solution to certain problems by solving a sequence of related problem instances. We study the size of the solutions arising from the sequence of problems produced by the iterative refinement algorithm when applied to linear optimization problems (LPs). We introduce a class of problems for which the size of such solutions can grow exponentially with the number of refinement iterations, and we show evidence that to avoid this undesirable behavior, a black-box LP solver would have to be \emph{lucky}---a concept introduced formally in this paper, by which we mean that the solver would have to return a solution of better quality than what is required by its termination tolerances. Furthermore, we show that the exponential scaling occurs if one uses a natural instantiation of the simplex algorithm using Bland's pivoting rule. We discuss the implications of our lower bound on the solution size for optimization algorithms whose running time depends polynomially on the solution size, such as quantum multiplicative weights update algorithms and quantum matrix games algorithms.

papers.title: Sharp coercivity estimates and stability loss for the Ginzburg-Landau energy
papers.abstract: In this paper we investigate how the coercivity of the Hessian of the Ginzburg-Landau energy at local minimizers $u$ depends on the Ginzburg-Landau parameter $\kappa$ in the regime of large $\kappa$. This question is motivated by its crucial role in the numerical approximation of energy minimizers. Accounting for the degeneracy that is induced by phase invariance and possible additional neutral directions, we establish a universal lower bound of order $\kappa^2$ for the inverse coercivity constant $\rho_u(\kappa)$ of local minimizers with uniformly bounded Hessian kernel dimension. For nonvanishing states that satisfy a quantitative subcriticality condition, we prove a matching upper bound, showing that the quadratic scaling is sharp. On a fixed annulus with a fixed smooth magnetic potential, we then construct nonvanishing local minimizers for which $\rho_u(\kappa)\simeq\kappa^4$. Moreover, we exhibit branches of strictly stable local minimizers along which the inverse coercivity constant diverges as stability is lost. Consequently, no locally bounded upper estimate depending only on $\kappa$ can hold uniformly over all phase-nondegenerate local minimizers, even for a fixed domain and magnetic potential.

papers.title: Singular parabolic Anderson models - From flat space to geometric contexts
papers.abstract: These notes (which grew out of some lecture notes prepared for the first Aarhus Summer School in Analysis and Probability) are an introduction to the parabolic Anderson model (PAM), or otherwise stated the stochastic heat equation $\partial_{t} u \,=\, \tfrac{1}{2}\Delta\, u \,+\, \beta\, u\,\dot{W}$. In this system, a multiplicative random potential $\dot{W}$ drives the solution away from the smooth spreading of the classical heat flow and toward intermittency. Namely one observes that mass concentrates, as time grows, on a few tall and widely separated peaks. Through the Feynman-Kac representation this analytic phenomenon has an equivalent probabilistic reading as the localization of a directed polymer in a random environment. We first develop this picture on the flat space $\mathbb{R}^{d}$, covering the construction of the driving noise, well-posedness of the equation, and two-sided bounds on the moment Lyapunov exponents that quantify intermittency. We then turn to the more original goal of the monograph: understanding how these phenomena, and the exponents attached to them, change when $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ is replaced by a genuinely geometric background, such as a sub-Riemannian manifold or a fractal set. Throughout, the emphasis is on concepts, main results, and the intuition behind their proofs, rather than on exhaustive technical detail.

papers.title: Ranks of fibers in random elliptic surfaces
papers.abstract: For random integer polynomials $P$ of arbitrary degree we prove that for $100\%$ of elliptic surfaces $y^2=x^3-P(t)^2x$ the average 2-Selmer rank of the fibers is 3. Consequently, for $100\%$ these random elliptic surfaces we establish a lower bound for the proportion of fibers attaining algebraic rank $0$ and $1$.

papers.title: Dlab--Ringel standardization in algebraic triangulated categories
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of derived standardly stratified algebras as a connective dg analogue of standardly stratified algebras. To this end, we extend the Dlab--Ringel standardization method to algebraic triangulated categories and show that every basic proper derived standardly stratified algebra arises from this extended method. We establish Ringel duality for derived standardly stratified algebras using silting objects. More precisely, the Ringel dual is again derived standardly stratified, and the corresponding perfect derived categories are related by mutually quasi-inverse contravariant triangle equivalences. We also show that, over an algebraically closed field, a proper derived standardly stratified algebra is smooth if and only if its derived standard modules are exceptional. Finally, we prove that dg algebras given by finite acyclic graded quivers with arrows of non-positive degrees and homogeneous relations are derived standardly stratified with respect to every total order on the vertices.

papers.title: Equivalence of finite and infinite survival and sharpness of the phase transition for additive particle systems
papers.abstract: Krone's two-stage contact process is an interacting particle system in which each site on a grid can be in one of three possible states: 0 (empty), 1 (young individual), and 2 (adult individual). Only adults can multiply, and their offspring is initially young, before growing up after an exponential time. There are two death rates, one for adult trees, and a higher one for young trees. The process is additive and has an additive dual, but unlike the contact process it is not self-dual. Answering a question of Krone, for the process on the $d$-dimensional integer grid, Foxall proved that survival of finite populations is equivalent to nontriviality of the upper invariant law. Using a completely different method, we generalise this result to processes on countable groups and along the way also establish sharpness of the phase transition for a general class of additive interacting particle systems.

papers.title: A Geometry-Robust Ne\v{c}as-Type Inequality for Stokes Preconditioning
papers.authors: Qi Xin, Xie Yan, Shihua Gong
papers.abstract: Pressure mass preconditioners for the incompressible Stokes equations can deteriorate on domains with narrow gaps. We develop a pressure preconditioner that uses the distance to the boundary to account for spatially varying geometric scales. Its application consists of a pressure mass solve and a weighted pressure Poisson solve, with the squared boundary distance as the diffusion coefficient. The theoretical basis is a distance-weighted pressure norm defined by splitting the pressure into an $L^2$ component and a component controlled by its weighted gradient. We prove that this norm is bounded by the negative norm of the pressure gradient on every bounded connected open set, with a constant depending only on the dimension. A reverse bound follows from the boundary Hardy inequality, giving norm equivalence uniformly over families with bounded Hardy constants. Two-dimensional finite element experiments on slender, perforated, and composite domains demonstrate stable performance across the tested geometric parameters and mesh refinements. The smallest eigenvalues of the preconditioned pressure Schur complement remain close to $0.54$, and block preconditioning with algebraic multigrid auxiliary solves requires about 20--30 FGMRES iterations across the geometric sweeps.

papers.title: Finite models for the order axioms of the Hilbert Plane: Redundancies and Finite Independence Models
papers.abstract: Results on the redundancy and on the independence of the order axioms of the Hilbert plane are scattered in the literature, from Veblen's 1904 remark that the independence of the axioms of order can be shown by finite models to the redundancies removed from Hilbert's axioms of order in later editions of the Grundlagen. The aim of this note is to collect them in an organic and self-contained form for the incidence and order axioms as presented by Greenberg. In doing so we single out three redundancies inside the order axioms: the symmetry of betweenness, the existence part of trichotomy, and the second clause of plane separation. Each of them dictates which part of the corresponding axiom an independence model must violate, and we give explicit finite models of three, three, nine and twenty-five points. A model of all the incidence and order axioms, on the contrary, is necessarily infinite, so the independence of any axiom added to them requires infinite models; for two of the order axioms the finite models also give independence from all the remaining axioms of the Hilbert plane.

papers.title: Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
papers.authors: H. Meng, A. Ballester Bolinches, P. Jimenez Seral
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Ced\'o and Okni\'nski \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.

papers.title: From Imperfect Information to Controlled Steps: Stochastic Optimization under Heavy-Tailed Noise and Compression
papers.abstract:
Stochastic optimization relies on information whose statistical quality, availability, and computational cost can vary substantially. Heavy-tailed observations challenge concentration, compression distorts communicated vectors, and generalized smoothness changes how far an algorithm can move. This dissertation studies these difficulties through two linked design decisions: how to construct an informative search vector and how to convert it into a controlled step.
  We first develop high-probability methods under bounded central $p$-th moments, $p\in(1,2]$, allowing infinite variance when $p<2$. Clipped gradient, accelerated, extragradient, and gradient descent-ascent methods come with guarantees for stochastic minimization and variational inequalities, with smoothness and moment conditions needed only where the iterates lie with high probability. For composite and distributed problems, shifted and innovation clipping preserve the fixed point that direct clipping can disturb, while retaining linear speedup.
  We then characterize the value of richer stochastic information: lower complexity bounds quantify when same-sample gradient differences and stochastic Hessian information improve heavy-tailed nonconvex optimization, and normalized momentum variance reduction and Hessian-corrected momentum attain matching or near-matching in-expectation bounds. Separately clipping gradients and their correction terms yields batch-free high-probability methods.
  For compressed distributed optimization, we prove convergence of normalized error-feedback methods under generalized smoothness without a uniform gradient-dissimilarity assumption, and develop parameter-agnostic variants with five momentum estimators. Finally, we extend the estimator hierarchy to linear minimization oracles over arbitrary norm balls, recovering the Euclidean rates under estimator-specific generalized smoothness.

papers.title: Sharp Rates for Optimal Recovery of Bandlimited Functions from Localized Oversampling
papers.abstract:
It is well-known that one can recover a function $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ ( $0<\delta<\pi$) from its finite sample data $f(j),-n\le j\le n$, with an approximation error exponentially decaying to zero as $n$ tends to infinity. Various regularized Shannon sampling formula have been proposed to achieve such exponential approximation. So far the best rate has been
  $$
  O\biggl(\frac1{\sqrt{n}}\exp(-(\pi-\delta)n)\biggr).
  $$
  We establish that the optimal recovery algorithm in the worst-case scenario achieves an approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}$ satisfying
  $$
  c_* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2}\le \rho_{n,\delta}\le C^* \frac1{\sqrt{n}}(\tan\frac\delta 4)^{2n+1/2},
  \quad 0<\delta\leq\pi,\quad n\geq1,
  $$
  where $c_*,C^*$ are positive constants independent of $n$ and $\delta$. This result identifies the best possible exponential rate to reconstruct bandlimited functions from two-sided finite oversampling data. In other words,
  $$
  \rho_{n,\delta} \asymp \frac{\tan\frac\delta 4}{\sqrt{n}}\exp\bigl(-c_\delta(\pi-\delta)n\bigr),
  $$
  where $c_\delta$ is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi]$ and
  $$
  \lim_{\delta\to\pi^-}c_\delta=1,\ \lim_{\delta\to 0^+}c_\delta=+\infty.
  $$
  We also make the new finding that one can also reconstruct $f$ bandlimited to $[-\delta,\delta]$ with exponentially decaying error from one-sided sample data $f(j)$, $1\le j\le n$, and the sharp rate of approximation error $\rho_{n,\delta}'$ of the optimal algorithm is
  $$
  \rho_{n,\delta}' \asymp \sqrt{\delta/\pi}\sin^n(\delta/2).
  $$

papers.title: On Poincar\'e spaces which are not manifolds
papers.abstract: This expository note gives a short derivation of the classical Spivak normal fibration formula for the total space of a spherical fibration over a Poincar\'e duality space. We review the associated smooth, PL, and topological manifold realization criteria and illustrate them with examples from the stable stems. The principal application combines these criteria with the completed solution of the Kervaire invariant problem to identify the exceptional stems in a specified family of three cell Poincar\'e spaces.

papers.title: A DG method for the pseudostress-velocity formulation of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem
papers.abstract: We introduce a discontinuous Galerkin method for the approximation of the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Stokes-Brinkman eigenvalue problem. The method is based on a mixed formulation in which the pseudostress tensor and the fluid velocity are the main unknowns, while the pressure can be recovered through a post-processing procedure applied to the pseudostress tensor. Using discontinuous polynomial spaces of degree $k\geq 1$, we propose a consistent symmetric interior penalty discretization for the approximation of the spectrum. Relying on the spectral theory for non-compact operators, we establish convergence of the discrete spectral approximation and derive error estimates for the method. A series of numerical experiments is presented to assess its computational performance. On the one hand, we investigate the convergence rates for different polynomial degrees, computational domains, and values of the permeability. Furthermore, we study the influence of the stabilization parameter on the discrete spectrum by comparing different choices of this parameter and examining their impact on the occurrence of spurious eigenvalues.

papers.title: Dimension reduction by bi-H\"older maps
papers.abstract: The H\"older dimension of a metric space is the infimum of its Hausdorff dimension over all bi-H\"older changes of the metric. Colvin asked whether it can take noninteger values. We show that every metric space of finite upper box dimension has integer H\"older dimension. For a bounded subset of a Euclidean space, the dimension reduction is carried out by a global homeomorphism of the ambient space, built from randomly translated singular functions, which brings the Hausdorff dimension of the set arbitrarily close to its integer part.

papers.title: The Lee-Yang property of the Blume-Emery-Griffiths model
papers.abstract: The Lieb-Sokal theorem provides a tool for establishing the Lee-Yang property of the partition function of a spin model if the corresponding single-spin partition function has this property and the interaction term in its Hamiltonian is of the form $-\sum J_{ij} S_iS_j$ with $J_{ij}\geq 0$. According to the result of this paper, the spin $S=1$ model with the Hamiltonian $-\sum (J_{ij} S_iS_j + K_{ij}S_i^2S_j^2) + \sum \Delta S_i^2$ has the Lee-Yang property for all $K_{ij}\in \mathds{R}$ and $\Delta >0$, whenever each $J_{ij}$ exceeds an explicitly computed bound $C(\beta, \Delta, K_{ij})>0$, such that $C(\beta, \Delta, K_{ij})\to + \infty$ as $\beta \to 0$. The latter suggests that the Lee-Yang property of this model may hold only for sufficiently low temperatures.

papers.title: Sitewise Generator Decomposition and Non-Equilibrium Steady States for Generalized Zero-Range Processes
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the generalized zero-range processes considered in [20, 11, 12] with boundary driving. In these processes mass is moved between neighboring sites with rates depending only on the departure site. For a wide class of such models, the equilibrium stationary states are known to be of product form. We show that for such models, the boundary-driven generator can be decomposed into a sum of generators acting on single sites when integrating against (possibly inhomogeneous) products of the equilibrium marginals. We exploit this structure to derive new results for the harmonic models introduced in [15]. In particular, we prove that the propagation of mixture measures in [19] is still valid on graphs with asymmetric edges. On the chain geometry with asymmetric edges, we identify a class of models for which the NESS is given precisely by the NESS of the symmetric harmonic model on the chain. In addition to these results for harmonic models, we also present a new class of asymmetric models on the chain for which the NESS can be found explicitly and exhibits shock behavior. The large deviations for the density profile corresponding to these NESS are stated and proved.

papers.title: A Legendre-Galerkin Method for Kinetic Models of Opinion Dynamics with Quasi-Invariant Consistency
papers.abstract: Kinetic models of opinion dynamics provide a mesoscopic framework for describing collective behavior arising from interactions among a large number of individuals. Highly accurate numerical approximation to such Boltzmann-type equations, however, remains challenging due to the nonlinear inelastic collision operators involving multiple integrals coupling opinion variables and random perturbations. To address the difficulties, we develop a Legendre-Galerkin spectral method for a general class of kinetic models with opinion-dependent interaction rules. Our method exploits an exact decoupling of the weak collision kernel to obtain a time-independent tensor representation of the Galerkin collision operator. A recursive construction reduces collision-tensor assembly to one-dimensional quadrature, allowing the coefficients to be precomputed for subsequent use. A rigorous $L^2$-error estimate, along with mass preservation, is established for the fully discrete scheme under suitable regularity and stability assumptions. In the quasi-invariant regime, we derive the limiting Fokker-Planck equation and establish consistency between the exact Legendre-Galerkin operators of the rescaled Boltzmann equation and its limit for each fixed polynomial degree. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results, illustrate quasi-invariant consistency, and capture the formation of opinion clusters under the bounded-confidence interactions.

papers.title: Compression of Sources with Memory and Private Random Access
papers.authors: Venkat Chandar, Aslan Tchamkerten, Shashank Vatedka
papers.abstract: Private local decoding imposes a stringent constraint on compression: the codeword bits used to recover a source symbol must reveal nothing about the remaining symbols beyond what the recovered symbol itself reveals. For memoryless sources, this constraint is known to be compatible with entropy-rate compression. We show that the same holds for any stationary ergodic source over a finite alphabet. Specifically, every rate above the entropy rate is achievable with exact privacy and error-free local decoding on a set of source sequences whose probability tends to one. In contrast, we exhibit non-ergodic sources for which private local decoding incurs a strictly positive rate penalty.

papers.title: Bounded Spaces without a Geodesic in the Gromov-Hausdorff Class
papers.abstract: We construct two countable complete bounded metric spaces at Gromov-Hausdorff distance $1/4$ with no midpoint and hence no shortest curve between them. The proof uses the local existence of optimal correspondences near a space with finitely many self-correspondences of distortion below a fixed positive threshold, each of which is the graph of a bijection.

papers.title: Stability and Optimal Decay of Viscous Contact Waves under Large Perturbations
papers.abstract: The stability of viscous contact waves is established for the one-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations under large integrable perturbations. A unique global positive solution is obtained, which converges uniformly to a fixed Eulerian contact profile at the optimal inverse square-root rate in time. The wave-strength threshold depends only on bounds for the initial density perturbation in the first-order Sobolev norm, the energy of the initial velocity perturbation, the thermal relative entropy and the total conserved excess, together with positive lower bounds for the initial density and temperature. It is independent of higher Sobolev norms and the common far-field velocity. No square-integrability condition is imposed on the initial anti-derivatives. Derivative and pressure decomposition estimates are also established for the evolving solution.

papers.title: Asymptotic Stability of Planar Viscous Contact Waves for the Three-Dimensional Full Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations in the Whole Space
papers.abstract: The asymptotic stability of planar viscous contact waves is established for the three-dimensional full compressible Navier--Stokes equations in the whole space. The exact evolving planar background is constructed in a companion one-dimensional paper and may arise from a large integrable perturbation. The three-dimensional remainder has small energy, prescribed second-derivative bounds for density and velocity, and a prescribed first-derivative bound for temperature. Its initial temperature lies in a fixed positive interval; its second derivatives need only be finite. A unique global positive strong solution and algebraic decay in the uniform norm are obtained. The wave-strength threshold depends on lower-order planar bounds, while the allowed remainder size may depend on the complete planar datum.

papers.title: SU(2) Yang-Mills: Spectral Bounds, Vacuum Concentration, and Criteria for the Continuum Limit
papers.abstract: A continuum mass-gap argument must preserve nonzero renormalized states and a positive spectral estimate while the spatial cutoff is removed and physical volume grows. We develop quantitative results that separate these requirements. Gauge reduction, reflection positivity and attributed strong-coupling estimates give physical-transfer bounds with nontrivial local sectors. At fixed spatial cutoff and positive coupling, we construct subsequential infinite-volume physical-time dynamics from local history correlations, with nonconstant gauge-invariant observables. For finite spatial boxes, explicit bounds apply to the entire physical vacuum complement; finite-matrix criteria include all omitted representations. Vacuum concentration gives extensive entropy bounds, quantitative fidelity obstructions for hard electric cutoffs, and necessary growth of retained representation spaces. A sharper local comparison yields complete bounds on fixed discarded-link sectors, while collective projection and Schur estimates isolate the additional input needed for a volume-uniform gap. The work also certifies a finite three-link conditioning functional through Wilson coupling 0.354, with its physical interpretation conditional on the stated block-comparison hypotheses. Exact blocking, corrected effective-potential theorems and a representation-by-representation two-dimensional benchmark clarify which approximations preserve the relevant observables. Published glueball measurements retain their original attribution; their reanalysis and the reproduced winding-channel and replica studies have explicitly statistical scope. Complete derivations and reproducible calculations support a set of certified benchmarks and continuum transfer criteria. A nontrivial four-dimensional spatial-cutoff construction and a positive spectral bound along it are not established; no exact continuum mass is asserted.

papers.title: On S\l oci\'nski-type decomposition, BCL model and unitary extension of commuting Banach space Wold isometries
papers.authors: Swapan Jana, Sourav Pal, Saikat Roy
papers.abstract: The adjoint of an operator plays the central role in Hilbert space operator theory. In particular, dilations of Hilbert space contractions, extension of commuting Hilbert space isometries to Hilbert space unitaries, orthogonal decompositions of contractions and functional models for commuting isometries are heavily dependent on the presence of adjoint. In this paper, we develop a theory of Banach space Wold isometries with right-complemented ranges by showing explicit constructions of Berger-Coburn-Lebow model and unitary extension for such isometric tuple without the help of adjoint. We also show that a S\l oci\'nski type decomposition is possible for such a commuting tuple of Banach space isometries. Each of our results generalizes the corresponding result in the Hilbert space theory.

papers.title: Infinite sumsets via model theory
papers.abstract: We prove versions of (variations of) Erd\H{o}s sumset and $B+B+t$ conjectures asked by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson for semigroups equipped with pairwise commuting non-algebraic definable Keisler measures. Our results use model-theoretic methods involving the existence of \emph{many} coheir independent tuples in every definable relation of positive density.

papers.title: Suboptimality of Gaussian quadrature for Freud and logistic weights in weighted Sobolev spaces
papers.abstract:
We study the worst-case error of Gaussian quadrature for integrals over the real line weighted by Freud weights $\exp(-|x|^\beta)$ with $\beta>1$, and by the logistic density $\mathrm{e}^{-x}/(1+\mathrm{e}^{-x})^2$. The integrand functions are assumed to live in the $\rho$-weighted $L^2$-based Sobolev space of smoothness $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}$.
  We prove that any linear quadrature using the $n$ Gaussian nodes, irrespective of the choice of quadrature weights, has a worst-case error bounded from below by a constant times $n^{-\alpha(1-1/\beta)}$ for the Freud weights, and by a constant times $(\log n)^{-\alpha}$ for the logistic weight. Our proof is based on three simple observations. First, the worst-case error of any linear quadrature is bounded from below in terms of the number of its nodes in a fixed interval. Second, the number of Gaussian nodes in such an interval is bounded from above by means of Christoffel functions. Third, Christoffel functions admit sharp lower bounds on such an interval. For the Freud weights with even integer exponents and for the logistic weight, all steps are proved in an elementary and self-contained way; for the logistic weight, we use explicit recurrence coefficients of the corresponding orthogonal polynomials. Our results provide a theoretical explanation, for integrands of finite smoothness, of the slow convergence of Gauss--Logistic quadrature observed in the literature. In contrast, for the logistic weight and for the Freud weights with even integer exponents, the M\"obius-transformed trapezoidal rule attains the optimal rate $n^{-\alpha}$. This rule does not depend on the smoothness $\alpha$ and requires only point values of the integrand and the weight.

papers.title: Universal Critical Relations and Nonuniversal Scaling in Inverse-Square Ising Chains
papers.abstract: For ferromagnetic Ising chains with $n^2J_n\to B>0$, the critical excess magnetization in a field inversely proportional to spin separation determines the connected correlation. Their slowly varying profile has finite logarithmic integral exactly when the ordered thermal slope is finite. For any finite nonnegative core, an exact tail gives inverse-logarithmic correlations and a square-root cusp. A relative correction $c/\log(n+e)$ with $c>1$ gives continuously varying logarithmic powers and a linear cusp. A lower bound on its disordered susceptibility excludes the usual Kosterlitz--Thouless law.

papers.title: Linear bound for commuting matrix algebra II
papers.authors: Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field, and let $A_1,\cdots,A_m$ be pairwise commuting $n\times n$ matrices. For $m\geq3$ and $n\geq2$, we prove \[
  \dim_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{F}[A_1,\cdots,A_m]
  \leq \left\lceil C_m(n-1)\right\rceil \quad\text{with}\quad
  C_m=\frac{\Gamma(m)}{\Gamma((m+1)/2)^2}. \] In particular, three commuting matrices generate an algebra of dimension at most $2n-2$.

papers.title: Comparability for quadratic forms with space-dependent singular measures
papers.abstract: This paper investigates quadratic forms $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ generated by configurations $\Gamma$ and families of measures that are parametrized in the space variable and singular with respect to the Lebesgue measure. A first basic result is the construction of corresponding integro-differential operators in divergence form. These operators are obtained by symmetrizing the family of singular measures. The main result is the comparability of the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ with the quadratic form $\mathcal{E}^s$ which is associated with the fractional Laplacian $(-\Delta)^s$. Comparability of $\mathcal{E}^\Gamma$ and $\mathcal{E}^s$ implies H\"older regularity and a weak Harnack inequality for solutions to integro-differential equations involving these operators.

papers.title: Multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups by Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity
papers.abstract:
A numerical semigroup is a subset of the nonnegative integers, closed under addition and with finite complement. The size of the complement is its genus. The problem of counting semigroups by the largest gap got very important through the so-called Frobenius problem, first documented in 1884. Accordingly, the largest gap is called the Frobenius number. In the last two decades, counting by the genus has become a subject of even more intense study, mostly because of the non-solved conjectures on its monotonic and super-Fibonacci growth.
  It is known that the number of semigroups of each genus grows asymptotically with the genus like the Fibonacci numbers and that the number of semigroups of each Frobenius number grows asymptotically in such a way that each number doubles the previous but one. We prove a formula for the number of numerical semigroups of each Frobenius number, genus, and multiplicity (first nonzero nongap), under the assumption that the multiplicity $m$ and the Frobenius number $F$ satisfy $m\geq\frac{F+1}{3}$. It has been proved that asymptotically almost all semigroups satisfy this condition. From this formula we prove multiparameter recurrence relations. They give, under the required restriction, a multiparameter exact version of the increasing behaviours previously mentioned. Indeed, we prove that the number $n_{F,m,g}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$, multiplicity $m$ and genus $g$ satisfies $n_{F,m,g}=n_{F-2,m-1,g-1}+n_{F-2,m-1,g-2}$ and that the number $n_{F,m}$ of semigroups with Frobenius number $F$ and multiplicity $m$ satisfies $n_{F,m}=2n_{F-2,m-1}.$

papers.title: A rank-zero $2$-converse to the Gross--Zagier and Kolyvagin theorem for elliptic curves with abelian two-division field
papers.abstract: Let $E/\mathbb{Q}$ be an elliptic curve with abelian two-division field. We prove that finiteness of ${\mathrm Sel}_{2^\infty}(E/\mathbb{Q})$ implies $L(E,1)\ne0$. The proof follows the quadratic twist deformation approach of OpenAI: Beilinson--Kato elements are interpolated over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension and over families of quadratic twists, and congruences in the resulting group ring transfer non-vanishing from the twists to $E$. The integral control of this interpolation is governed by one cohomological $\mu$-invariant, which depends only on $E[2]$ and vanishes for abelian two-division fields. Together with Kato's cyclotomic divisibility and the fixed lattice in his construction, it bounds the denominator by a fixed power of $2$, independently of the twisting primes and the family dimension. Congruences among coefficients of a half-integral-weight form, in the style of Ono--Skinner, construct the required twist families.

papers.title: On the $\Delta$-primitive squares conjecture
papers.abstract: A natural number $n$ has the $\Delta$ property if some difference of complementary divisors of $n$ is the sum of two such differences; equivalently, if some split graph has a factor graph containing an $n$-simple triangle. In additive terms, $n$ has the $\Delta$ property exactly when the positive part of the factor-difference set of $n$, introduced by Erd\H{o}s and Rosenfeld, is not sum-free. The set $\mathbb{N}(\Delta)$ of such numbers is closed under multiplication by squares, and it was conjectured that it contains infinitely many $\Delta$-primitive perfect squares. We prove this conjecture, and show that these squares can be chosen to avoid any prescribed finite set of primes but $3$.

papers.title: Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices). Our main result shows that given an $R[x]$-lattice $V$, it admits a left module structure over the Weyl algebra (equivalently, an $R$-linear connection) if and only if all of its indecomposable summands have the form $R[x]\otimes_{R[x^p]}N$, where $N$ is an indecomposable $R[x^p]$-lattice of rank divisible by $p$. We also classify, up to isomorphism, all lattices over the $p$-Weyl algebra (defined by $[y,x]=p$) for which the action of $x$ modulo $p$ is regular nilpotent.

papers.title: No regular icosahedron has a rational point on every face: a proof checked in Lean
papers.abstract: We prove that no regular icosahedron in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has a point with rational coordinates on each of its twenty closed faces, in every position, size and orientation, reflections included. This answers a question of I. Bogdanov on MathOverflow. A field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ that sends $\sqrt5$ to $-\sqrt5$ reduces the problem to the following statement: for every complex orthogonal $3\times3$ matrix $T$ some real linear combination of $\mathrm{Re}\,T$ and $\mathrm{Im}\,T$ separates ten intervals determined by the faces. We prove this statement by a computer-assisted case analysis over rational parametrizations of rotation frames, in which every inequality is an exact polynomial bound over $\mathbb{Z}[\varphi]$, $\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2$; no floating-point arithmetic and no Lipschitz estimates are used. The whole argument, including the $48$ certificates, is formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant with Mathlib and checked by the Lean kernel; the main theorem depends only on the standard axioms. The mathematical argument and the formalization were produced by AI systems (OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude) under the direction of the author; see the statement at the end of the paper.

papers.title: Recursive Pricing and Incumbent Subtree Column Generation for Solving Optimal Classification Trees
papers.authors: Tengmu Hu, Chen Chen, Theodore T. Allen
papers.abstract: Solving optimal classification tree (OCT) problems is computationally challenging because branching, routing, and leaf-assignment decisions must be optimized jointly. We develop an incumbent subtree column generation algorithm (ISCG-OCT) that exploits the recursive structure of classification trees. We first introduce a mixed set-packing and set-partitioning formulation (MSSF). We then construct a restricted master problem whose columns represent feasible subtree patterns. Unlike conventional dual-based column generation, our incumbent-centered pricing evaluates objective improvements relative to the current solution. We establish a recursive decomposition in which fixing a branching decision separates the remaining pricing problem into independent subtree subproblems, enabling exact dynamic programming. We also develop threshold-based variants that trade optimality guarantees for computational efficiency. Computational experiments on 27 benchmark datasets demonstrate competitive training and testing accuracy and substantial reductions in solution time on many instances. When initialized with a CART solution, ISCG-OCT can certify global optimality faster than warm-started mixed-integer programming solvers on selected instances. These results demonstrate how recursive pricing and structured subtree optimization can improve the computational efficiency of exact classification tree methods.

papers.title: Robust Gaussian process regression: posterior contraction
papers.authors: Isma\"el Castillo, Paul Egels, Riccardo Lazzarini, Botond Szab\'o
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes form a popular and flexible class of prior distributions with principled uncertainty quantification, but the Gaussian likelihood on which the corresponding posterior relies makes them highly sensitive to outliers and contaminated observations. We study Gaussian process regression when among the $n$ observations, $m$ of these are possibly contaminated. A generic framework to obtain posterior contraction rates in this setting is considered, from a frequentist perspective as the sample size $n$ and the number of corrupted observations $m$ grow. We adopt a generalized Bayes approach in which the log--likelihood is replaced by a robustified version; we discuss various choices thereof, such as one recently proposed by Altamirano et al. that preserves conjugacy. We investigate the minimax rate of estimation under adversarial contamination in terms of the Sobolev smoothness $\beta$ of the regression function and $m$. The question of building adaptive procedures to both $\beta$ and $m$ is investigated, and we show that a polynomial loss for adaptation must be paid in general. We instantiate our results for Mat\'ern Gaussian process and deep ReLU network priors. Numerical experiments for existing and new robust algorithms are provided, illustrating the practical applicability of our results.

papers.title: Probabilistic Weapon-Target Allocation Models for the Critical Infrastructure Protection
papers.abstract: This paper analyzes methods for solving optimal resource/weapon allocation problems for the protection of critical infrastructure. It examines nonlinear discrete "Attacker-Defender" and "Weapon-Target Allocation" models, incorporating criteria based on the difference in expected losses and risk-related constraints. Methods are proposed for solving these problems by reformulating them as mixed-integer linear programming problems.

papers.title: $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported pro-\'etale cohomology
papers.authors: Pierre Colmez, sally Gilles, Zhenghui Li, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}
papers.abstract:
We prove the \'etale-de Rham direction of the $C_{\st}$-conjecture for compactly supported cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties over local fields of mixed characteristic. More precisely, we recover filtered de Rham cohomology and (under a finite-rank assumption) Hyodo--Kato cohomology from compactly supported $p$-adic pro-\'etale cohomology as derived Hom (in a category of Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces) with values in $\B_{\pdr}$ and $\B_{\pFF}$ respectively (period rings related to $\B_{\dr}$ and $\B_{\st}$ whose higher Galois cohomology vanishes).
  The proof uses, via the geometrized basic comparison theorem, Poincar\'e duality for Hyodo--Kato and (filtered) de Rham cohomology, explicit extension calculations for period sheaves, and fully-faithfulness of the passage from Galois equivariant perfect complexes on the Fargues--Fontaine curve to Arithmetic Topological Vector Spaces.

papers.title: Discrete Distributions and Their Limit Theorems in the Surreal Numbers
papers.abstract: We extend the discrete uniform, hypergeometric and binomial distributions to the surreal numbers, allowing infinitely many outcomes, chips and trials. A uniform distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ gives each outcome probability $1/\omega$; on the eventually periodic sets we define the needed sizes explicitly, obtaining a probability that is regular and strictly monotone. For an urn with infinitely many chips and finitely many draws, the hypergeometric distribution is within an infinitesimal of the binomial. With infinitely many trials, and under a hypothesis on factorials of omnific integers that we show can be satisfied, we prove a surreal de~Moivre--Laplace theorem, and we show that the hypergeometric distribution with infinitely many draws is locally normal with a finite-population correction. Near its center, it is relatively close to the binomial distribution if and only if the sampling fraction is infinitesimal, an exact form of a familiar rule of thumb. For rare successes we prove, without any hypothesis on factorials, a surreal Poisson limit theorem and describe urns with finitely many red chips, where the binomial approximation fails beyond the first success.

papers.title: Kronecker coefficients of large degree and Littlewood-Richardson inequalities
papers.abstract: We prove that Kronecker coefficients are uniformly asymptotic to $f^\lambda f^\mu f^\nu/n!$ when all three irreducible dimensions are at least $\sqrt{n!}\,e^{-A\sqrt n}$, for any fixed $A>0$. This strengthens a conjecture of Pak, Panova and Yeliussizov. For triple staircase and triple square partitions, we obtain relative asymptotics with respective limiting factors $e^{-1/24}$ and $e^{-1/3}$. For Littlewood-Richardson (LR) coefficients, we bound the sum of the three dimension deficits by the LR coefficient deficit times $O(\log n)$, proving their Conjecture 5.5 and extending it to arbitrary fixed size proportions. We also construct vanishing LR coefficients with three Plancherel dimension sequences and determine the exact stabilization threshold of the largest LR coefficient with one input size fixed.

papers.title: Receding horizon control with sensor-induced positive semidefinite state penalization
papers.abstract: This paper develops and analyzes a receding horizon control (RHC) framework for the stabilization of infinite-dimensional nonautonomous continuous-time systems with an infinite-horizon control objective. The considered stage costs penalize only a finite-dimensional component of the state and are therefore positive semidefinite with respect to the full state. Without imposing terminal costs or terminal constraints, we establish exponential stability and derive suboptimality estimates under suitable stabilizability and detectability-type assumptions, together with an online selection of the sampling times. In the linear case, we extend the framework to output-feedback RHC by combining it with a Luenberger-type state estimator based on finitely many sensors, and establish closed-loop stability using an augmented Lyapunov functional. The abstract state-feedback results are verified for a nonlinear Schl\"ogl parabolic equation around an unstable steady state and, in the output-feedback setting, for nonautonomous linear parabolic equations. The control and observation realizations involve finite-dimensional actuation and sensing, including localized boundary controls and spatially localized state-penalization operators. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings and illustrate the performance of the proposed RHC schemes.

papers.title: The Canonical Family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms and the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm for Linear Programming
papers.authors: A. G. Paraskevopoulos, D. A. Patsouras
papers.abstract: A complete canonical family of uniquely normalized, row-equivalent representatives of an $m\times n$ matrix is introduced and termed the family of Reduced Row Pivot Echelon Forms (RRPEFs). All RRPEFs represent the same row space, with the standard reduced row echelon form, renamed the Upper RREF (URREF), and the Lower RREF (LRREF) as its extreme members. A reformulation of Noether's Complementary Subspace Basis Theorem yields normalized bases of the row space that coincide with the nonzero rows of the corresponding RRPEFs. Constructively, each RRPEF is obtained by multi-index Gauss--Jordan reduction of a nonsingular transition submatrix. Factoring the admissible pivot-index sets by equality of their associated RRPEFs yields a quotient set in canonical bijection with the set of distinct RRPEFs. This bijection transfers the strict lexicographic order to the distinct RRPEFs and induces a finite chain from the URREF to the LRREF. The resulting structure gives rise to the Induced Lexicographic Canonical Algorithm (ILCA). Lexicographic confinement and singular-transition skipping restrict the candidate domain, whereas RRPEF reuse and scalar-equivalent transition bypassing avoid redundant Gauss--Jordan reductions while retaining the corresponding basic-solution tableaux. Strict lexicographic progression prevents cycling, while the traversal proceeds independently of objective improvement under degeneracy-induced stalling. ILCA terminates when a feasible tableau satisfies the standard optimality conditions and otherwise completes the finite traversal, including for Tucker- and Cunningham-type totally degenerate configurations.

papers.title: Lift Height and the Structure of Classification Failure
papers.abstract:
We introduce a framework for measuring the depth of classification failure relative to a chosen invariant. A \emph{shadow map} records visible structure while suppressing finer information; lift packages recover this information in successive layers, and lift height measures the depth through which classification ambiguity persists. Canonical reduction removes redundant stages and yields an essential notion of lift height. For nilpotent groups, the lower central series provides a natural commutator lift tower, with lift height controlled by nilpotency class and decreasing under refinement of the shadow. The associated graded structure gives a Lie-theoretic interpretation of the successive commutator layers.
  The main examples show that classification depth is genuinely unbounded. Over any field of characteristic different from two, and for every positive integer, there exist nilpotent Lie algebras with the same fixed four-dimensional abelianisation whose commutator lift packages agree through the prescribed number of layers but differ at the next layer. Moreover, such separation can occur at arbitrarily large degree even when the complete underlying lower-central graded vector space is fixed. Thus neither a fixed shadow nor the dimensions, or even the underlying vector-space structure, of the lower-central graded object impose a uniform bound on the depth at which new commutator information may appear.

papers.title: Pluriclosed flow on K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove the maximal existence conjecture for pluriclosed flow on K\"ahler backgrounds. This leads to a priori generalizations of the Aubin-Yau and Calabi-Yau theorems, and resolves the question of connectedness of generalized K\"ahler structures on Calabi-Yau backgrounds.

papers.title: A Talenti-type result for the Pompeiu-Schiffer Conjecture
papers.abstract: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded simply connected domain carrying a Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In August 2026 it was disproved in the plane by computer-assisted constructions. We revisit the shape-optimization approach of~\cite{Se24} in the light of these counterexamples. We first show that the vanishing of the material derivative on the boundary, assumed in~\cite{Se24}, never holds, and we compute the correct optimality condition, involving an adjoint state, for the associated functional $J_2$. We prove that every planar Schiffer domain satisfies $\max|u| > \sqrt{2}|c|.$ Our main result is a Talenti-type theorem: if $u < c$ in $\Omega$ , then $kR^* \geq j_{1,1},$ where $R^*$ is the radius of the disc of equal area, and equality holds only for the disc. Finally, using Siegel's transcendence theorem, we prove the infinitesimal rigidity of the disc for the Berenstein problem.

papers.title: Division ring extensions and the realization of Coxeter diagrams $I_2(n)$
papers.abstract: For each integer $n\ge5$, we construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(n)$. Both of its diagonal division rings are two-generated over the field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta)$, where $\zeta$ is a primitive root of unity of order $n-2$. The construction is based on a chain of quantized Weyl relations and a shift automorphism. We give one-sided bases for the corresponding division ring extensions and compute the right dimension sequence of the bimodule. The resulting ring has exactly $n$ isomorphism classes of indecomposable finitely generated right modules.

papers.title: A Talenti-type rigidity theorem and P-function constraints for the Pompeiu--Schiffer problem in every dimension
papers.abstract: Schiffer's conjecture asserts that the ball is the only bounded domain, with boundary homeomorphic to a sphere, carrying a nonconstant Neumann eigenfunction of the Laplacian that is constant on the boundary; for such domains it is equivalent to the Pompeiu problem. In 2026 it was disproved in the plane and in many higher dimensions by computer-assisted and analytic constructions. We study what survives.
