Our mathematical formulation relies on a mean field representation of the data assimilation process as well as a mean field Pontryagin minimum principle for the optimal control problem. Such mean field formulations are computationally attractive because they allow for simultaneous implementation in terms of Hamiltonian interacting particle systems. A more detailed discussion is included for the ensemble Kalman-Bucy filter in combination with affine approximations of the receding horizon control laws. This paper sets out the mathematical framework, while a computational study is left for future research.

papers.title: Anomalous regularity and scaling limit by rough transport noise for stochastic 2D fluid models on the torus
papers.abstract: We consider the stochastic 2D Euler and mSQG equations on the torus, with $L^2$ initial data and driven by rough Kraichnan transport noise, for which we construct weak solutions enjoying anomalous regularity and dissipation properties. Moreover, we show that weak solutions in this regularity class are pathwise unique, thus establishing probabilistically strong well-posedness. We further obtain the scaling limit from these equations to the deterministic Navier--Stokes/mSQG equations, with respect to positive Sobolev norms. The proofs rest on the analysis of energy spectrum of the vorticity and on a uniform weighted discrete Poincar\'e inequality on the lattice, the latter being crucial for making the positive norms accessible.

papers.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
papers.authors: Tran Nam Trung, Hoang Le Truong
papers.abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

papers.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
papers.abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

papers.title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
papers.abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same St\"ackel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

papers.title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
papers.abstract: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.

papers.title: Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs
papers.abstract: For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chv\'atal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian. Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible. A graph $G$ is said to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor if and only if $G$ contains a spanning subgraph consisting of components that are either cycles or single edges. A $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor can be viewed as a combination of a $1$-factor and a $2$-factor, motivating the study of such factors in tough graphs. In this paper, we establish sharp sufficient conditions in terms of the adjacency spectral radius, the distance spectral radius, and the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius for a $t$-tough graph to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor.

papers.title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
papers.authors: Xifeng Su, Chengxiang Zhang, Jiwen Zhang
papers.abstract:
We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schr\"odinger equation \begin{equation}
  -Q'' + (-\Delta)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$.
  For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation.
  Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.

papers.title: Adding minimal fresh subsets to $\aleph_\omega$
papers.abstract: Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_\omega$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $\omega$-sequence in $\aleph_\omega$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.

papers.title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
papers.abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $\phi^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

papers.title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
papers.abstract:
We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(\psi,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form
  \begin{align}
  \psi(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}},
  n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)
  \end{align}
  in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system.
  The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(\psi,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$.
  We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

papers.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
papers.authors: Moritz Poguntke, Eda Oktay, Yuanzhe Xi, Erin Carson, Martin Stoll
papers.abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

papers.title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lov\'asz--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

papers.title: Good colorings of doubled triangles and a conjecture of Schwartz
papers.authors: Lakshitha Fernando, Eranda Dhananjaya, Rajitha Ranasinghe, Dinusha Priyadarshani
papers.abstract: A good coloring of a sphere triangulation is a black-and-white coloring of its faces such that, at every vertex, the numbers of black and white faces differ by a multiple of~$3$. Good colorings correspond to proper vertex $4$-colorings. For a good coloring with fold count $\mathrm{f}$ (the number of black-white edges) on a triangulation with $F$ faces, R.~E.~Schwartz introduced the Eisenstein isoperimetric ratio $\eta=\mathrm{f}^2/F$. For triangulations with degree sequence $6,\dots,6,2,2,2$, he proved that $\eta\ge3$ and conjectured that every such triangulation has a good coloring with $\eta$ below a universal constant. These triangulations are indexed by the nonzero Eisenstein integers~$\beta$. We study the family $\T(n)$ given by $\beta=n$, a positive integer, which consists of the doubled equilateral triangles of side~$n$. We prove that every good coloring of $\T(n)$ has at least $3n$ folds, so $\eta\ge9/2$, and that this bound is attained for every~$n$. Thus the minimum of $\eta$ on this family is exactly $9/2$, and Schwartz's conjecture holds for it. We also prove that subdividing a good coloring of $\T(\beta)$ gives a good coloring of $\T(n\beta)$ with the same value of $\eta$. Consequently, Schwartz's conjecture holds in general if and only if it holds for primitive Eisenstein integers.

papers.title: A Computational Brainsphere Model for the Simulation of Alzheimer's Disease
papers.authors: Angela Kunoth, Anna Weller, Tolunay Yilmaz
papers.abstract:
Nowadays, there are different medical imaging techniques to collect data about the progression of
  Alzhei\-mer's disease in a patient's brain. These data describe different phenomena which are still
  not understood from a biological point of view.
  How can these data sets be combined in a mathematical model to simulate the evolution of such a
  neurodegenerative disease in a computer?
  In this snapshot, we present one possible approach to address this task with the help of graph theory
  and partial differential equations.

papers.title: Operational Interpretation of Controllability Allocation Scores via Randomized Interventions
papers.abstract: Controllability allocation scores (CASs) assign weights to virtual input channels without specifying how interventions should be implemented. This paper provides an operational interpretation through randomized finite-duration interventions with prescribed, possibly candidate-dependent waveforms. Selection probabilities are fixed before a mean-output target is specified, while waveform amplitudes are optimized after the target is revealed. We derive the unique minimum expected-energy amplitude policy and formulate volumetric and weighted average-energy allocation criteria. We also establish a finite-trial mean-output error bound and show that waveform-based weighted AE-CAS minimizes an upper bound on the target-averaged mean-square error. We establish uniform convergence of normalized waveform-response Gramians and show that accumulation points of optimal allocations solve the limiting problem. With uniform timing, equal positive waveform efficiencies recover the original CAS in the short-duration limit, whereas unequal efficiencies yield waveform-weighted limits. Under the former conditions, the limiting error bound is proportional to the original weighted AE-CAS objective. For common waveforms, we further establish an exact finite-duration correspondence with the original full-state V-CAS under uniform timing.

papers.title: Branched real projective structures on surfaces, cyclic Higgs Bundles and Anosov representations
papers.abstract: We use the theory of $3$-cyclic $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$-Higgs bundles to study real branched projective structures on compact surfaces recently introduced by the authors. After fixing a Riemann surface structure on $S$, the Higgs bundle approach allows us, on the one hand, to construct branched structures with prescribed branching data and, on the other hand, to introduce new classes of such structures. The latter are directly related to singular hyperbolic affine spheres and carry a Blaschke metric with conical singularities. In the final part of the paper, using different methods, we prove that every Anosov surface group representation into $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{R})$ is either Hitchin or belongs to the Barbot component. As a by-product, we obtain that some of the representations associated with the branched structures constructed above are not Anosov.

papers.title: Permutons
papers.authors: Jacopo Borga, Valentin F\'eray, Peter Winkler
papers.abstract: Permutons are limit structures for large permutations. Intrinsically, a permuton is a familiar mathematical object: a probability measure on the unit square with uniform marginals. The compact space of permutons completes the set of permutations of all sizes under a natural topology; each permuton is not only a limit of permutations but also a generator of random permutations. Since their (relatively recent) discovery as a tool for understanding the behavior of large (possibly random) permutations, permutons have proved remarkably fruitful, with dozens of fascinating connections to combinatorics and probability. We review the fundamentals of permutons, sometimes providing new, shorter proofs, and give an account of some of their myriad applications. The survey concludes with a long list of open problems. An extensive -- but not comprehensive -- bibliography is appended.

papers.title: Geometry and Stochastic Analysis of Flow and Diffusion Models: A Survey
papers.abstract: Flow-based and diffusion-based models have become the principal means of learning and sampling high-dimensional probability distributions, from images and video to proteins, molecules and physical fields, and increasingly language. Each carries a simple law to the law of the data along a curve of probability measures, and behind the variety of their names lie three geometries, those of the state space on which the data live, of the space of probability measures through which the curve passes, and of the space of paths traced by the generating process. A single analytic idea runs through the subject. Every score identity used to train a diffusion model is an integration by parts, on the noise, on the data or on Wiener space, and Malliavin calculus extends this to nonlinear and infinite-dimensional diffusions. We develop these foundations with full definitions and follow them through normalising flows, flow matching and few-step maps, diffusion models and their convergence theory, conditioning, Schr\"odinger bridges and stochastic control, and their extension to manifolds, Lie groups, discrete and function spaces and jump processes. We close with statistical physics, renormalisation and, more speculatively, holography, in which the radial direction of anti-de Sitter space can play the role of flow time. A table of the main methods and a collection of open problems complete the survey.

papers.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
papers.authors: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Benedetto Piccoli, Emmanuel Tr\'elat
papers.abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

papers.title: Almost complex structures on triple blow-ups
papers.abstract: We show that for certain smooth 4-manifolds, almost complex structures on its triple blow-up induce all its spin$^c$ structures with a non-negative-dimensional Seiberg-Witten moduli space. Since this includes all basic classes, our result provides an approximation to the simple type conjecture. Moreover, we expand a result by Dieter Kotschick showing that every finitely presented group is the fundamental group of an almost complex 4-manifold. We show that it can furthermore be chosen to have every even integer as the virtual dimension of the Seiberg-Witten moduli space of a spin$^c$ structure.

papers.title: Ride-time inequalities for the event-based formulation of the dial-a-ride problem
papers.abstract: The paper investigates the model structure of the event-based mixed-integer programming formulation of the Dial-a-Ride Problem. We find that the design of events allows introducing new valid inequalities on the ride times. Time progression is modelled using Big M constraints which lead to a weak LP relaxation and deteriorate the solution process. The newly introduced valid inequalities deal with this issue and allow reducing the computation times by up to 99% for benchmark instances (a-X* instances) in comparison to the state-of-the-art event-based model formulation. To evaluate the potential of the new valid inequalities, we increase the time windows on the benchmark set by another 15 minutes and evaluate the model on the same instances with a time-related objective function where the Big-M-influenced time variables directly occur in the objective function. Even for the large time windows only two instances could not be solved to optimality within two hours (final gaps of at most 0.8%). With the time-oriented objective the largest average computation time with our valid inequalities was 74 seconds.

papers.title: On necessary conditions for feedback stabilizability when the control space is a fiber bundle
papers.authors: Wouter Jongeneel, Martina Scolamiero, Karl Henrik Johansson
papers.abstract: Within control theory, a question of great interest is to understand when a stabilizing feedback exists. Building upon Krasnosel'ski\u{\i} and co-workers, necessary conditions for the existence of a continuous stabilizing feedback have been pioneered by Brockett and Coron, providing so-called adversarial and homological conditions, respectively. Kvalheim recently generalized their conditions from equilibria to compact attractors and---in line with earlier work by Coron---showed that when a control system can be identified with a vector bundle, the homology condition is stronger, that is, the homology condition implies the adversary condition. Kvalheim also showed that this comparison breaks when extending the case of vector bundles to fiber bundles. In this work, we propose and characterize an appropriate adversarial condition for control systems represented by fiber bundles. The homology condition, on the other hand, is already well-defined, showcasing its general applicability. With the generalized conditions at hand, we show that by appropriately relaxing the regularity of the feedback under consideration, that is, by allowing for mild discontinuities, the homology condition implies the adversarial condition for fiber bundles. Thereby, in this work, we extend these earlier comparative results.

papers.title: Controllability with and without Dissipation - a Port-Hamiltonian Approach
papers.authors: Jochen Gl\"uck, Anthony Hastir, Birgit Jacob, Hannes Wagener
papers.abstract: A port-Hamiltonian system with energy dissipation can be modelled by connecting a larger, non-dissipative system with a so-called closure relation. We study whether approximative controllability of the dissipative system is characterised by the same property of the larger system. The answer is negative in general, but positive for sufficiently well-structured systems - this is our main result. As a simple illustration, we show how approximate controllability of a wave equation implies approximate controllability of a heat equation.

papers.title: On semigroups of order-decreasing partial isometries: presentations and ranks of certain ideals
papers.authors: Gonca Ay\i k, Hayrullah Ay\i k, V\'itor H. Fernandes
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the monoid of all order-decreasing partial isometries on a chain with $n$ elements, and let $\mathcal{ODP}_{n}^{-}$ denote the submonoid of $\mathcal{DP}_{n}^{-}$ consisting of all order-preserving partial isometries. In this paper, for each $1\leq r\leq n$, we determine minimal generating sets of the ideals $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}(n,r) =\{ \alpha \in \mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n} : \lvert \im(\alpha) \rvert \leq r \}$ of $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$, thereby determining their ranks. Furthermore, we give presentations for the monoids $\mathcal{ODP}^{-}_{n}$ and $\mathcal{DP}^{-}_{n}$.

papers.title: Super-positivity via Dirichlet theta functions
papers.abstract: Let $\chi$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character and let $\Lambda(\chi, s)$ be its associated completed $L$-function. The super-positivity property, introduced by Yun--Zhang (2017), asserts that $\Lambda^{(m)} \left( \frac{1}{2}, \chi \right) \geq 0$ for all $m \geq 0$. We show that a certain positivity property of its Dirichlet theta function $\theta(t, \chi)$, namely that $\theta(t, \chi)>0$ for all $t \geq 1$, implies the super-positivity property for $\chi$. We then investigate a refined form of the above property: we conjecture that the sequence $\{ \Lambda^{(2m)}\left(\frac{1}{2}, \chi \right )\}_{ m \geq 0}$ is always eventually increasing and has at most one turning point, and we prove these assertions again when $\theta(t, \chi)>0$ for $t \geq 1$.

papers.title: The strong cylinder conjecture over prime fields
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be prime and let $S\subseteq\mathbb F_p^3$ have $p^2$ points, with every affine plane meeting $S$ in a multiple of $p$ points. We give a self-contained argument that $S$ is a union of $p$ parallel lines.

papers.title: Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.

papers.title: A Rooted Structure Theorem for $5$-Connected Graphs and $K_6^-$-Minors
papers.abstract: Jorgensen conjectured that every $6$-connected graph with no $K_6$-minor is apex. For a $6$-connected graph containing a $K_4$ on vertices $a_1,\dots,a_4$, being apex is equivalent to $G-a_i$ having a planar embedding with the other three roots on a common face for some $i$, so that for such graphs the conjecture becomes a rooted planarity statement. Robertson, Seymour, and Thomas showed that the failure of the corresponding three-rooted planarity is witnessed by a legless tripod. We introduce a four-root structure, called a frame, that extends this certificate, and prove a structural theorem: every $5$-connected graph containing a frame rooted at four prescribed vertices contains a subgraph of one of five explicit types, denoted $A$--$E$. This theorem does not depend on the edges among the roots. As an application, we show that when the four roots span a $K_4^-$, each of the five configurations yields a $K_6^-$-minor. Together with a planar argument for the case without a frame and an induction based on a theorem of Kawarabayashi, this gives a proof that every non-planar $5$-connected graph contains a $K_6^-$-minor. This statement also follows from a recent theorem of Lo; our proof is independent and is driven by the rooted structure theorem, whose method we expect to apply to Jorgensen's conjecture with other target configurations.

papers.title: Scalar curvature deformation of isoparametric tubes
papers.abstract: We resolve Ge's local scalar curvature rigidity conjecture for spherical isoparametric tubes. The conjecture fails throughout its stated radius range for families with at least two distinct principal curvatures, via arbitrarily small smooth deformations supported in any regular annulus. Geodesic balls of radius less than $\frac{\pi}{2}$ are locally rigid under $C^2$ smallness. We also prescribe sufficiently small smooth nonradial scalar-curvature increments with fixed compact interior support, under antipodal symmetry for families with 2, 4, or 6 distinct principal curvatures and without symmetry for families with 3 distinct principal curvatures.

papers.title: Functions with finite energy on the Sierpinski gasket
papers.abstract: This paper develops a systematic framework for constructing finite-energy functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket using Lipschitz maps and various classes of contractions. Several properties of the constructed functions are investigated, including the min--max property and bounds for their energy. Several examples of finite-energy functions, along with their graphical representations, are provided to illustrate the functions constructed using the proposed framework. It is further shown that finite energy does not necessarily imply membership in the domain of the Laplacian. The framework is then applied to a class of fractal interpolation functions on the Sierpi\'nski gasket, for which necessary and sufficient conditions for finite energy are established under suitable contractivity assumptions.

papers.title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
papers.abstract: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.

papers.title: Whitney-Type Real-Analytic Approximation on Banach Spaces I: The $C^0$ and $C^1$ Cases
papers.abstract:
The classical Whitney theorem on real-analytic approximation is a fundamental result in finite-dimensional analysis and geometry. Extending this theory to general infinite-dimensional Banach spaces involves longstanding open problems. This paper is the first part of our study of Whitney-type real-analytic approximation on Banach spaces, focusing on the $C^0$ and $C^1$ cases.
  We prove that a real Banach space admits a separating polynomial if and only if it admits a polynomial topological embedding into a real Hilbert space. We also introduce classes of mappings that locally factor through polynomial maps into finite-dimensional spaces and develop methods of real-analytic approximation for these classes. Using these tools, we establish fine $C^0$ and $C^1$ real-analytic approximation theorems for broad classes of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones.
  As applications, we resolve several open problems, including those concerning Whitney-type extensions with real analyticity off closed sets, real-analytic approximation preserving Lipschitz constants, and the real-analytic equivalence of diffeomorphic open subsets of Hilbert spaces.

papers.title: On Relative Smoothness in Dually Flat Geometry
papers.abstract: We study the geometric meaning of relative smoothness on dually flat manifolds and its implications for the convergence analysis of mirror descent. Our main result yields one-sided counterparts of the classical Levi--Civita characterizations of Lipschitz Riemannian gradients, each equivalent to relative smoothness. We further investigate the stationarity of mirror descent iterates for possibly nonconvex objectives and show that relative smoothness alone does not guarantee convergence of the Riemannian gradient norm to zero. We identify a one-sided condition on the cubic tensor that ensures such convergence and yields an $O(1/N)$ stationarity bound. Examples based on the negative entropy potential illustrate the role of metric variation.

papers.title: Involution-Preserving schemes through constrained mesh motion: a novel Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian framework
papers.authors: Sacha Cardonna, Elena Bernardelli, Walter Boscheri
papers.abstract: We introduce a novel structure-preserving finite volume method that exploits mesh motion to enforce differential involutions arising in hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. The key idea is to leverage the geometric degrees of freedom of an Arbitrary-Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) framework to construct a constrained mesh motion that is intrinsically compatible with the involution constraints embedded in the governing equations. The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Particular care is devoted to the consistent evolution of the mesh geometry and the satisfaction of the Geometric Conservation Law (GCL). The proposed framework is applied to two representative hyperbolic systems featuring distinct involution constraints: the ideal magnetohydrodynamics equations, endowed with the divergence-free condition on the magnetic field, and the hyperbolic Euler-Heat equations, subject to a curl-free constraint on the thermal impulse. Second-order accuracy in time is achieved through a Runge-Kutta discretization, with the geometric constraints consistently enforced at each stage. A comprehensive set of classical benchmark problems is presented to assess the accuracy and effectiveness of the method. The numerical results demonstrate that appropriately constrained mesh motion provides an effective mechanism for preserving differential involutions, establishing a novel connection between mesh geometry and the structure-preserving discretization of hyperbolic systems.

papers.title: The multiplicity bound for near-group fusion categories of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z+k$. We show $k\in\{0,3,4\}$, which then gives a complete characterization of near-group fusion categories determined by $\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$.

papers.title: Negative normal degree and holomorphic sectional curvature pinching
papers.abstract: We obtain an upper bound for the local holomorphic sectional curvature pinching of a K\"ahler manifold containing a smooth rational curve of negative total normal degree. As an application, we prove that a compact K\"ahler surface with positive holomorphic sectional curvature and local pinching constant at least $1/9$ is biholomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$, $\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, or the first Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_1$. For pinching strictly greater than $1/9$, only the first two possibilities occur, confirming a conjecture of Yang and Zheng. We also determine the optimal local pinching constants on $\mathbb F_1$ and $\mathbb F_2$.

papers.title: Hilton's Conjecture on Uncomplemented Incomparable Families
papers.authors: Yuejian Peng, Zilong Yan, Cheng Zhao
papers.abstract:
A family ${\mathcal A}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is \emph{uncomplemented} if it contains no set together with its complement. Families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t$ are \emph{strongly incomparable} if every set in one family is incomparable with every set in another family.
  In 1976, Hilton conjectured that if ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ are uncomplemented and strongly incomparable, then $$\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|\le 2^{n-1}.$$ We confirm this conjecture by a matrix rank argument that encodes incomparability and uncomplementedness in the same matrix, which is quite different from the earlier methods on this problem.
  We also study weak incomparability, in which the same set may occur in different families. Goldwasser, Hilton and Zheng conjectured an upper bound in this setting and claimed that their conjecture is equivalent to Hilton's conjecture. We give counterexamples to their conjecture for every $t\ge3$ and identify the error in the claimed equivalence. We then propose a replacement conjecture and confirm it when $t$ is large.
  The upper bound $2^{n-1}$ in Hilton's conjecture can be attained if some families are allowed to by empty. It is natural to consider the maximum size of $\sum_{i=1}^t |{\mathcal A}_i|$ for uncomplemented and strongly incomparable families ${\mathcal A}_1,\ldots,{\mathcal A}_t\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ when all families are required to be non-empty. Denote this maximum number by $M(n,t)$. We show that \[ 2^{n-1}-1\le M(n,t)\le 2^{n-1} \] for $n\ge3$ and $3\le t\le n$.

papers.title: Generalizations of Igusa surfaces
papers.authors: Pascal Fong, Matilde Maccan, Ludvig Modin
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.

papers.title: Minimum cumulative power divergence estimation with applications to copulas
papers.abstract: Parametric inference based on distribution functions is useful when a model is naturally specified through its cumulative distribution function or when a tractable density is unavailable. We study minimum cumulative power divergence estimation, obtained by comparing a parametric distribution function with its empirical counterpart. For a fixed positive tuning parameter and a fixed finite integration measure, we establish the existence of a consistent sequence of local solutions to the estimating equations and derive its asymptotic normality. The resulting covariance has a sandwich form whose components involve derivatives of the distribution function and the covariance kernel of the multivariate empirical process. We specialize the construction to copulas using Lebesgue measure on the unit cube, and distinguish estimation with known margins from estimation based on ranks. In the latter case, the covariance incorporates the effect of estimating the marginal distributions. The relationship with the copula divergences of Eguchi and Kato is made explicit: the power loss is closely related, whereas the integration measure determines a different estimation criterion. A simulation design for Gumbel, Clayton, and Frank copulas examines the estimation of Kendall's tau under correct specification, family misspecification, and contamination by independence. The simulations show competitive clean-data accuracy but no general robustness advantage over the empirical-copula-weighted alternatives under independence contamination.

papers.title: Geodesic connectedness of globally hyperbolic spacetimes with a causal Killing vector field
papers.abstract: We characterize the existence of a geodesic joining two prescribed points of a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ admitting a complete causal Killing vector field $K$ and a complete smooth spacelike Cauchy hypersurface $S$. We prove that two points $p,q\in M$ are joined by a geodesic if and only if there exists an $H^1$ curve $\gamma$ from $p$ to $q$ such that $g(\dot\gamma,K)$ is constant almost everywhere. The statement is intrinsic and allows $K$ to be timelike at some points and lightlike at others. A global splitting induced by the flow of $K$ is used in the proof, but no global bounds on the metric coefficients are imposed. The proof relies on stationary perturbations of $(M,g)$, whose relevant compactness properties follow from global hyperbolicity of $g$, and on uniform estimates based on an integral admissibility condition and a Glaeser-type inequality. Two examples illustrate geodesic connectedness and the obstruction detected by the characterization.

papers.title: On operators with many spectral components
papers.abstract: For a complex Banach algebra $\mathscr A$ with unit and $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ be the set of all elements whose spectrum has at least $n$ connected components, and let $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)=\sup\{n;\;\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)\neq\varnothing\}$ be the spectral depth of $\mathscr A$. We characterize nonemptiness of $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ in terms of orthogonal idempotents, compute $d_\sigma(\mathscr A)$ for finite-dimensional algebras, and show that every class $\mathcal C_n(\mathscr A)$ is open. For operators on an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space $X$ these classes are dense in $\mathscr B(X)$, which implies that $\mathcal C_\infty(\mathscr B(X))$ is a dense $G_\delta$-subset of $\mathscr B(X)$. By contrast, we exhibit a commutative Banach algebra whose spectral classes are all nonempty and none of which is dense. For self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space, we obtain sharper perturbation results, with positive semi-definite perturbations of prescribed rank producing spectra with exactly $n$ components. We show that a quasinilpotent weighted forward shift $S_w$ on $X$ admits a nilpotent rank-one operator $F$ such that the spectrum of $S_w+\alpha F$ has infinitely many components for every nonzero $\alpha$.

papers.title: Branch points and natural boundaries of Poincar\'e functions and of solutions of nonlinear functional differential equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the singularity structure of the analytic continuation of solutions to the equation $g(\lambda w)=R(g(w))$, where $|\lambda|<1$ and $R$ is a rational function. We show that the analytic solution \(g\) near zero is branched, and that its analytic continuation yields an infinite-sheeted Riemann surface with various patterns of branch points. In one specific pattern, some branch points are delayed: they appear only when the analytic continuation reaches a particular Riemann sheet. Using this functional-equation framework, we extend the study to first-order nonlinear functional differential equations. We show that the continuation of certain special solutions near an attracting fixed point yields either single-valued or multivalued functions, with the unit circle as a natural boundary on every sheet.

papers.title: A criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval for a certain class of multigeometric series
papers.authors: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn
papers.abstract:
The paper studies the topological structure of the set of subsums (incomplete sums) of multigeometric series of the form $\frac{k_1}{s} + \frac{k_2}{s} + \ldots + \frac{k_m}{s} + \frac{k_1}{s^2} + \frac{k_2}{s^2} + \ldots+ \frac{k_m}{s^2} + \frac{k_1}{s^3} + \frac{k_2}{s^3} +\ldots$, where $k_1, \ldots, k_m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. In terms of graph theory, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for the set of subsums of a given series not to be a finite union of closed intervals, as well as necessary and sufficient conditions for this set to contain an interval. As a consequence of these statements, a criterion for the set of subsums to be a Cantorval is obtained. An example of applying the criterion to a series whose Cantorval property was previously unknown is given.
  A more general object of study of topological properties is the set of numbers whose representations in a numerical system with a natural base and a redundant alphabet are subject to restrictions on the use of digits. It is for this object that the above statements are proved.

papers.title: Globally Simple Heffter Arrays $H(n;k)$ with $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$
papers.abstract: Heffter arrays are combinatorial structures that can be used to construct orthogonal cyclic cycle decompositions of complete graphs. A square Heffter array $H(n;k)$ is a partially filled $n \times n$ array with $k$ filled cells in each row and column. Its entries are distinct and nonzero, form a half-set of the group $\mathbb{Z}_{2nk+1}$, and sum to zero in every row and column. If the natural orderings of the rows and columns of an array are simple, the array is called globally simple. The globally simple property guarantees the orthogonal cycle decompositions constructed from the Heffter array consist of simple cycles. While existence results are known for most congruence classes of the parameters $n$ and $k$ modulo 4 for square globally simple Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$, the existence for $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ has remained largely open. In this paper, we present a construction for globally simple integer Heffter arrays $H(n;k)$ covering all admissible values of $n$ when $k \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$. This settles the existence question across all congruence classes.

papers.title: Generation of semigroups for vector-valued pseudodifferential operators on the torus with space-dependent symbols
papers.authors: Bienvenido Barraza Mart\'{i}nez, Robert Denk, Jairo Hern\'andez Monz\'on, Max Nendel
papers.abstract: We consider toroidal pseudodifferential operators with spatially dependent, operator-valued symbols of positive order and finite regularity. For an arbitrary complex Banach space $E$, we prove that the negative of the closure of a parabolic operator on $C^\infty(\mathbb T^n,E)$ generates an analytic semigroup on $W_p^k(\mathbb T^n,E)$, where $1\le p<\infty$ and $k\in\mathbb N_0$, provided the symbol has sufficiently many spatial derivatives and discrete differences. The proof combines uniform estimates for parameter-dependent kernels with right and left parametrices. It does not require the UMD property of $E$. Real interpolation gives corresponding resolvent estimates on $B_{pq}^s(\mathbb T^n,E)$ for $0<s<k$ and $1\le q\le\infty$. The induced semigroups are strongly continuous for $q<\infty$ and on the little Besov spaces when $q=\infty$.

papers.title: Mitigating the BICM Loss in MIMO Receivers with Correlation-Informed Logits
papers.abstract: Bit-interleaved coded modulation (BICM) is widely used in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) wireless systems. However, separating MIMO data detection from channel decoding and only exchanging per-bit soft information discards correlation information among the bits within each transmit vector. We show that the resulting information loss limits the performance of practical one-shot receivers. Even though iterative detection and decoding (IDD) can recover most of this loss, IDD significantly increases receiver complexity and latency. In order to reduce this loss, we propose COrrelation-Informed Logits (COIL), a soft-output format that combines per-bit soft information with pairwise coupling logits for correlated bits. We show how to incorporate these coupling logits into a conventional belief-propagation-based channel decoder, which enables correlation-aware decoding in a one-shot receiver without IDD. We evaluate COIL in a MIMO-BICM system with a conventional low-density parity-check code. For a 4x4 MIMO orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) system, a one-shot linear minimum mean-square error (LMMSE) receiver with COIL outperforms a conventional one-shot unbiased LMMSE receiver by 1.3dB and operates within 0.8dB of four-iteration IDD, while requiring only a single pass through the data detector.

papers.title: Multi-Target Tracking via Mean Field Feedback Control
papers.authors: Changming Lei, Junhao Dai, Donghua Shi
papers.abstract: Cooperative tracking of multiple moving targets requires a swarm to continually adjust its deployment. Existing methods often rely on repeated agent-target reassignment or updates to position-dependent partitions, which can complicate coordination as swarms grow. This motivates us to seek an approach with a lighter coordination burden. Specifically, we formulate multi-target tracking as a time-varying density-tracking problem, with the targets' tracking and sensing demands encoded in a task-demand density. From an Onsager-type variational formulation, a closed-form mean-field feedback law is derived to make the swarm density track this evolving density, and the resulting closed-loop system is shown to be well posed. Under the stated assumptions, a Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence analysis establishes exponential KL convergence under ideal feedback and conditional robustness to feedback mismatch under estimated. Numerical experiments demonstrate effective tracking of multiple moving targets and show smaller density errors at comparable applied control energy compared with an existing density-tracking feedback method.

papers.title: Cube tilings, partition counters, and the Calkin--Wilf and Kepler trees
papers.authors: Jaros{\l}aw Grytczuk, Andrzej P. Kisielewicz, Krzysztof Przes{\l}awski
papers.abstract: A tiling of the integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ by translates of the discrete cube $K_d=\{0,1\}^d$ cuts every translate $K_d+x$ into subcubes. We study the function $\ell(x)$ counting these parts. Its sum over every translate of $K_d$ equals $3^d$, for an arbitrary translation set. For lattice tilings with a triangular basis we obtain a dimension-reduction formula, and we describe every cocyclic lattice by a single normalized congruence. Along a cyclic generator, the counter of a signed bidiagonal lattice is a row of Stern's diatomic sequence; pairs of counter values realize the Calkin--Wilf tree, and complementary binary words realize the Kepler tree. For the binary lattice, the translated counter labelings of the cube carry generating face partitions, supplied by the tiling itself, which force the levels of the Kepler tree, and every nontrivial face partition has a unique lamination direction. Using finite Fourier analysis we prove that the ordered cyclic profile determines a standard cocyclic cube tiling lattice up to coordinate reflections. For lattices tiling by discrete boxes we determine exactly when the analogous statement holds.

papers.title: Odd realisation numbers of rigid graphs
papers.authors: Sean Dewar, Anthony Nixon, Ben Smith
papers.abstract: Determining the number of realisations of a rigid graph for a specific choice of edge lengths is a fundamental problem in discrete geometry. Gortler, Healy and Thurston showed that the number of real realisations of a generic framework is always even or equal to one. Despite being rare, there do exist graphs whose number of complex realisations is odd and not equal to one. In this article, we exhibit two necessary conditions for a rigid graph to have an odd realisation number other than one. We also provide an infinite family of rigid graphs with an odd realisation number other than one.

papers.title: Fundamental Outage and Diversity Limits of Fluid Antenna Multiple Access Under Correlated Nakagami-$m$ Fading
papers.abstract:
Existing analytical studies of fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) are largely confined to Rayleigh fading, independent-port assumptions, or asymptotic selection metrics, leaving the fundamental outage behavior under realistic fading and spatial correlation conditions uncharacterized.
  This paper fills this gap by presenting the first exact and asymptotically tight outage analysis of interference-limited FAMA systems under spatially correlated Nakagami-$m$ fading. By explicitly modeling the joint statistics of the desired and interference powers across fluid-antenna ports, \textcolor{black}{we first formulate the outage probability in terms of the joint
  desired-signal and interference distributions and then derive an explicit
  integral expression under a tractable single-reference-port spatial
  correlation model.} Building on this result, we establish a rigorous diversity-order characterization
  revealing that the achievable diversity is jointly dictated by the fading severity and the spatial correlation rank imposed by the finite antenna aperture, rather than by the nominal number of ports. 
  To enable accurate and tractable performance evaluation beyond the asymptotic regime, we further introduce a Gamma-matched outage approximation that preserves both the exact diversity order and the array-gain constant. The resulting closed-form expression provides an accurate characterization over a wide range of signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) thresholds and offers clear physical insight into the role of spatial correlation in FAMA systems. Extensive Monte Carlo (MC) simulations confirm the tightness of the exact analysis, the sharpness of the asymptotic results, and the accuracy of the proposed approximation.

papers.title: Certified finite-precision readout for $p$-adic kernel aggregation
papers.abstract: In non-archimedean numerical analysis, a verified $p$-adic approximation can determine an absolute value, and hence downstream probabilistic rankings and classification decisions, with mathematical exactness long before the underlying number is fully resolved. We turn this observation into rigorous finite-precision certificates for norm-based readouts of amplitude families. For a common error radius, a nonempty resolved set already fixes every exact maximizer, ties included, at the sharp integer absolute precision $v_*+1$, and conditioning on that set yields an exact total-variation identity separating unresolved $p$-adic mass from real rounding error. For aggregates of $p$-adic exponentials, we give a centered-moment certificate with an explicit remainder bound: on rational data it runs in exact rational arithmetic without individual exponential evaluations, attains its minimal bound at an active phase, and resolves every nonzero aggregate at high order; we also obtain an aggregate perturbation bound free of summand-count factors. For multiclass $p$-adic classifiers that decode by minimizing the norm of a class discriminant, we prove a necessary and sufficient certification condition and show that the sharp common precision threshold is $v^{(2)}+1$, governed by the second-largest discriminant valuation, so the winning discriminant need not itself be resolved. We apply these certificates to discrete $p$-adic path-integral actions on uniform affine chains, deriving explicit action centers and proving exact output-independence at zero effective quadratic coupling. Pseudocode and a reproducible reference implementation accompany the theory.

papers.title: Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms II: traces of quantum modular cocycles
papers.authors: Stavros Garoufalidis, Danylo Radchenko, Campbell Wheeler
papers.abstract: We study traces of quantum modular cocycles at fixed points of hyperbolic elements $\gamma\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, formulate an algebraicity conjecture for these traces, and prove it for the cocycles associated to 1-dimensional state-integrals. In addition, we analyse a finite TQFT associated with $\gamma$ and conjecture that its invariants for 3-manifolds agree with the traces of their $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ quantum modular cocycles. The finite TQFTs predict a yet-to-be-defined motive with cohomology equipped with a $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-degree grading and a $\mathbb{Z}$-weight grading coming from a version of the Riemann hypothesis, which suggests a similar grading should exist for an extension of the Kauffman bracket skein module, for the framed $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Floer cohomology of Abouzaid--Manolescu, and for the quantum modular cocycle. This leads to surprising additive identities among algebraic units, which we confirm for the complement of the simplest hyperbolic knot $4_1$, as well as for $S^1 \times \Sigma_g$ for a closed genus $g$ surface.

papers.title: On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
papers.authors: Alexandr Garbali, Cengiz Gazi, Jan de Gier, William Mead, Michael Wheeler
papers.abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

papers.title: Asymptotics of matrix orthogonal polynomials with non-scalar varying weights
papers.abstract: We study the $2\times 2$ matrix orthogonal polynomials $\mathbf{P}_N$ on the real line with respect to the varying weights $\mathrm{e}^{-N\mathbf{Q}(z)}\mathbf{B}(z)$, where $\mathbf{Q}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ are real symmetric matrix polynomials that commute with a Hermite-type matrix weight, $\mathbf{Q}$ is not scalar and $\mathbf{B}$ is positive definite. We are motivated by the non-Abelian Toda deformation of the Hermite-type weight, in the sense of Dea\~no, Morey and Rom\'an. The weight depends on $N$ through a matrix exponential that is not scalar, so that its two eigenvalues have different exponential rates. The matrix orthogonality reduces to two scalar orthogonality problems on the real line, with a varying weight that has an essential singularity at the origin. Assuming that the associated equilibrium measure is one-cut regular, we obtain the strong asymptotics of $\mathbf{P}_N$ and of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$ by the Deift-Zhou steepest descent method. Our main result is the limiting zero distribution of the entries of $\mathbf{P}_N$. These zeros are complex in general, and they accumulate on a curve where the contributions of the two eigenvalues of the weight have the same size. When this curve crosses the real segment that attracts the zeros of $\det\mathbf{P}_N$, the zeros of the entries display a critical behavior, and a positive fraction of them accumulates on this segment.

papers.title: Rates in the weak invariance principle for slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems
papers.abstract: We obtain rates of convergence in the weak invariance principle for certain classes of slowly mixing sequential dynamical systems. In particular, for systems satisfying a Functional Correlation Bound with rate $n^{-\gamma} \ (\gamma>1)$, we establish an explicit bound in the Wasserstein-$r$ metric for $1\le r<\gamma+1$ whenever the variance grows at a sufficiently fast polynomial rate. The proof is based on Bernstein's ``big block--small block" method. Examples covered by our result include sequential heterochaos baker maps and sequential LSV maps. In particular, for random LSV maps over an ergodic base, we obtain rates in the quenched weak invariance principle.

papers.title: Resonances of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck Operator
papers.abstract: We study the subellipticity of the analytically deformed Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator and give two definitions of resonances, one based on analytic dilation and the other on analytic distortion in the $x$-variables. Due to the failure of global subellipticity of the distorted operator in dimensions $n \geq 2$, the second method can only be used in dimension one. We show that, whenever both methods are applicable, they give rise to the same set of resonances. We also prove that, when $|\na V(x)| = O(\w x^{-\rho})$ with $\rho>1$, positive resonances are embedded eigenvalues and/or scattering resonances whose resonant states belong to weighted $L^2$-spaces and satisfy an outgoing radiation condition.

papers.title: Translation continuity for the local bilinear circular maximal operator
papers.abstract: We prove a positive power translation-continuity estimate for the local bilinear circular maximal operator on the real line. More precisely, there is $\eta>0$ such that the operator applied to a translation difference in either input maps $L^8(\mathbb{R})\times L^8(\mathbb{R})$ to $L^4(\mathbb{R})$ with norm $O(|h|^\eta)$. This answers Question 6.3 in Borges's survey on bilinear spherical averages. The main step is a frequency-localized estimate for arbitrary bounded inputs. A $TT^*$ argument converts it into a linear maximal problem on the plane, associated with pairs of circles. We verify the corrected multi-parameter cinematic curvature condition of Chen, Guo, and Yang by proving an irreducibility and infinitesimal independence statement for the resulting quartic curves. Uniform algebraic sublevel estimates control the degeneracies. Interpolation also gives continuity for all finite exponents $2<p,q<\infty$, with output exponent $pq/(p+q)$.

papers.title: Asymptotic spreading of Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments with time-periodic limits
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the rightward spreading speed of solutions for Fisher-KPP equations in shifting environments. The linear growth rate has time periodic limits at the two ends of the moving frame. Each limit has a positive average and may be negative during a period. When the growth rate lies between the two limits at each time, we show that the spreading speed depends only on their averages and the asymptotic shift speed. For intermediate shift speeds, the formulas give nonlocal pulling if the right end has the larger average and speed locking if the left end has the larger average. The interior growth profile may be nonmonotone in space and aperiodic in time. We prove the formulas by constructing upper and lower solutions for a stepwise profile and then comparing with shifted stepwise problems.

papers.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

papers.title: Large deviations, optimal trajectories and conservation of momenta in generalised Jackson networks
papers.abstract:
We study properties of optimal trajectories for
  the quasipotential that governs large deviations of queue lengths in generalised Jackson networks (GJN). The trajectories are shown to satisfy Hamilton equations. The Hamiltonian is identified. Optimal trajectories and associated costs are found for networks with two and three stations. A conservation law for adjoint variables
  is discovered to the effect that certain components are maintained along an optimal trajectory. A process is proposed for finding optimal trajectories and computing their costs
  in general GJN.

papers.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
papers.authors: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu, Huaiqing Zuo
papers.abstract: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.

papers.title: A Note on Similarity Classes From Atomic Factorizations in Domains
papers.abstract: We construct an example of a non-Archimedean valued skew field k, with elements a and b of distinct absolute value such that there are no p, q $\in$ k[x] (x a central indeterminate) such that (x -b)(x -a) = pq, p similar to x -a, and q similar to x -b. The obstruction lies in the non-existence of a solution in k to Sylvester's equation at -tb = 1. We also disprove a 1963 result by Cohn (also reproduced in Cohn's 2006 monograph), by constructing a domain with similar elements a and b with a an atom and b not a product of atoms (resp., a product of two atoms, one of them central).

papers.title: On the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un Model for Incompressible Two-Phase Flows with Unmatched Densities: Phase Separation and Rayleigh--Taylor Instability
papers.authors: Fei Jiang, Maoyin Lv, Hao Wu
papers.abstract: Instability phenomena are ubiquitous in multi-fluid flows. For binary fluid mixtures, phase separation may occur under specific conditions, in which a homogeneous state becomes unstable and spontaneously segregates into different phases, leading to the formation of distinct patterns. Furthermore, when a heavier fluid is superposed over a lighter one in a gravitational field, the fluid interface can be sensitive to perturbations that trigger the Rayleigh--Taylor (RT) instability, i.e., the lighter fluid penetrates upward into the heavier fluid against gravity. We investigate such instability phenomena and the inhibiting conditions for incompressible, immiscible two-phase flows with unmatched densities, within the framework of a diffuse-interface model, which is called the Abels--Garcke--Gr\"un (AGG) model. More precisely, we adopt energy methods to establish several stability/instability conditions for the perturbed system of the AGG model, which is obtained by slightly perturbing the equilibrium profile $(\mathbf{0},\overline{\varphi})$, where $\overline{\varphi}=\overline{\varphi}(x_3)$ depends solely on the vertical coordinate $x_3$. Notably, for a constant equilibrium profile $\overline{\varphi}=\alpha\in(-1,1)$ satisfying $\Psi''(\alpha)<0$, we establish a threshold for stability and instability of the phase-separation problem.Similar stability results are also established for the perturbed system with $\overline{\varphi}$ satisfying the RT instability condition in the presence of gravity. In particular, if the phase-separation condition fails and $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$ is a constant, a larger value of $\partial_{x_3}\overline{\varphi}$, a greater interfacial thickness and a higher surface energy density contribute to inhibiting RT instability.

papers.title: Upper bounds on all-terminal reliability polynomials in terms of cycle basis lengths
papers.authors: Tingzeng Wu, Xueqing Li, Jianxuan Luo, Hong-Jian Lai
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V(G),E(G))$ be a connected multigraph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The all-terminal reliability polynomial of $G$ can be written as $R_G(q)=(1-q)^{n-1}\sum\limits_{i=0}^{d}H_iq^i$ where $d=m-n+1$ is the cycle rank, each edge fails independently with probability $q\in[0,1]$, and $H_0,\ldots,H_d$ are the associated coefficients. A cycle basis, which consists of cycles that form a basis of the cycle space of a graph, is an important tool for characterizing its cycle structure. The structural properties of cycle bases, together with the associated length optimization problems and construction algorithms, have been extensively studied. In this context, Colbourn posed the following open problem, which concerns upper bounds on the reliability coefficients in terms of cycle-basis lengths: For all-terminal reliability, is it true that if $G$ has a cycle basis containing cycles of lengths $c_1,\ldots,\allowbreak c_{m-n+1}$, then $H_i \le\sum\limits_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m-n+1\},|I|=i}}\prod\limits_{j\in I}(c_j-1)$? In this paper, we establish a result that resolves this open problem.

papers.title: Unmasking shortcut solutions of coding agents on partial differential equations
papers.abstract: Coding agents now write simulation programs, but benchmarks usually judge only whether their output matches a reference. In manufactured-solution tasks the data determine the exact solution, so a matching output need not come from a solver. We introduce PDEViBench, a benchmark of 290 tasks in six equation families that traces each passing program to the computation behind its output and reruns unclear programs on changed data. A Codex agent (GPT-5.2) passed 80% of 1,450 runs, yet about one pass in ten returned the exact solution without solving the equation. Counting only solved passes changed which task features made problems seem hard and reversed the ranking of two prompts. Once the prompt forbade the shortcut, every pass was a numerical solve, and on tasks without a closed-form solution passing programs stayed correct on changed data. Scientific coding benchmarks should check how each answer was computed as well as whether it matches.

papers.title: Split Kernel Multiplication Modules
papers.abstract: We introduce split kernel multiplication (SKM) modules, for which every submodule has the form $N=IM\oplus\ker f$, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$ and $f$ is an endomorphism of $M$. We study direct sums, localization, and connections with multiplication and retractability properties. For the idempotent version (ISKM), we prove that $R\oplus k^b$ is ISKM over a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, with residue field $k$ and $b\geq1$, if and only if $\mathfrak m^2=0$. We also classify ISKM modules of the form $R^a\oplus k^b$ over local rings. For commutative Noetherian rings, we show that $R^2$ is SKM if and only if $R$ is an Artinian principal ideal ring. Finally, we prove that every finitely generated $R$-module is ISKM if and only if $R$ is a finite product of fields.

papers.title: Lower intermediate dimensions of classical Denjoy minimal sets
papers.abstract: We study the $\theta$-intermediate dimension of the minimal set of the classical $C^{1+\delta}$ Denjoy map, an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of the circle not conjugate to a rigid rotation. This follows on from work of Kra and Schmeling, who showed how the box and Hausdorff dimensions may differ, depending on the Diophantine properties of the rotation number. The $\theta$-intermediate dimension interpolates between these two dimensions. We use the well-understood gap structure of the irrational rotation map to develop a covering strategy to get upper bounds on the lower $\theta$-intermediate dimension, and use results of Banaji to show that these upper bounds are sharp for $\theta$ in an interval.

papers.title: Singular bifurcations in implicit discrete dynamical systems
papers.abstract: A periodic orbit of an implicit discrete system can persist when the implicit function theorem no longer guarantees a smooth successor. We develop a joint Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction of the periodic equations and the determinants marking singular transitions. In unrestricted smooth one-parameter families, the generic event is a single evolution fold on a continued orbit. Simultaneous normal forms describe its interactions with saddle-node and period-doubling bifurcations, locating the singular transitions and, under backward regularity, determining the diverging multipliers. The results cover arbitrary periods and periodically non-autonomous systems. Exact realisations and applications to labour-market equilibrium, machining and implicit integration illustrate the theory.

papers.title: Piercing a Chessboard with Restricted Slopes
papers.abstract: Is it true that for $n\geq 3$, $n-1$ lines are needed to pierce every cell of an $n\times n$ board? This problem was independently rediscovered several times: Alkauskas (1998), Harel-Ackerman-Pinchasi (2012, without claiming the $n-1$ bound), B\'ar\'any-Frankl (2021). However, apparently the first to pose it was T. Keller (Honolulu, Hawaii), in 1980, in the problem section of The American Mathematical Monthly. In this note, we give an affirmative answer to Keller's problem when all lines have slopes in $(-\infty,-1]\cup(0,1]$.

papers.title: Cut Conditions, Integrality, and Obstructions for Directed Multiflows
papers.authors: Srinwanti Debgupta, Martin Skutella, Philipp Warode
papers.abstract:
In contrast to the max-flow/min-cut theorem for single-commodity flows, the cut condition is necessary but not sufficient for the existence of directed multiflows, even with only two commodities. Poremba and Shepherd (IPCO 2023) conjecture that the cut condition is sufficient for all capacities and demands on a directed two-commodity topology if and only if it contains neither of two specific topologies as a relevant minor. We prove this conjecture. As a consequence, the fractional and integral flow-cut gaps of every directed two-commodity topology coincide and are either 1 or 2.
  We then investigate stronger necessary conditions for multiflow feasibility and their implications for integrality. We introduce a hierarchy of five conditions, ranging from the classical cut condition through conditions based on blocking edge sets and binary edge lengths to the linear programming dual characterization of fractional feasibility. The corresponding classes of sufficient topologies are strictly nested. We extend the Nagamochi-Ibaraki theorem: whenever one of the first four conditions is sufficient on a topology, integral capacities and demands satisfying that condition admit an integral multiflow, computable in polynomial time.
