Finally, we prove that recognizing topologies on which any of these four conditions is sufficient is coNP-complete, even for two commodities.

papers.title: Persistence in weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero-Moser derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of invariant weighted Sobolev spaces for the Calogero--Moser derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CMDNLS) equation on the real line. For \(s\geq 1\) and \(0\leq r\leq s\), we first prove that the \(H^s(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the condition \((1+x^2)^{r/2}u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\). The proof uses truncated weighted energy estimates and weighted interpolation. We then establish the persistence of weighted regularity for spatial derivatives. For integers \(p\geq 3\) and \(1\leq m\leq p-2\), and for \(0\leq r\leq p-m \), the \(H^p(\mathbb R)\) flow preserves the conditions \((1+x^2)^{r/2}\partial_x^j u\in L^2(\mathbb R)\) for \(0\leq j\leq m\). This result combines weighted energy estimates, the unitary equivalence and the integrable structure of the CMDNLS equation.

papers.title: A Silverman-Meadows-type criterion for the null controllability of time-dependent coupled heat equations with non-diagonalizable diffusion matrices
papers.authors: Kala Agbo Bidi (XLIM,IMB,IDP), Thibault Liard (XLIM), Pierre Lissy (CERMICS UMR 9032)
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to a uniform spectral Silverman-Meadows rank condition for the nullcontrollability of coupled systems of heat equations with time-dependent diffusion, coupling and control matrices. The proof relies on an adaptation of the Lebeau-Robbiano strategy combined with uniform finite-dimensional observability estimates associated with each Laplace eigenmode.

papers.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
papers.authors: Dae-Won Lee, Masaru Nagaoka, Masatomo Sawahara
papers.abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Sufficient conditions for spanning trees with bounded total excess in tough graphs
papers.authors: Sizhong Zhou, Chunjie Sun, Zhiren Sun
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected graph and $T$ a spanning tree of $G$. The toughness of $G$ is defined by $t(G)=\min\Big\{\frac{|S|}{c(G-S)}:S\subseteq V(G), c(G-S)\geq2\Big\}$ for $G\neq K_n$. A graph $G$ is said to be $t$-tough if $t(G)\geq t$. The size, the adjacency spectral radius and the signless Laplacian spectral radius of $G$ are denoted by $e(G)$, $\rho(G)$ and $q(G)$, respectively. The $k$-excess of a vertex $v$ in $T$ is defined as $\max\{0,d_T(v)-k\}$. The total $k$-excess $\mbox{te}(T,k)$ is defined by $\mbox{te}(T,k)=\sum\limits_{v\in V(T)}{\max\{0,d_T(v)-k\}}$. A tree $T$ is called a $k$-tree if $d_T(v)\leq k$ for every $v\in V(T)$, namely, the maximum degree of a $k$-tree is at most $k$. It is obvious that $T$ is a spanning $k$-tree if and only if $\mbox{te}(T,k)=0$. This paper investigates a generalization of spanning $k$-trees using a concept called total $k$-excess and puts forward three lower bounds based on $e(G)$, $\rho(G)$ and $q(G)$ in a connected $\frac{k}{k(k-2)+b+3}$-tough graph $G$ to guarantee that $G$ has a spanning tree $T$ with $\mbox{te}(T,k)\leq b$, where $k\geq3$ and $b\geq0$ are two integers. As corollaries, we obtain three sufficient conditions for a connected $\frac{k}{k(k-2)+3}$-tough graph to has a spanning $k$-tree.

papers.title: Edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--\v{S}ir\'{a}\v{n} graphs $H_q$ for every prime power $q\geq 3$
papers.abstract: Motivated by Hamilton cycle problems and applications to collective communication, we study edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in the McKay--Miller--\v{S}ir\'{a}\v{n} (MMS) graphs. The MMS graph $H_q$ (indexed by a prime power $q$) is a highly symmetric graph arising from finite fields. For every prime power $q\geq 3$, we prove that the MMS graph $H_q$ contains $\big\lceil\frac{q-1}{2}\big\rceil$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles. This resolves a problem of Li, Wang and Zheng, who established the result for prime $q$ and for $q=4$. Our construction uses graph lifts over finite fields and joins the components of lifted Hamilton cycles by adding edges within vertex fibres. The resulting cycles can be constructed using $O(|E(H_q)|)$ finite field operations, comparisons, and elementary list operations. As an application, these cycles provide edge-disjoint spanning rings for parallel ring-all-reduce algorithms on MMS networks.

papers.title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.

papers.title: Induced packing treewidth III. Branch decompositions
papers.abstract:
The notion of induced packing treewidth aims to unify classes defined by forbidden induced subgraphs or induced minors with classes defined by the existence of certain structured tree decompositions.
  In this paper, we introduce induced packing branchwidth, a branch-decomposition analogue of induced packing treewidth. For a graph $H$, the induced $H$-packing branchwidth of a graph $G$, denoted by $\branchpi_H(G)$, is the minimum, over all branch decompositions of $G$, of the largest number of pairwise anticomplete induced copies of $H$ that cross one displayed cut. For $H=P_2$, it equals sim-width. We prove several structural properties of graphs of bounded $\branchpi_H$, for various choices of $H$, including $\chi$-boundedness, polynomial degree-boundedness, and metric properties.

papers.title: Avoiding short progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory II
papers.authors: Hei Chun Leung, Chi Hoi Yip
papers.abstract:
Recently, Currier, Moore, and Yip developed a general framework for constructing colorings avoiding prescribed monochromatic arithmetic progressions in Euclidean Ramsey theory. Writing $\ell_m$ for an $m$-term arithmetic progression with unit spacing, they proved $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\ell_{20})$ and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{6889})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We refine and simplify their framework, proving $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{22})$ for every $\alpha>0$. We further establish $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{21})$ except possibly for four values of $\alpha^2$, and $\mathbb E^n
ot	o(\ell_3,\alpha\ell_{17})$ for all but finitely many $\alpha>0$. Our approach also recovers several earlier results and avoids some technical arguments used in previous works.

papers.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
papers.abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.

papers.title: Reconstructing Flash-Evoked Potentials in the Human Brain and Tracking Cortical Activity Using Spatiotemporal Filtering: Numerical Simulation Study
papers.authors: Qiong Tao, Joonas Lahtinen, Sampsa Pursiainen
papers.abstract: Electroencephalographic source reconstruction of visual evoked activity is challenging because distributed, temporally evolving, and overlapping cortical sources generate scalp potentials. We present a controlled simulation framework for flash visual evoked potentials (FVEPs) based on a coupled Jansen--Rit neural mass network and a realistic finite-element EEG forward model. The framework generates a sequential activation pattern across early visual, parietal, and frontal regions and enables direct comparison of reconstructed activity with known ground truth. Standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), change-rate SKF (CrSKF), conventional Kalman filtering (KF), and linearly constrained minimum variance (LCMV) beamforming are compared using parcel-wise time courses, temporal lags, and assessments of spatial focality and Earth Mover's Distance. In the inverse comparison, SKF and CrSKF preserve the principal temporal progression more consistently than KF and LCMV, while CrSKF produces smoother temporal estimates. The results also demonstrate parcel-wise leakage and reduced separation of closely spaced components, emphasizing the need to interpret temporal ordering together with spatial reconstruction quality. The proposed framework provides a reproducible test environment for evaluating dynamic EEG inverse methods under controlled noise conditions.

papers.title: Vector metrics with values in pre-Riesz spaces I: transfer of order convergence along vector lattice covers
papers.abstract: Vector metric spaces in the sense of \c{C}evik and Altun take values in a vector lattice, but their axioms use only the order of the value space. We develop the theory for vector metrics with values in an Archimedean pre-Riesz space $E$, i.e.\ an ordered vector space admitting a bipositive order dense embedding $i$ into a vector lattice $Y$. We ask when an $E$-valued vector metric $d$ and the vector-lattice-valued metric $i\circ d$ have the same convergent and Cauchy nets and sequences. Relatively uniform convergence transfers along every cover. For nets, $\mathrm{o}_3$-convergence transfers if and only if the cover has an intrinsic domination property. This property holds for pervasive covers, by a result of Kalauch and van Gaans, for uniformly dense covers and in finite dimensions; it fails for an example of Kalauch and van Gaans. Sequential convergence transfers under a countable domination property implied by uniform density, but not under pervasiveness. For uncountable $\Gamma$, the vector lattice $\mathbb{R}\mathbf 1\oplus c_{00}(\Gamma)$ is pervasive in its Dedekind completion $\ell^\infty(\Gamma)$ without the transfer, while for countable $\Gamma$ the transfer holds; the difference is explained by order separability. In finite dimensions, with a closed generating cone, all these convergences coincide with norm convergence in every cover. For $C^1[0,1]$-valued integral metrics, positivity of the kernel on the diagonal forces all order convergences to coincide with $L^1$-convergence. For the Volterra kernel $(t-s)_+$, by contrast, $L^1$-convergence, relatively uniform convergence and order convergence are pairwise different, and we describe each explicitly.

papers.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

papers.title: Orbits along primes in totally minimal systems
papers.authors: Wen Huang, Song Shao, Hui Xu, Xiangdong Ye
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show that every totally minimal system admits a point whose orbit along the primes is dense. Moreover, assuming the Dickson-Hardy-Littlewood conjecture, we show that in any totally minimal distal system, the orbit along the primes of every point is dense.

papers.title: Linear disjointness and values of Mahler M-functions
papers.abstract: We prove that the algebra generated by the values of Mahler M-functions at algebraic points admits a decomposition as the tensor product, over Q, of a countable family of linearly disjoint algebras. Consequently, the study of linear and algebraic relations among such values reduces to the corresponding problem within each of these smaller algebras. Our proof relies on recent advances of the authors on Mahler's method in several variables. As an application, we obtain a complete description of the algebraic relations among the values of the Fredholm series and their derivatives at nonzero algebraic points. This fully resolves an old problem originating in Mahler's work.

papers.title: Singularities in leaf closures on complex surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove a geometric and dynamical criterion excluding minimal sets contained in the regular locus of a holomorphic foliation on a compact complex surface. In particular, we prove that every Jouanolou foliation of degree at least two has no exceptional minimal set. We also give an explicit lower bound, growing linearly with the degree, for the number of singularities in every regular leaf closure of a Jouanolou foliation. This bound persists under small perturbations, as does the existence of a nonempty open saturated set whose leaves accumulate at all singularities. Under finite pullback unramified over the singular set, the bound is multiplied by the degree of the normalised component over the base leaf. Together with a general persistence theorem, this yields nonempty analytic open sets of foliations on every smooth projective surface with arbitrarily large uniform lower bounds on the number of singularities in their regular leaf closures. On double-plane K3 surfaces, we obtain foliations with ample canonical bundle and explicitly describe and count their singularities.

papers.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
papers.authors: Vladimiro Benedetti (UniCA,LJAD), Daniele Faenzi (UBE,IMB), Simone Marchesi (UB)
papers.abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

papers.title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
papers.authors: Chongying Dong, Kaiwen Sun, Haowu Wang
papers.abstract: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.

papers.title: Positive solutions of power equations in planar corner domains
papers.authors: Hongtao Hu, Zhouyu Long, Hongzhe Tao, Qiaoran Wu, Wenming Zou
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of $\Delta u=\lambda u^k$ on bounded planar corner domains with zero boundary values away from the vertex. For negative-power absorption we identify the admissible interval of Martin masses and prove uniqueness at the minimum mass. Along the ordinary boundary, we identify the weak Hessian endpoint and its sharp tail when the set of zero inward derivative has positive length. For superlinear sources we prove attainment of the largest positive Martin mass in the subcritical range. At criticality we construct a family of singular solutions with zero Martin mass and distinguish its members by their second logarithmic coefficient and the endpoint integrability of their Hessian differences. Above criticality an angular eigenvalue governs the Morse index away from its zero threshold. We also give sharp physical-Hessian asymptotics for finite-mass remainders and joint corner and side estimates for negative-power sources.

papers.title: An Algebraic Foundation of Rate-Product Style Quantity Calculus
papers.abstract: Using the new notion of a scalable (right) monoid-heap, the quantity calculus in [1] is generalized to include quantities that may not be possible to multiply as well as both (weak) rates and products of quantities. Several examples are given of applications in metrology and physics

papers.title: Nontrivial Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function and Its Derivative
papers.authors: Chuancun Yin, Xianghua Zhao, Zuolu Hao, Zhongyang Sun
papers.abstract: The nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function lie at the heart of analytic number theory. Through the explicit formulas, they govern the distribution of prime numbers: the closer all nontrivial zeros lie to the critical line $\Re(s)=\frac12$, the more uniformly the primes are distributed. The Riemann Hypothesis-asserting that all nontrivial zeros satisfy $\Re(s)=\frac12$-is equivalent to the optimal error bound $O(\sqrt{x}\log x)$ in the Prime Number Theorem. Beyond number theory, the zeros of $\zeta(s)$ and its derivative $\zeta'(s)$ are deeply intertwined: the horizontal distribution of $\zeta'$-zeros near the critical line encodes information about the spacing of consecutive $\zeta$-zeros. This paper establishes some results concerning the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
papers.abstract:
We study the mixing time of Glauber dynamics for sampling uniformly from the proper $q$-colorings of sparse Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi random graphs $G(n,d/n)$. Our main result establishes that with probability $1-o(1)$ over the draw of $G$, Glauber dynamics is rapidly mixing for every $q\geq d+d^{1/2+\varepsilon}$, given any fixed $0<\varepsilon\leq1/2$ and any sufficiently large fixed $d$. In particular, the surplus of colors above $d$ is sublinear and close to $\sqrt{d}$. The achieved color range therefore approaches the tree uniqueness threshold and improves over the previously best achievable number of colors $q > 1.763 d$ due to Efthymiou, Hayes, Stefankovic, and Vigoda [SODA 2018]. Moreover, our mixing-time bound is $O(n^{2+o_d(1)})$, and hence almost quadratic as $d\rightarrow\infty$.
  Our proof is based on establishing a spectral gap for block dynamics resulting from a suitable decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ into blocks and singleton vertices, ensuring that every high-degree vertex is encapsulated within a block. Our main technical contribution is a novel way of establishing rapid mixing of block dynamics via an integrated Bochner-Bakry-\'{E}mery approach, which we expect to have applications beyond sampling colorings. We further devise a new block decomposition of $G(n,d/n)$ that strengthens and simplifies similar constructions used in previous work. Finally, to compare block and Glauber dynamics, we establish a novel recursive separator decomposition of tree-like blocks, together with a coupling argument that avoids the need for nearly uniform color marginals at vertices adjacent to hubs. This comparison argument might be of independent interest.

papers.title: Total variation error bounds for Schr\"odinger-F\"ollmer samplers
papers.abstract: Sampling from high-dimensional, multimodal target distributions plays a fundamental role in scientific computing, statistics and machine learning. Recently, the Schr\"odinger-F\"ollmer sampler (SFS) has been proposed by Huang et al. (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, 2025) as an efficient sampling algorithm that transports the degenerate distribution at $t=0$ to the target distribution at $t=1$, without relying on long-time ergodicity. In this paper, we establish non-asymptotic error bounds for SFS in the total variation distance by deriving regularization estimates for the associated Kolmogorov equation via the Bismut-Elworthy-Li formula. When the drift can be computed exactly, a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|)$ was obtained under certain smoothness conditions on the drift with a uniform time step-size $h>0$. When the drift is approximated by Monte Carlo methods, we obtain a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}( h|\ln h|+ 1/M)$, where $M$ is the number of samples used in the Monte Carlo approximation. This yields a sharper dependence on $M$ than the existing bound $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{M})$ in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance in the aforementioned paper, by turning the total variation error to the weak error analysis in the setting of non-smooth test functions. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the convergence rate with respect to the time step-size $h$ and the Monte Carlo sample size $M$ and the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

papers.title: Unique continuation property for $\bar\partial$ with $L^{2n}$ potentials
papers.authors: Guokuan Shao, Ziming Shi, Jujie Wu
papers.abstract:
We establish the sharp unique continuation property for the Cauchy--Riemann operator $\bar{\partial}$ in higher dimensions. Let $0\in\Omega \subset \C^n$ be a domain. Suppose $u \in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,2}(\Omega; \C^N)$ satisfies the differential inequality
  \[
  |\bar{\partial} u| \leq V |u| \quad \text{a.e.~on } \Omega
  \]
  with $V \in L_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2n}(\Omega)$. If $u$ is $L^2$ flat at the origin, then $u \equiv 0$ on $\Omega$.

papers.title: $\lambda_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
papers.authors: Renzo Cavalieri, David Klompenhouwer, Paolo Rossi
papers.abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $\lambda_g\psi^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

papers.title: A proof of the Theta conjecture
papers.authors: Haojun Bai, Feng Gu, Zhuowei Lin, Dun Qiu, Minhao Zhang
papers.abstract: We prove the touching refinement of the Theta conjecture of Interdonato and Iraci, giving a formula for $\Theta_{e_\ell}\Theta_{e_k}\nabla E_{d,j}$ as a weighted sum over parking functions with decorated rises and valleys and touch number $j$. Summing over $j$ gives the Theta conjecture. As corollaries, we prove the valley Delta conjecture of Haglund, Remmel, and Wilson and its generalized version proposed by Qiu and Wilson. Our proof compares algebraic and combinatorial recurrences using an extension of the plethystic substitution $X\mapsto(q-1)X$ to quasisymmetric functions. The algebraic recurrence follows from an endomorphism constructed by D'Adderio, Interdonato, Iraci and Pagaria on the Dyck path algebra of Carlsson and Mellit. The combinatorial recurrence is obtained by introducing signed labels and deleting the main diagonal. The two recurrences have the same initial conditions, which identifies the corresponding generating functions.

papers.title: Exact local spectral thresholds for loose and tight Hamilton cycles in $3$-graphs
papers.abstract: For an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph $H$, let $\sigma(H)$ denote the minimum adjacency spectral radius of its vertex links. We determine the exact thresholds for $\sigma(H)$ that force loose and tight Hamilton cycles for all sufficiently large admissible orders, and give constructions showing that each bound is best possible. The loose threshold is $(1+\sqrt{13})n/8+O(1)$, with two forms according to $n$ modulo four. The tight threshold is $2n/3+O(1)$, with four forms determined by $n$ modulo three and, when $3\mid n$, modulo nine. The resulting spectral conditions and the corresponding minimum vertex degree conditions do not imply one another. For loose cycles, we combine fractional packing stability and absorption with exact completion near a space barrier. For tight cycles, spectral stability and rooted sampling reduce the problem to three extremal configurations. We resolve these configurations by controlling the spectral loss caused by missing triples and constructing short paths that extend to Hamilton cycles, including in the presence of exceptional vertices.

papers.title: A capillary logarithmic Gauss curvature flow and the capillary Minkowski problem
papers.abstract: We study a logarithmic Gauss curvature flow of strictly convex capillary hypersurfaces in the Euclidean half-space. For an acute contact angle and an arbitrary positive smooth prescribed function, we prove that a suitable initial dilation yields a global solution which converges smoothly after a horizontal translation with a uniquely determined constant velocity. As an application, we provide a logarithmic flow proof of the capillary Minkowski problem, previously established by Mei-Wang-Weng [Adv. Math. 469, 110230 (2025)].

papers.title: The symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric problem in the plane
papers.abstract: We resolve the symmetric Gaussian isoperimetric conjecture in the plane: every minimizer of Gaussian perimeter among centrally symmetric sets of prescribed Gaussian measure is a centered ball, a symmetric strip, or the complement of one of these sets. A quadrant-reflection argument reduces the problem to unconditional sets. The planar structural results of Barchiesi, Cagnetti and Julin then leave only a noncircular strictly convex stationary oval. We exclude this oval by an explicit volume-preserving and perimeter-decreasing linear deformation, which geometrically corresponds to an "unconditional squeezing". More generally, without requiring any symmetry assumptions, we show that any noncircular closed embedded $\lambda$-self-shrinker is always unstable via linear deformations. We also record a reduction to the unconditional case in dimension three, using an orthogonal equipartition theorem of Musin.

papers.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
papers.abstract:
We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $\phi$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $\phi$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses.
  Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $\phi$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Bor\r{u}vka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

papers.title: VEM-bubble discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for a fluid induced seismicity model with rate-and-state friction
papers.authors: El Hadi Zerga, Roland Masson, Jean-Paul Ampuero, Pierre Romanet
papers.abstract: This work addresses the discretisation and iterative coupling algorithm for an induced seismicity model accounting for fault reactivation and slip driven by subsurface fluid injection. The model couples single-phase Darcy flow in both the porous matrix and the fault network with a quasi-static poroelastic mechanical response in the bulk and fault slip governed by a rate-and-state friction law with radiation damping stabilisation leading to a quas-dynamic formulation. The contact mechanics problem is discretised using the Virtual Element Method with bubble stabilisation of the facewise constant Lagrange multiplier. It is combined with a Hybrid Finite Volume scheme for the mixed-dimensional Darcy flow model. The time discretisation is implicit and the nonlinear system is solved at each time step using an iterative coupling algorithm which iterates between the Darcy flow, the frictional contact-mechanics, and the state differential equation. The contraction of this iterative coupling algorithm is established with a smallness assumption on the time step independent on the mesh size. This proves convergence of the fixed-point as well as well-posedness of the system. The frictional contact-mechanical model is solved using a semi-smooth Newton algorithm based on a local nonlinear inversion of the friction rate-and-state law and a block Gauss--Seidel preconditioner exploiting the structure of the VEM-bubble-$\mathbb{P}^0$ mixed discretisation.

papers.title: An almost sharp tomas-stein restriction theorem for a class of anisotropic operators
papers.abstract: Let $d\geq 2$. For each $j\in \{1,\dots,d\}$, let ${\ell}_{j}\geq 1$ and $m_{j}\geq 2$ be integers, and let $a_{j}$ be a nonzero real number. We prove that the oscillatory integral operator \begin{equation*} T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f(x):=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} e^{\dot{\imath} \left(a_{1}x^{{\ell}_{1}}_{1}y^{m_{1}}_{1}+\dots +a_{d}x^{{\ell}_{d}}_{d}y^{m_{d}}_{d} \right)}f(y)dy,\;\;\; x\in \mathbb{R}^{d}, \end{equation*} satisfies the restriction estimate \begin{equation*} \|T_{{\ell}_{1},\dots,{\ell}_{d},m_{1},\dots,m_{d}}f\|_{L^{2}(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})}\lesssim \|f\|_{L^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})}, \end{equation*} for each $1\leq p\leq 2$, whenever $(\frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}-\frac{1}{m_{j}}+1)\frac{2}{p^{\prime}}\geq 1$, for every $j\in \Gamma$, and \begin{equation*} \mathcal{E}:=\min{\left\{\min_{1\leq j\leq d}{\frac{m_{j}}{{\ell}_{j}}},\,\min_{1\leq k\leq d}{\frac{d-1}{\sum_{j\neq k} \frac{\ell_{j}}{m_{j}}+\frac{2}{m_{k}}}}\right\}}> \frac{2}{p^{\prime}}. \end{equation*} We also give counterexamples that show that the condition $\mathcal{E}\geq 2/p^{\prime}$ is necessary for this restriction inequality.

papers.title: An asymptotic formula for primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$
papers.authors: Yujiao Jiang, Yuk-Kam Lau, Guangshi L\"u
papers.abstract:
We prove Motohashi's conjecture on primes of the form $u^2+v^2+1$, with Iwaniec's corrected constant. Let $b$ denote the characteristic function of the positive integers representable as a sum of two squares. Then, as $x\to\infty$, \[
  \sum_{p\le x}b(p-1)
  =\kappa\Spr\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}}
  +O\!\left(\frac{x}{(\log x)^{3/2}\sqrt{\log\log x}}\right), \] where $\kappa$ is the Landau--Ramanujan constant and $\Spr=\prod_{p\equiv3\,({\rm mod}\,4)}\bigl(1-1/(p(p-1))\bigr)$. The proof combines auxiliary prime factors with a mean square estimate for bilinear sums. We obtain the minor arc bound through harmonic switching and high moments, replacing arithmetic divisibility conditions by independent projective lines. We remove the auxiliary weights using Selberg's sieve.

papers.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
papers.abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.

papers.title: The full length of short pants
papers.abstract: Bers proved that any genus $g$ hyperbolic surface admits a pants decomposition of length bounded above by a function of its genus. The goal here is to provide an explicit upper bound for the sums of lengths which is on the order of $(g \log(g)) ^{3/2}$.

papers.title: Reference-Dependent Utility Optimization for Goal-Oriented Communication Systems
papers.authors: Symeon Vaidanis, Photios A. Stavrou, Marios Kountouris
papers.abstract: Traditional communication resource allocation optimizes operational metrics such as rate, latency, energy efficiency, and reliability. Motivated by goal-oriented semantic communication, we develop a generalized allocation framework that transforms operational rewards through reference-dependent user utilities and evaluates them via expected utility, cumulative prospect theory (CPT), or related decision criteria. The formulation separates operational rewards, user-side valuations, and system-level decision criteria under uncertainty. We characterize utilities incorporating QoS/service reference levels, deficit sensitivity, post-reference saturation, and loss aversion. Weighted sum-reward maximization, proportional fairness, $\alpha$-fairness, and stochastic expected utility maximization emerge as exact special cases, while soft QoS-aware allocation follows from a deficit-penalty generalization. For deterministic orthogonal systems, we derive utility-weighted marginal-reward KKT conditions characterizing global optimality under concave composite objectives. For nonorthogonal and stochastic systems, we develop successive convex approximation (SCA) algorithms and establish stationary-point guarantees under explicit smooth and composite nonsmooth assumptions, including a CPT branch-stationarity result under eventual nondegenerate ordering identification. For globally solved penalized problems, we derive an $O(1/\lambda)$ bound on excess aggregate soft-QoS deficit, and on the deficit itself whenever a QoS-feasible allocation exists. Additionally, we establish an $O(1/\epsilon^2)$ outer iteration bound for the smooth fixed-step SCA best-response residual. Numerical examples demonstrate how reference points, marginal utility slopes, channel quality, and resource budgets influence active users and allocation policies.

papers.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
papers.abstract: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

papers.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
papers.abstract: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $\beta=(\beta_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_\beta$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_i\beta_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $\beta_i$ on each block. Here $n_\beta$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.

papers.title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
papers.abstract:
We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant.
  The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.

papers.title: On definable closure in closed $H$-fields
papers.authors: Matthias Aschenbrenner, Lou van den Dries, Joris van der Hoeven
papers.abstract: The definable closure of a real closed $H$-field $H$ in an ambient closed $H$-field extension $M$ is shown to be an immediate extension of $H$, except in two very special cases, where this is only true after adjunction to $H$ of a particular $H$-definable element of $M$ and then taking the real closure in $M$.

papers.title: Quantitative stability of classical, entropic, and doubly entropic Wasserstein barycenters
papers.authors: Guillaume Carlier, Julien Gu\'erin, Quentin M\'erigot
papers.abstract: In this paper, we show how the recent analysis of (sharp) strong convexity properties of the Kantorovich functional by the third author can be used to establish new global quantitative stability estimates for Wasserstein barycenters and their entropic regularizations with respect to perturbations of the population distribution. For classical Wasserstein barycenters, we improve the state-of-the-art H\"older continuity exponent with respect to the $\mathcal{W}_1$ metric from $1/6$ to $1/4$, while drastically weakening the assumptions on the population distribution. We also provide an example which shows that the exponent $1/4$ cannot be improved. Motivated by computational considerations, we also analyze regularizations of Wasserstein barycenters with \emph{outer} and \emph{inner} entropic penalizations. For outer entropic barycenters, we establish novel higher-order stability results and in particular give a quantitative bound on relative Fisher information. Another contribution of our paper is a strong convexity estimate for an entropic version of the Kantorovich functional via soft Legendre transforms, enabling us to extend our stability results to \emph{doubly} entropic barycenters, as introduced by Chizat.

papers.title: Fixed-occurrence cases of the shuffle-word-embedding conjecture
papers.abstract: For self-adjoint contractions in a finite tracial von Neumann algebra, binary shuffle traces with $m=1,2,4$ occurrences of the second variable admit simultaneous finite-dimensional approximation by commuting diagonal contractions. For every odd $m$, a commuting diagonal self-adjoint pair reproduces any prescribed finite set of shuffle traces exactly. When the first operator has finite spectrum and $m\geq3$ is odd, a weighted symmetric cycle reproduces all degrees simultaneously. We prove fourth-order trace-derivative positivity in finite tracial von Neumann algebras and obtain a positive measure representing the four-occurrence coefficients. For each even $m$, we characterize the contraction model property by positivity of an associated trace-derivative functional.

papers.title: Dynamic Topological Completeness for $\mathbb R^2$
papers.abstract:
Dynamic topological logic (${\bf DTL}$) combines topological and temporal modalities to express asymptotic properties of dynamic systems on topological spaces. A dynamic topological model is a triple $\left <X,f,V\right >$, where $X$ is a topological space, $f:X\to X$ a continuous function and $V$ a truth valuation assigning subsets of $X$ to propositional variables. Valid formulas are those that are true in every model, independently of $X$ or $f$. A natural problem that arises is to identify the logics obtained on familiar spaces, such as $\mathbb R^n$. Slavnov showed that any satisfiable formula could be satisfied in some $\mathbb R^n$ for $n$ large enough, but the question of how the logic varies with $n$ remained open.
  In this paper we prove that any fragment of ${\bf DTL}$ that is complete for locally finite Kripke frames is complete for $\mathbb R^2$. This includes ${\bf DTL}^\bigcirc$; it also includes some larger fragments, such as ${\bf DTL_1}$, where ``henceforth" may not appear in the scope of a topological operator. We show that satisfiability of any formula of our language in a locally finite Kripke frame implies satisfiability in $\mathbb R^2$ by constructing continuous, open maps from the plane into arbitrary locally finite Kripke frames, which give us a type of bisimulation. We also show that the results cannot be extended to arbitrary formulas of ${\bf DTL}$ by exhibiting a formula which is valid in $\mathbb R^2$ but not in arbitrary topological spaces.

papers.title: Horizontal estimates for Kloosterman sums under Hecke eigenvalue constraints
papers.abstract: We prove weighted cancellation under small-value conditions on Hecke eigenvalues of finitely many non-CM holomorphic newforms. We also obtain many squarefree integers of each sign with fixed normalized amplitude, simultaneously small Hecke eigenvalues, and a fixed bound on the number of prime factors, uniformly in growing reduced residue classes. Our questions are motivated by Xi's noncorrelation conjectures and the mixed-moment estimates of Jiang and Lau. Their estimates imply that small Hecke eigenvalues can occur together with non-small Kloosterman values. Our result retains this property with a fixed prime-factor bound, both signs, and the residue conditions. Using OpenAI's zero-free half-plane theorem for Dirichlet $L$-functions, we give an example with at most $83$ prime factors, normalized amplitude at least $10^{-21}$, and moduli $M\le C^{11/200}$.

papers.title: Vanishing Control Times for Single-Input Bilinear Quantum Systems under Rapid Drift Spectral Growth
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the asymptotic behavior, as the Hilbert space dimension tends to infinity, of the state-to-state control time of single-input bilinear quantum systems whose control operator is drawn from an isotropic (unitarily invariant) random ensemble. Relying on deterministic graph-theoretic bounds, namely star cuts of the interaction graph for the lower bound and spanning trees for the upper bound, and on integration over the Haar measure, we derive high-probability lower and upper bounds on the control time, expressed in terms of the empirical spectral variance and of the relative concentration of the drift spectrum. Whenever the spectrum grows fast enough (for instance polynomially with an exponent larger than 3/2, geometrically, or super-exponentially), the upper bound vanishes and the control time tends to zero in probability: in these cases, enlarging the Hilbert space constructively speeds up control.

papers.title: Preference-Based Constraint Handling for Multi-Objective Design-Decision Optimisation: Acceptability Relaxation and Feasibility Guidance
papers.authors: E. Ozer, A. R. M. Wolfert
papers.abstract: Multi-objective design-decision optimisation (MODO) problems contain negotiable acceptability limits and non-negotiable feasibility constraints. Hard constraints define the feasible design space, whereas actors may reconsider acceptability limits through deliberation and compromise. Relaxing such limits is a preference judgement: penalties or violation measures do not necessarily represent how actors value departures from initial requirements. This paper introduces a preference-based constraint-handling framework. For negotiable limits, preference functions model how actor preference changes with relaxation, allowing the preferred design and acceptable degree of relaxation to be determined through the same aggregation process. Approach 1 represents relaxation as an additional objective and search variable; Approach 2 incorporates it into the preference function of the affected criterion. When constructed consistently, both yield the same best-fit-for-common-purpose solution but differ in complexity and computational effort. The framework addresses stalemate problems, where relaxation is required to recover an acceptable solution, and non-stalemate problems, where modest relaxation may reveal a better design. Hard feasibility constraints remain fixed, and infeasible designs remain inadmissible. A feasibility-guidance function supplies IMAP-IGS with graded information on scaled violations, guiding the search towards difficult-to-reach feasible regions. Every feasible design takes precedence over every infeasible design, and the final recommendation is selected exclusively from the feasible set through A-FINE preference aggregation. The framework integrates acceptability negotiation, feasibility guidance, and design optimisation without conflating their meanings, while preserving preference consistency and decision validity.

papers.title: Projections between Ramsey quasi-orders and topological Ramsey spaces
papers.abstract: A Ramsey quasi-order is a quasi-order $(\cal{R},\leq)$ such that $\cal{R}$ is a Polish space, $\leq$ is analytic and every analytic subset of $\cal{R}$ is Ramsey. In this paper, we study the transfer of the analytic Ramsey property via monotone quasi-open maps, which are closely related to a family of forcing projections between quasi-orders (ranging from weak projections to strong projections). We apply this framework to the class of topological Ramsey spaces by providing a detailed list of examples of strong projections between topological Ramsey spaces, and show that, for many of these examples, there is no weak projection in the reverse direction. We also exhibit pairs of topological Ramsey spaces that do not weakly project into each other. Finally, partially confirming a conjecture of Dobrinen, we show that every space in a large class of topological Ramsey spaces either strongly projects into the Ellentuck space or contains a dense set of atoms.

papers.title: An approximation for solutions to Helmholtz equation in polygons and its application in learning based numerical method
papers.abstract: A learning based method for Helmholtz equations was proposed in [J. Comput. Phys. 520:113478,2025]. Based on Runge's approximation, it can be proved that when the solution can be continued outside the computational domain, using fundamental solutions as learning samples is sufficient to obtain the solution mapping with spectral accuracy. However, for complex geometries, such as domains with corners, approximation by fundamental solutions may only have logarithmic convergence due to the regularity issue, which is computationally impracticable. Moreover, approximation of a solution to the elliptic equation with those on larger domains is an ill-posed problem. In this work, we investigate how to feed additional learning samples to essentially get a practicable convergence rate and a stable algorithm, so as to ensure the generalizability of the learning based method. Error analysis and numerical examples illustrate flexibility and high-accuracy features.

papers.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

papers.title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
papers.abstract: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Pad\'e methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.

papers.title: Linear Functional Estimation under Multiplicative Measurement Error with Unknown Error Distribution
papers.abstract: In this work we consider i.i.d. observations from a multiplicative deconvolution model, i.e. generated by $Y= X\varepsilon$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent strictly positive random variables. The goal is to statistically infer the unknown signal $X$. Starting from the scenario where the probability density $f_\varepsilon$ of the error is known, we revisit local estimation strategies for several quantities of interest including the probability density function f and the survival function $S^X$ of the signal $X$. We use these results to propose a thresholded plug-in estimation technique for linear functionals in situations where the distribution of the error $\varepsilon$ is unknown, while having some additional data at our disposal. This estimation procedure combines the reconstruction of the unknown Mellin transform of $f$ as well as its regularized inversion by a spectral cut-off. We establish oracle-type upper bounds and discuss rates of convergence in explicit scenarios including estimating $f$ and $S^X$ pointwise. In addition, we develop a fully data-driven choice of the cut-off parameter via model selection, which is able to obtain the oracle risk up to a constant without any previous knowledge of the error distribution. The results are illustrated in a simulation experiment, where we compare different classes of distributions in settings with known and unknown $f_\varepsilon$.

papers.title: The space of Dimension functions on a $C^*$-algebra
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the space of normalized dimension functions on a unital $C^*$-algebra is either empty or a Choquet simplex. As a byproduct, we show that $W(A)$ is hereditary in $\operatorname{Cu}(A)$ for every $C^*$-algebra $A$. The argument combines an exact factorization for Cuntz comparison with Birkhoff's decomposition of lattice valuations. Moreover, we show that the space of normalized rank functions on a unital ring is either empty or a Choquet simplex.

papers.title: Chv\'atal's Toughness Conjecture for Dense Almost Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: Chv\'atal's toughness conjecture asserts that there is a constant $t_0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian. Most partial results on this conjecture concern graphs with a restricted structure, such as chordal graphs and $H$-free graphs for small linear forests $H$. We confirm the conjecture with $t_0=4$ for dense almost regular graphs, without any structural assumption: for every $\alpha>0$, there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $n_0$ such that every $4$-tough graph $G$ on $n\ge n_0$ vertices with $\delta(G)\ge\alpha n$ and $\Delta(G)-\delta(G)\le\varepsilon n$ is Hamiltonian. This result also bears on a conjecture of Bollob\'as and, independently, H\"aggkvist from the 1970s that every $k$-connected $D$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $D\ge n/(k+1)$ is Hamiltonian. This conjecture is false for every $k\ge4$, even for large $n$. Our result shows that its conclusion holds for all large $n$ when $k$-connectivity is replaced by $4$-toughness, and that the degree condition can then be weakened to $D\ge\alpha n$ for an arbitrarily small fixed $\alpha>0$. We also construct $3/2$-tough regular non-Hamiltonian graphs of linear degree, showing that the constant $4$ cannot be replaced by $3/2$.

papers.title: Rationally Null-homologous Floer Simple Knot
papers.abstract: We prove that every rationally null-homologous Floer simple knot in a closed, oriented, irreducible three-manifold with nonzero Thurston norm is unknotted. The proof combines a cut-and-reglue comparison for extremal Floer groups with Binns's theorem on Floer-minimal knots in balanced sutured manifolds.

papers.title: Existence of a non-zero steady-state solution to a population density equation subject to horizontal transfer
papers.abstract: From plasmid dynamics and efflux pump expression in bacteria to risk-taking behaviour in human groups, horizontal interactions can drive the transmission of deleterious traits that spread despite carrying no selective advantage, thereby burdening the population. How can such detrimental traits persist, and under what conditions can the population avoid extinction?  To address these questions, we model a population structured by a continuous trait representing individual burden within a non-linear, non-local integro-differential framework. From an analytical perspective, mutations are modeled via a jump operator rather than a diffusion term; consequently, the mutation operator lacks regularizing properties and is generally non-self-adjoint. Moreover, working in a weighted L 1 setting precludes the direct application of standard Krein-Rutman theory. To overcome these hurdles, we construct a custom fixed-point operator by first freezing the non-linearities to solve an auxiliary eigenvalue problem, and then tuning the resulting principal eigenvalue. Applying the Leray-Schauder fixed-point theorem to this operator rigorously yields the existence of a non-trivial steady state. Finally, numerical simulations illustrate the qualitative dynamics of the model and delineate the parameter regimes governing population persistence and extinction.

papers.title: Probabilistic counting of labelled trees with prescribed vertical edge profile
papers.abstract: The vertical edge profile of a labelled plane tree $t$ is the collection of integers counting the number of oriented edges from label $i$ to label $j$ for every possible pairs of labels $(i, j)$. In a previous work by the second author, it was shown that a process constructed from the vertical edge profile forms a Markov chain for a wide class of models of random labelled plane trees where edge label increments are constrained to lie in $\{-1, 0, 1\}$. The purpose of this paper is twofold. First, we continue the study of Markov properties of the vertical edge profile. In particular, we derive general formulas for the transition kernel and the initial distribution of a class of Markov chains related to the vertical edge profile. Second, we apply these results to the probabilistic enumeration of trees with a prescribed vertical edge profile. These applications yield a unified probabilistic derivation of several enumeration formulas. In particular, we recover some results established Bousquet-M\'elou and Chapuy for binary trees and Cayley trees. These enumeration formulas admit a remarkable factorized form, already noted in previous works. The probabilistic methods developed here explain this phenomenon by showing that these factorizations arise naturally from the Markov structure underlying the vertical edge profile.

papers.title: Ternary quadratic genera and generalized Hurwitz class numbers via quaternion orders
papers.authors: Yifan Luo, Tianze Wang, Haigang Zhou
papers.abstract: We classify the genera of primitive positive definite ternary quadratic forms in the extremal cases of Lehman's level and discriminant conditions. The genera are parametrized by their level, discriminant, and genus conductor, which also distinguishes local forms having the same isotropy. Using the correspondence with quaternion orders of level $(N_1,N_2)$, we express their weighted representation numbers and class numbers in terms of generalized modified Hurwitz class numbers. The formulas allow arbitrary admissible prime power exponents and include the additional genera obtained by Watson's transformation. As an application, we determine all $255$ one-class genera in these families and give an explicit representation formula for each. Of these formulas, $110$ concern nonsquarefree $N_1N_2$.

papers.title: Exponential mixing for the randomized two-vortex model
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the mixing of passive scalars advected by a randomized two-vortex model on $\mathbb{T}^2$, in which the vortices interact through a regularized Biot--Savart kernel and are driven by independent Brownian motions. We establish quenched exponential mixing for the Lagrangian flow, characterized by the exponential correlation decay of mean-zero $H^s$ observables. The proof proceeds by establishing ergodicity of the associated two-point Markov process. We combine a uniform contraction estimate with controllability arguments to verify the Lyapunov drift and minorization conditions, allowing us to apply Harris-type theorem.

papers.title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
papers.abstract:
We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$.
  Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits hexagons. For the central simple examples in which all root spaces are non-zero, we determine which ones are Tits-hexagonalizable; in certain cases, this imposes an additional balancing condition on the idempotent.

papers.title: Independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions over rings of Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: We study linear and algebraic independence of Hasse--Weil $L$-functions of abelian varieties over $\mathbb{Q}$, with Dirichlet series as coefficients. For nonzero varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, we prove that their $L$-functions with arbitrary Dirichlet twists, together with all their derivatives and $1$, are linearly independent when the coefficient series use only primes from a set of natural density zero. For untwisted $L$-functions, this independence is equivalent to the condition that the varieties are pairwise non-isogenous over $\mathbb{Q}$. If the individual monodromy groups are connected, the result for varieties that are pairwise non-isogenous over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ extends to larger coefficient rings: the prime supports of coefficients are unrestricted outside a prescribed set of positive upper natural density and meet it in a set of natural density zero. We also characterize algebraic independence of untwisted $L$-functions in terms of the multiplicities of the simple isogeny factors of the varieties. The proofs combine an arithmetic-function lemma of Kaczorowski--Molteni--Perelli with Frobenius density arguments and require no analytic continuation or automorphy.

papers.title: Investigating parameter dependence for counterexamples to Payne's nodal line conjecture using HPC
papers.abstract: The behavior of the nodal line of the second eigenfunction of the negative Laplacian has been widely studied. Dahne could show numerically for one domain with six holes in two dimensions that it is possible to reject Payne's nodal line conjecture. We investigate the behavior of the nodal line if it does not touch the boundary, specifically the general shape, its prediction, its dependence on the parameters, and the numbers of holes. In this paper, we could address these issues numerically with a very efficient parallelized algorithm showing the rejection for various domains with six and five holes.

papers.title: Learning inexact alternating minimization for convex problems with quadratic coupling
papers.authors: Paul H\"ausner, Jevgenija Rudzusika, Jens Sj\"olund, Ozan \"Oktem
papers.abstract: Alternating minimization is a standard tool for optimization problems with two coupled variable blocks. Its cost is dominated by the inner subproblem solvers, which rarely have a closed-form solution. In this paper, we propose to learn an inexact alternating scheme in which neural networks approximate the subproblem solution at each iteration. For convex problems with quadratic couplings between the variable blocks that satisfy a quadratic growth condition, we derive a worst-case bound on the optimality gap that exposes the per-iteration error that each network is trained to minimize in a greedy fashion. Combining the bound with a PAC-Bayes argument, we obtain a fixed-horizon, high-probability bound on the expected optimality gap over the distribution of problem instances. We apply the learned scheme to robust matrix completion and low-dose CT reconstruction with dictionary regularization where we achieve a 5x-13x speedup over the inexact first-order baseline at matched accuracy. A brief end-to-end fine-tuning stage extends this up to 30x and outperforms other learned schemes. The code is available at https://github.com/paulhausner/learned-alternating-minimization.

papers.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
papers.abstract: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.

papers.title: A Strict Upper Bound for Three-Point Weighted Selection in Planar Vector-Valued Regression
papers.abstract: We prove $F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$ for minimum-Frobenius-norm least-squares regression with two input and two output coordinates, improving the upper bound $15/8$. More precisely, a universal $\varepsilon_0>0$ satisfies $\mathcal T_3\le(5/6-\varepsilon_0)E$ for every finite residual frame. The proof combines an exact scalar certificate, rigidity of equality in planar selection, and a compactness argument that controls disappearing weights. Together with the known lower bound, this gives $13/8\le F_{\mathrm{weighted}}(2,2,3)<11/6$. No numerical value of $\varepsilon_0$ is claimed.

papers.title: Single-point determination of a potential and a nonlinearity in a semilinear biharmonic equation
papers.authors: Song-Ren Fu, Li Li, Hongyu Liu, Zhikun Zhang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the inverse problem of determining the coefficient $q$ and the nonlinearity $F$ in the semilinear biharmonic equation $\Delta^2 u+q(x)u=F(x,u)$ with Navier boundary data. The measurement consists of $\partial_\nu u(x_0)$ at a fixed boundary point $x_0$. We apply the mixed variation approach to linearize the nonlinear problem and construct semiclassical boundary-localized solutions for the linearized equation. Under suitable analyticity, nonresonance, and nondegeneracy assumptions on $q$ and $F$, we prove that this boundary point measurement uniquely determines both $q$ and $F$. We also establish boundary determination of all normal derivatives of $q$ and of the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of $F$ on a nonempty relatively open subset of the boundary. When the linear potential $q$ is known, we prove that either component of the Navier boundary input alone suffices to determine $F$, and that the polynomial nonlinearity can be uniquely determined without requiring any analyticity conditions. For suitable finite-dimensional classes of nonanalytic potentials, we also obtain, for fixed $F$, the stable determination of $q$ from finitely many boundary inputs and the associated point measurements. In addition, as an important supplement, we provide nontrivial examples verifying the main assumptions, as well as counterexamples concerning the recovery of the linear coefficient. Finally, we present numerical experiments that demonstrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Optimal Actuator Support Design for Infinite-Horizon Linear-Quadratic Parabolic Control Problems
papers.abstract: We study an optimal actuator design problem for infinite-horizon LQ control problems governed by parabolic equations. The control acts only on a small measurable subregion of the spatial domain, and the objective combines the infinite-horizon control value with a cost for the actuator region. Using the Riccati representation of the value function, we derive a comparison identity for two actuator supports and obtain an exact expansion of the objective. This leads to a topological derivative with respect to local changes in the support. We prove a localized Riccati sensitivity estimate to control the remainder and show that the infinite-horizon term in the derivative can be computed by solving a Lyapunov equation. This yields a computable support-update algorithm with a measure-controlled Armijo search. Under explicit uniform remainder and admissibility assumptions, its first-order stationarity defect tends to zero. Numerical experiments illustrate these results.

papers.title: Gelfand and sampling numbers of weighted Wiener spaces
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to establish sharp asymptotic bounds on the Gelfand numbers of weighted Wiener spaces $\mathcal{A}^r_\theta$ measured in $L_q$. This is done by using results for Gelfand numbers of sequence spaces and applying them to each layer of a hyperbolic cross to obtain results for Gelfand numbers between different (weighted) Wiener spaces. These can then be used to establish bounds in $L_q$ by combining them with known results and techniques for Besov spaces. This significantly narrows a gap in the current research, since the Gelfand numbers provide a lower bound on the (non-linear) sampling numbers, whereas upper bounds on this quantity have been studied in multiple papers via an upper bound given by the best m-term approximation.

papers.title: Completely monotone memory systems
papers.abstract: Linear time-invariant (LTI) relaxation systems are characterized by a completely monotone impulse response. This paper proposes an extension of this property to nonlinear systems: a system is said to have completely monotone memory if a positive increment in the past input leads to a completely monotone increment in the future output. We show that this property constitutes a strong form of monotonicity, while also imposing stability constraints that closely resemble fading memory, contraction, and incremental stability. We also show that completely monotone memory is equivalent to classical relaxation for LTI systems and to a combination of monotonicity and stability for a class of scalar state-affine systems. Finally, we illustrate the relevance of our framework to the gating dynamics of conductance-based models.

papers.title: Differential Flatness of Nonlinear Consensus Networks: A Graph-Theoretic Perspective
papers.abstract: We study the property of differential flatness for networks of identical flat agents coupled through a consensus protocol, where a single exogenous input acts on one agent and the output of another agent is measured. We distinguish whether the network admits a flat output at all from whether the measured task output is a flat output. For the former, we show that flatness at a synchronized equilibrium requires controllability of the Laplacian leader--follower pair, which is also sufficient for linear agents but not for nonlinear ones. For the latter, we show that the relative degree of the task output is determined by its graph distance to the input node, so that it is a flat output if and only if the graph is a path with the input and output nodes at its ends. Numerical examples illustrate how flatness enables finite-time transitions between consensus configurations through a single input.

papers.title: Monetisation and Cost Function Scalarisation Cannot Guarantee Valid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making
papers.abstract:
Monetary quantities are not preferences. Cost is an object-related system performance; value-for-money is an actor's subjective evaluation of it. Monetisation embeds trade-off information: its conversion coefficients express valuations and determine how heterogeneous performances compensate one another. Cost-benefit analysis, even net present value, yields quantities of money, not the preference value actors attribute to them.
  This creates a monetisation paradox. Cost enters a multi-criteria problem as one performance among several, but money is then elevated into the universal representation of all others, creating representational dominance. The problem collapses into a single-criterion one in which every performance acts only through its imposed monetary equivalent. Cost-function scalarisation does not resolve this by substituting points, normalised scores, losses, or penalties: these transformations and their weights fix preference directions, intensities, and trade-offs, so they are implicit preference models, yet are treated as technical constructs rather than measured and validated.
  A well-defined scalar optimum is therefore not necessarily a decision-valid multi-criteria outcome. Numerical commensurability does not establish preference commensurability. Decision validity requires heterogeneous performances to be transformed into actor preferences in a unified preference domain. Preference is relational and contextual, yet can be represented on an affine scale. Preference Function Modelling and the Linear Preference Space provide the commensurability required for valid aggregation. The decision criterion should thus maximise aggregated actor preference over the feasible and acceptable design-decision space, not monetised quantities or scalarised scores.

papers.title: Exact codegree Tur\'an densities of even zycles
papers.abstract: We determine the exact codegree Tur\'an density of the $3$-uniform zycle $Z_\ell$ for every even integer $\ell\ge 8$ with $3\nmid\ell$,showing that $\gamma(Z_\ell)=1/3$. More generally, we prove that $\gamma(Z_\ell)\le 1/3$ for all even $\ell\ge 8$. Our results partially answer a question of Piga and Sch\"ulke [Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. 58 (2026), e70348] concerning the sharpness of their upper bound of $1/2$.

papers.title: Interface-Preserving ${H}_\infty$ Model Reduction of Network Systems
papers.abstract: We study projection-based reduced-order models that exactly retain specified input and output interfaces. Admissible projections are characterized geometrically: the retained subspace must contain every input and output direction, which fixes the minimum order. The reduction error factors into input-coupling, internal-dynamics, and output-coupling systems, giving a submultiplicative ${H}_\infty$ bound; for positively dominated factors the ${H}_\infty$ error equals a dc gain computable from linear solves. Strict dissipativity certifies the stability of every orthogonal reduction, and a Hankel singular value bounds the optimum a posteriori. These results motivate sequential graph-coarsening heuristics for networks. On a 65,566-state chip thermal network, interface-preserving coarsening yields sparse, positive lumped models that are more accurate than Kron reduction of the same interface at every order, with far fewer edges; balanced truncation is more accurate but destroys the network structure.

papers.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
papers.abstract: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for fine meshes with at least 512 elements has a proof checked by Lean 4. Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.

papers.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
papers.abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial.
