In the unforced case the solution is smooth at positive times. The qualitative argument adapts the resonant-averaging framework for rapidly rotating fluids to the different odd-viscous dispersion. Weighted lattice counts and signed corrected-energy estimates yield a sufficient bound for the odd-to-ordinary viscosity ratio that is polynomial in the normalized initial-data radius at each fixed normalized force radius, together with a separate bound in a specified force-dominated regime. No optimality is claimed for the polynomial exponents or prefactors; determining the sharp viscosity threshold for the original equation remains open. Direct kinetic and weighted enstrophy barriers also give regularity for every coefficient on explicit bounded data and force regions, including the closed unforced ball of homogeneous second-order Fourier Sobolev radius ninety-seven fortieths times the viscosity and seven closed forced rectangles. We specify how finite certificates enter the analytic argument and distinguish minimization of a sufficient formula from sharpness for the original equation. All three main theorems are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: Motivic Mirror Symmetry for Sink-recurrent Cluster Varieties
papers.abstract: We prove motivic mirror symmetry for full-rank sink-recurrent cluster varieties. We allow skew-symmetrizable principal parts and invert all frozen variables. The rational geometric motive of such a variety is isomorphic to the additive orbifold motive of the mirror stack of Hu and Shende. This gives comparisons of cohomology, higher Chow groups, and algebraic $K$-theory with rational coefficients. The proof combines quantum deformation with the splitting of these motives into Tate summands. For really full-rank skew-symmetric seeds, a finite \'{e}tale morphism realizes the comparison. We also study this geometric comparison in families over the projective line.

papers.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
papers.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We replace doubling, the usual hypothesis for landmark embeddings, by admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{\tau t}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers instead of generators fails: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

papers.title: A complete symmetric rank-two modularity classification, obtained through a sharp uniform degree bound
papers.abstract:
We classify modular Nahm sums with a rational symmetric positive-definite two-by-two matrix and rational shifts. Up to coordinate exchange, every modular datum belongs to three explicit rational-point families, is a product of two modular rank-one sums, or is one of thirty-four exceptional triples on twelve matrices. The list consists of Zagier's rank-two examples, the Vlasenko--Zwegers additions and split products; no further data occur. The proof first bounds the joint degree of the distinguished Nahm point by four, using an initial degree bound of twenty-four and exact local exclusions at the prime 7. Explicit height and exponent bounds then give exhaustive arithmetic classifications in degrees one through four. Exact polynomial elimination determines all rational shifts, and published identities of q-series establish modularity of the survivors. The degree bound is sharp. The finite steps are accompanied by exact certificates, verification programs and independently implemented checks.
  Computational companion: https://github.com/johnngy44/math/releases

papers.title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
papers.abstract: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,\delta_B,\epsilon_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $\delta_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $\epsilon_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $\iota_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,\delta_{O_q},\epsilon_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $\delta_{O_q}$ (resp. $\iota_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $\epsilon_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $\delta_{O_q}$ and $\iota_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Prze\'zdziecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.

papers.title: Legendre manifolds generated by the Barenblatt equations
papers.abstract: The paper is devoted to the construction of exact general solutions of the equations of oil filtration in a porous medium under the action of an active reagent injected into the reservoir. The choice of the reagent solution determines the control process of chemical oil flooding in hard-to-recover fields. The problem is described by a system of two first-order nonlinear partial differential equations (the Barenblatt model). Conditions are found on the Buckley--Leverett function, the adsorption function, and the distribution function of the reagent in oil under which the original system, by means of a nonlinear change of variables on a five-dimensional manifold endowed with a contact structure, is reduced to a linear wave system with constant coefficients. Six families of such functions are indicated. For them, contact transformations and Legendre surfaces corresponding to general solutions in implicit form are constructed.

papers.title: Efficient Kernelized Learning in Polyhedral Games Beyond Full-Information: From Colonel Blotto to Congestion Games
papers.authors: Andreas Kontogiannis, Vasilis Pollatos, Gabriele Farina, Panayotis Mertikopoulos, Ioannis Panageas
papers.abstract: We examine the problem of efficiently learning coarse correlated equilibria (CCE) in polyhedral games, that is, normal-form games with an exponentially large number of actions per player and an underlying combinatorial structure. Prominent examples of such games are the classical Colonel Blotto and congestion games. To achieve computational efficiency, the learning algorithms must exhibit regret and per-iteration complexity that scale polylogarithmically in the size of the players' action sets. This challenge has recently been addressed in the full-information setting, primarily through the use of kernelization. However, in the case of the realistic, but mathematically challenging, partial-information setting, existing approaches result in suboptimal and impractical runtime complexity to learn CCE. We tackle this limitation by building a framework based on the kernelization paradigm. We apply this framework to prominent examples of polyhedral games -- namely the Colonel Blotto, graphic matroid and network congestion games -- and provide computationally efficient payoff-based learning algorithms, which significantly improve upon prior works in terms of the runtime for learning CCE in these settings.

papers.title: Efficient Swap Regret Minimization in Combinatorial Bandits
papers.authors: Andreas Kontogiannis, Vasilis Pollatos, Panayotis Mertikopoulos, Ioannis Panageas
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of designing efficient no-swap regret algorithms for combinatorial bandits, where the number of actions $N$ is exponentially large in the dimensionality of the problem. In this setting, designing efficient no-swap regret translates to sublinear -- in horizon $T$ -- swap regret with polylogarithmic dependence on $N$. In contrast to the weaker notion of external regret minimization - a problem which is fairly well understood in the literature - achieving no-swap regret with a polylogarithmic dependence on $N$ has remained elusive in combinatorial bandits. Our paper resolves this challenge, by introducing a no-swap-regret learning algorithm with regret that scales polylogarithmically in $N$ and is tight for the class of combinatorial bandits. To ground our results, we also demonstrate how to implement the proposed algorithm efficiently -- that is, with a per-iteration complexity that also scales polylogarithmically in $N$ -- across a wide range of well-studied applications.

papers.title: Generalized Edge Ideals and Regularity Offset of Graphs
papers.authors: Grigoriy Blekherman, Jiaheng Li, Jianuo Zhou
papers.abstract: We introduce generalized edge ideals by assigning pairwise coprime monomials, instead of variables, to the vertices of a graph. We use the lcm-lattice to show that the multigraded Betti numbers and Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the quotient by a generalized edge ideal agree with the Betti numbers and resolution regularity of the quotient by an ordinary edge ideal in a non-standard Z-grading. We define the regularity offset as a measurement of the difference between the regularities of the quotients by a generalized edge ideal and its ordinary counterpart, and prove bounds for the regularity offset. We compute the regularity offset for co-chordal graphs and paths, and derive a formula for the regularity offset of forests. We also derive a graph-theoretic criterion for when a forest's regularity offset is always zero, or equivalently, its top-level Betti number is nonzero.

papers.title: Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials
papers.abstract: Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach \`a la Skolem, that for a root $\alpha\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(\alpha)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.

papers.title: Simply connected quotients of fake quadrics
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a short introduction to their arithmetic construction, aimed at low-dimensional topologists, and studies their holomorphic and antiholomorphic quotients and their fundamental groups. The running example in the paper comes from a quaternion algebra over a totally real cubic field. The lattice is generated by three explicit pairs of matrices. A holomorphic involution gives (after resolving the singularities) a simply connected minimal complex surface of general type with $p_g=0$ and $K^2=4$, a smooth $4$-manifold homeomorphic but non-diffeomorphic to $CP^2$ blown up $5$ times. An antiholomorphic involution gives a smooth four-manifold homeomorphic to $S^4$, with a knotted torus as branch locus.

papers.title: Fresh Enough to Decide: Age of Intelligence for Cost-Aware Model Synchronization in Dynamic IoT Systems
papers.authors: Hui Wang, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Jacob Chakareski, Ming Shi
papers.abstract: Resource-constrained IoT devices cache learned models for real-time decisions, but frequent updates incur substantial bandwidth, energy, and service overhead. Because decision-relevant model differences need not grow with elapsed time, we define Age of Intelligence (AoInt) as a model-version-relative, client-specific, and action utility distortion, and formulate synchronization as a tradeoff between stale-decision regret and refresh cost. Furthermore, we develop Kullback-Leibler-aware AoInt Synchronization (KL-AoIntSync), which accumulates output-distribution changes using client-specific unlabeled probes, whereas Parameter-aware AoInt Synchronization (Param-AoIntSync) uses a server-broadcast scalar parameter change. Then, we establish pathwise guarantees with fixed client distributions, action sets, and utilities. The numerical results show that calibrated Param-AoIntSync reduces joint synchronization cost by 6.15% relative to an Instant-Parameters policy while performing comparably to KL-AoIntSync.

papers.title: Topology and Information in Regularized Transport on Graphs
papers.abstract: We study how two geometries of mass on a finite graph interact: the information geometry of the generalized entropy $F_q$ used for regularized transport, and the arithmetic of divisors governed by the Riemann--Roch theorem of Baker and Norine and by the Jacobian. Because the correction term of $F_q$ is affine, $F_q$-regularization at strength $\gamma$ is Tsallis regularization at temperature $\gamma/q$. Over the reals, chip-firing connects all configurations of equal degree, so the Jacobian enters transport only through integrality. We introduce the transport defect, the worst-case cost of steering $d$ chips towards a target by chip-firing, and prove $1/d\le\delta_{\TV}(D)\le(d-r(D))/d=(g-1-r(K-D))/d\le\min(1,g/d)$ whenever $g\ge1$; vertex multiplicities give a lower bound and an equality criterion. A regularized topological gap $\Gamma_{q,\gamma}(D,E)$ tends to the chip-move defect as $\gamma\to0$, lies in an explicit window, has a high-temperature slope given by Tsallis coupling entropies, and admits a positive regime if and only if $g\ge1$. Dual potentials certify exactly the convex relaxation of a linear system; the remainder is an integrality gap. Zeros in optimal plans occur only for $q>1$, by a mechanism different from the sign change of $\Gamma$. Exact computations on $1784$ divisor classes find the rank bound $(d-r(D))/d$ attained in $1769$ of them, an observed frequency. Experiments on honeycomb and Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi networks with $10^2$ to $10^5$ nodes test the statements on regularized plans, not $\Gamma$; over $10^3\le n\le10^5$ their transport costs are consistent with growth like $n^{1/2}$ and $\log n$, respectively.

papers.title: Preconditioned Implicit Midpoint Langevin Sampling for Non-Smooth Bayesian Imaging
papers.abstract: We introduce P-IMLA, a preconditioned implicit-midpoint Langevin sampler for high-dimensional log-concave targets with non-smooth regularization. The obstruction is that the large steps enabled by matrix preconditioning are precisely where preconditioned Euler-Maruyama inflates stationary variance. Implicit midpoint removes this surplus via a Cayley-transform identity, making P-IMLA Gaussian-exact at any step size. Beyond Gaussians, whitening transfers the sharp IMLA contraction rate to $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and backward-error analysis gives drift-only rather than Euler-type diffusion bias under explicit smoothness assumptions. An $M$-norm Moreau envelope yields a proximal non-smooth variant with a three-term error budget. Controlled Gaussian and TV-regularized imaging experiments confirm the predicted separation: the unpreconditioned midpoint scheme retains long transients as $\kappa_f$ grows, whereas P-IMLA remains $\kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}$-governed and near variance-exact.

papers.title: Memory flows: geometry and dynamics of sequential retrieval in input-driven Hopfield networks
papers.authors: Simone Betteti, Matteo Martin, Morten Gram Pedersen, Sandro Zampieri, Giacomo Baggio
papers.abstract: Associative memory models classically describe retrieval as convergence to stored patterns, but the theory of sequential retrieval remains comparatively limited. We develop a two-timescale input-driven Hopfield network in which fast associative retrieval is modulated by a slow feedback variable evolving over a prescribed memory-transition graph. This yields autonomous, graph-constrained transitions while preserving analytical tractability. Using slow-fast and geometric singular perturbation theory, we characterize memory fixation via memory manifolds and identify the geometric regions that govern stability loss and escape from retrieved memories. We further derive reduced slow dynamics and explicit criteria for transition onset, self-sustained retrieval, and collapse, expressed through escape times, gain thresholds, and fixed points. Together, these results provide a tractable framework for analyzing feedback-driven sequential retrieval in Hopfield networks.

papers.title: A Free-Field Realization of Boundary Symmetries in Discrete Jackiw--Teitelboim Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate a finite-periodic Miura free-field realization of the classical Virasoro--dilaton sector relevant to sl(2,R) Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Starting from a single logarithmic Cartan field, we use the established discrete Miura map and its free-field Poisson bracket to construct the lattice spin-two current. The dilaton is then realized as a periodic composite of the same Cartan variables, selected by an inhomogeneous difference equation and its monodromy condition. This construction yields an explicit induced mixed Poisson bracket without postulating an independent dilaton bracket. We examine the associated transfer problem and quadratic adjoint invariant, and test the finite Fourier algebra against the continuous Virasoro--dilaton transformation, in which the dilaton has conformal weight minus one. The construction supplies a free-field counterpart of the JT boundary transformation laws; it does not by itself identify the Miura Poisson structure with the canonical BF boundary-charge algebra.

papers.title: Integrable AdS$_2$ branes in mixed flux AdS$_3$
papers.abstract: We show that half-BPS D3-branes wrapping AdS$_2\times$S$^2$ in AdS$_3\times$S$^3\times$T$^4$ with mixed NSNS and RR flux define integrable boundary conditions for the supercoset sigma model of the Green--Schwarz superstring. This extends the integrable D-branes of Dekel and Oz to backgrounds with a Wess--Zumino term, and previous bosonic results for mixed flux to the full superstring. Using the D3-brane action, we find that the electric and magnetic worldvolume fields that stabilise the branes at generic positions are obtained from those of the AdS$_2\times$S$^2$ branes of the WZW model by the same $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ rotation that maps the pure NSNS background to the mixed flux one, acting on the D3-brane as electric--magnetic duality. On the worldsheet, cancelling the fermionic boundary terms requires introducing a specific closed two-form in the boundary action, and its contribution to the bosonic boundary conditions reproduces precisely these worldvolume fields. We then construct field-dependent reflection matrices that lift the boundary conditions to gluing conditions for the Cagnazzo--Zarembo Lax connection and describe displacements along geodesics normal to the brane. The resulting double-row monodromy matrix generates infinitely many conserved charges, which establishes the classical integrability of the open superstring for any mixture of fluxes. In AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, these branes are expected to be dual to conformal interfaces in a deformation of the symmetric product orbifold of T$^4$.

papers.title: BiMuon: A Geometry-Aware Stochastic Bilevel Optimization Approach
papers.authors: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu
papers.abstract: Stochastic bilevel optimization provides a general framework for many machine learning applications, such as hyperparameter learning, data reweighting, language model alignment, and actor-critic reinforcement learning. However, most existing bilevel optimization methods treat matrix-valued gradients as flattened vectors and perform optimization in the resulting vectorized space, ignoring the matrix structures common in modern neural networks. Moreover, the lower-level (LL) problem curvature can induce significant spectral imbalance in the upper-level (UL) geometry. Such limitations of existing bilevel optimization methods motivate us to develop BiMuon, a geometry-aware stochastic bilevel optimization method that integrates implicit hypergradient estimation in bilevel optimization with Muon-style orthogonalized updates at the UL. To our knowledge, BiMuon is the first stochastic BLO method with Muon-style orthogonalized matrix updates and an $O(\epsilon^{-4})$ iteration-complexity guarantee, matching the best-known rates achieved by Muon-type methods based on matrix parameterizations. To improve computational and parallel efficiency for models with multiple matrix parameters, we further study BiMuon for blockwise diagonal matrix approximation and derive a relative stepsize allocation rule based on UL progress and blockwise LL sensitivity. We evaluate BiMuon on representation learning and blockwise bilevel optimization, providing empirical support for our methods.

papers.title: DisMUSE: An Efficient Distributed Singular-Spectrum-Based Optimization Approach with Theoretical Convergence Guarantee
papers.authors: Zhen Qin, Zhiyao Zhang, Yingbin Liang, Jia Liu
papers.abstract: In recent years, singular-spectrum-based optimizers have attracted increasing attention due to their ability to preserve the matrix structure of neural network gradients, thereby enabling geometry-aware optimization. However, most singular-spectrum-based (SSB) approaches remain centralized, limiting their use in distributed learning infrastructures that exploit massive parallelism. Distributed SSB optimization is still at an early stage, with open questions about convergence guarantees and communication efficiency. To fill this gap, we propose the Distributed Momentum-based Spectral Estimator (DisMUSE), an efficient distributed SSB optimization framework for both data-center and federated settings. Using Muon-style exact orthogonalized momentum as the spectral update, DisMUSE integrates a recursive variance-reduced momentum estimator and achieves an $O((KT)^{-1/3})$ convergence rate, where $K$ and $T$ denote the number of nodes and local iterations per node, respectively. This rate matches the best-known rates for variance-reduced nonconvex distributed optimization. Building on this variance-reduced framework, we study two extensions. First, our DisMUSE method with finite Newton-Schulz (NS) iterations preserves the same convergence order under a uniform normalized support-spectrum condition, up to a multiplicative factor. Second, we develop a communication-efficient variant based on low-rank (LR) momentum transmission and quantify the error it introduces to the stationarity bound, characterizing the trade-off between accuracy and communication cost.

papers.title: Turing Instability of a Closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus Model
papers.authors: Xiangye Xu, Sue Ann Campbell, Francis J. Poulin
papers.abstract:
We study Turing instability in a closed Nutrient-Phytoplankton-Zooplankton-Detritus (NPZD) ecosystem model with nutrient recycling, formulated as a reaction-diffusion system without an explicit time-delay. The detritus compartment represents the biomass during the recycling process and acts to introduce a time delay in this process. Total biomass in the system is conserved, leading to a closed model.
  Although spatial diffusion typically promotes stability, our focus is on understanding how different diffusion rates for different species can destabilize steady states and give rise to spatial patterns. To address this, we first perform linear stability analysis to identify conditions under which Turing instability may occur. We then validate these theoretical predictions through numerical simulations. Our approach develops both intuition and rigorous analysis of how diffusion influences instabilities in the context of a conservative system, offering a comprehensive framework for understanding pattern formation in multi-species plankton ecosystems.

papers.title: Lower-Level Agnostic Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Peiwen Qiu, Prashant Khanduri, Jia Liu
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization is a fundamental framework for machine learning problems, where an upper-level (UL) objective depends on the solution of a nested lower-level (LL) problem. Existing bilevel algorithms typically assume that the LL objective is available for evaluation, differentiation, or unrolling. However, this assumption can fail when the LL response is produced by a black-box solver, simulator, adversary, or learned predictor. In this paper, we study LL agnostic bilevel optimization, where the UL learner has access only to an approximate LL solution $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ and cannot query the LL objective, its gradients, Hessian/Jacobian information, or the procedure that generates the LL response. We propose LeGo-BiO, a coordinate-wise pseudo-hypergradient method that estimates the missing Jacobian $\nabla _{\mathbf{x}}\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\mathbf{x})$ using finite differences of $\bar{\mathbf{y}}(\cdot)$. For each UL coordinate, LeGo-BiO constructs a decision vector subject to 1-sparse updates, thereby isolating the corresponding Jacobian column needed in the UL gradient computation. This avoids the directional-projection limitation of full-parameter response differences and, unlike derivative-free/zeroth-order approximations of the entire UL gradient, preserves the available first-order gradient information with respect to the UL variables for more accurate UL gradient evaluation. We establish convergence guarantees for LeGo-BiO in both deterministic and stochastic settings under an LL error-bound/Polyak-Lojasiewicz-type condition, without requiring LL strong convexity. Our bounds yield an $O(T^{-1})$ rate in the deterministic setting and an $O(T^{-1/2})$ rate in the stochastic setting when the LL approximation error decreases geometrically. Experiments demonstrate competitive performance of LeGo-BiO despite being agnostic to the LL objective.

papers.title: Testing CCZ-equivalence to permutations via projections of Walsh zero spaces, with applications to APN functions
papers.abstract: Whether almost perfect nonlinear (APN) permutations exist in even dimension $n\ge 8$ is a long-standing open question, the big APN problem. The only example known in even dimension, on six bits, was found from a quadratic APN function that is not itself a permutation, by Carlet--Charpin--Zinoviev (CCZ) equivalence. It is therefore natural to test APN functions for CCZ-equivalence to a permutation. This amounts to finding two complementary $n$-dimensional subspaces among the zeros of the Walsh transform, which lie in $\mathbb{F}_2^{2n}$. A known necessary condition only uses their projections to $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and cannot decide every case. We give an exact test for functions whose Walsh supports are affine, including all quadratic functions. It reconstructs the subspaces from their projections, through searches for subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ and for constrained bilinear maps. On the benchmarked functions in dimension twelve, it lists them $39$ to $55$ times faster than the generic search of the commonly used sboxU library. We then study the functions $x^3+a^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}(a^3x^9)$, which G\"olo\u{g}lu and Pavl\r{u} proved not to be CCZ-equivalent to permutations when $4$ divides $n$. With their result, our computations show that this holds for every even $n\le 24$. In dimension $18$ the necessary condition is satisfied, and the new test decides the case. We conjecture this for every even dimension. We also compile $25$ classes of quadratic APN functions in dimension ten from published instances, with equivalence certificates. No function in these classes or in their switching closure is CCZ-equivalent to a permutation. All code and data are public.

papers.title: Mobility Information Capacity of Multi-Robot Systems: Safety-Aware Maneuver Design
papers.abstract: Multiple robots operating in shared workspaces must adjust their speed, direction, and trajectories to coordinate with one another and respond to changing tasks and disturbances. The available maneuver freedom depends on the dynamics, uncertainty, and safety margins, even for a fixed fleet size and workspace. However, robot count, workspace occupancy, and task throughput do not quantify how much the fleet can vary its motion or how reliably these variations can be observed. We develop a mobility information capacity (MIC) framework that jointly characterizes these two aspects. Mobility information is defined as the mutual information between a joint maneuver sequence and its noisy trajectory observation, and MIC maximizes this quantity under maneuver-resource constraints. For a linear Gaussian maneuver-to-observation model with feedback dynamics, we characterize the finite-horizon information benchmark and derive its stationary long-horizon spectral limit, accounting for heterogeneous mobility gains, colored uncertainty, and temporally coupled maneuver costs. We further map workspace-boundary, inter-robot separation, and actuator chance constraints into coupled maneuver-covariance restrictions and derive conditions under which covariance optimization reduces to resource allocation across mobility modes. Finite joint maneuver codebooks are then constructed through individual risk screening and noise-whitened trajectory separation, with bounds linking sequence recovery error and achieved information to the capacity benchmarks. An aerial-robot simulation study evaluates spectral convergence, safety-aware allocation, finite-codebook identification, and fleet-size scaling. The resulting framework complements occupancy and task-throughput measures by quantifying the maximum observable maneuver freedom supported by a mobility system.

papers.title: Simulating Nonlinear Resistive Networks using a Behavioral Splitting
papers.authors: Ryan Alizadeh, Thomas Chaffey, Dominic Liao-McPherson, Alberto Padoan
papers.abstract: An operator splitting method is developed for computing operating points of nonlinear resistive networks. Our behavioral formulation separates the device laws from Kirchhoff's laws and casts simulation as a zero-finding problem. Branch port resistances then provide a diagonal preconditioner for the relaxed Peaceman-Rachford iteration in scattering variables. Each iteration requires solving independent scalar equations and a linear system with a fixed weighted Laplacian matrix. Convergence is established for maximal monotone device laws when an operating point exists. Contractive branch reflections also yield a linear convergence bound independent of network topology. Numerical experiments on crossbar arrays illustrate the computational advantages.

papers.title: Sharp Logarithmic-Product Bounds for List Replicability of Sign Matrices
papers.abstract: List replicability measures how many accurate hypotheses suffice to contain the output of a learning rule with arbitrarily high confidence. We prove that every nonempty class of $m$ binary concepts on $n$ domain points has list replicability at most $805\ln(2m)\ln(2n)$. This resolves the logarithmic-product conjecture of Blondal, Hatami, Hatami, Lalov, and Tretiak. Hanner matrices give lower bounds of the same order, for square matrices and for explicit families with unequal logarithmic aspect ratios. The upper bound is obtained by constructing nested acyclic sets in the faces of a cube. A critical-point estimate supplies highly connected regions, weighted cell attachments keep the sets compatible across faces, and a cubical carrier theorem converts them into accurate finite covers and learning rules. Appending one constant coordinate turns list replicability into an exact geometric quantity, the face width, and graph-orientation classes satisfy exact product formulas. In particular, there are explicit classes with list replicability $4k+1$ and equivariant index $3k$, so the additive gap between the two is unbounded. We also develop entropy-tilting and two-sided Gibbs constructions, give combinatorial upper bounds adapted to structured matrices, compute exact values on classical families, and study the index of Paley matrices.

papers.title: Lower Bounds Above $\sqrt{3}$ for Online Makespan Minimization on Four Identical Machines
papers.abstract:
For deterministic online makespan minimization, $m = 4$ identical machines is the smallest case whose optimal competitive ratio is open: it is known only to lie between $\sqrt{3} \approx 1.73205$ and $26/15 \approx 1.73333$. We prove a lower bound of $14383/8304 \approx 1.73206$ using a single branching layer, and refine the construction with a second, mirrored branching layer to obtain $14350/8283 \approx 1.73246$, closing about a third of the gap.
  Our constructions are the first branching adversaries for $m = 4$ machines, and the first explicit lower bounds for online makespan minimization in which the adversary presents jobs in non-monotone order of size.

papers.title: Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Yujing Huang, Yingyan Zeng
papers.abstract: Many scientific responses take values in Riemannian manifolds, with predictors that are scalar- and/or manifold-valued. A regression analysis in such settings must provide accurate prediction with hypothesis testing for individual coefficients. Yet no current manifold-regression framework accommodates both predictor types and enables per-coefficient hypothesis tests. We propose Riemannian Ordinary Least Squares (ROLS) as a tangent space conditional-mean model, which is the ordinary least squares (OLS) analogue for Riemannian manifolds. ROLS is well-defined under an explicit injectivity condition that keeps the logarithm maps single-valued, with cut-locus conditions for branch-sensitive cases outside it. Within the local geometric setting it admits a closed-form estimator, an $O(n^{-1})$ excess prediction-error bound with explicit curvature bias, and asymptotic $t$- and Wald tests for individual coefficients. With synthetic simulations and three real-data case studies, ROLS is shown to be competitive with the state-of-the-art baselines. In addition, the per-coefficient tests agree with effects reported in literature. We envision ROLS to be a standard tool for manifold-valued regression with coefficient-level inference to support scientific discovery, which can be interpreted in the same way as Euclidean OLS. The source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyuChenPub/ROLS.

papers.title: The Fast Tree Transform
papers.abstract: The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.

papers.title: Group-Conditional Conformal Risk Control: Exact Guarantees, Limits, and Overlapping Extensions
papers.abstract:
We study group-conditional conformal risk control (CRC) for disjoint and overlapping groups under bounded monotone losses. For disjoint groups, we establish exact finite-sample conditional risk control, two-sided bounds on the group-restricted risk, and fundamental limitations arising from local support and calibration-rank granularity.
  For overlapping groups, we study two exactly valid approaches: group-restricted calibration followed by union deployment, and direct calibration of the deployed prediction-set family. We characterize the union's limiting reconciliation gap, identify conditions for its disappearance, and establish sharp lower bounds for structured losses in specified product-form models. We also demonstrate a strict size advantage for direct calibration in an ordinal model.
  Experiments show that direct calibration can reduce prediction-set size, but its efficiency depends on group structure, loss type, and shape fitting. Results on historical diabetic-retinopathy scores further illustrate these tradeoffs. Overall, local support, reconciliation slack, and threshold heterogeneity determine efficiency, with neither approach uniformly dominating.

papers.title: A trace costs one quantifier: the exact complexity of perfect play in nonlocal games
papers.abstract: Given a finite nonlocal game, can the players win with certainty? We prove that the existence of a perfect normal spatial strategy is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, even when restricted to games of value one, so it cannot be decided even with an oracle for the halting problem. This is strictly harder than perfect play in the finite-dimensional and commuting-operator models, which are $\Sigma^0_1$-complete and $\Pi^0_1$-complete. Within the commuting model, the existence of a perfect normal strategy with a finite or semifinite von Neumann host is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete, whereas for every fixed type $\mathrm{III}_\lambda$ subtype it has the same $\Pi^0_1$-complete language as unrestricted commuting play. A trace thus costs one existential number quantifier: the hardness constructions force every perfect strategy to choose a finite clock period or a finite tree depth. Spatial $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness also holds when finite entanglement entropy is required, and both forms are formally verified in Lean. For every computable $0<\alpha<1$, perfect spatial play with $\mathrm{Tr}\,h^\alpha<\infty$ for the reduced density $h$ is $\Sigma^0_2$-complete as well; these conditions form a strict ladder between finite rank and finite entropy. We also prove $\Sigma^0_2$-completeness for one-shot zero-error communication with normal entanglement, and construct a finite channel with zero-error codes of a given size each of which needs infinite entanglement entropy.

papers.title: Reconstructing Interacting Blood Flow and Wall Interface Deformation from Noisy Flow Data Using PirateNets
papers.authors: Han Zhang, Xue-Cheng Tai, Alessandro Veneziani, Raymond H. Chan
papers.abstract: Blood flow and elastic vessel-wall motion interact with each other: fluid stress drives wall deformation, while the moving wall changes the domain in which blood flows. Given noisy flow images, we study the inverse problem of reconstructing the coupled, unsteady three-dimensional motions. We solve the reconstruction through Gauss--Seidel-type alternating fluid and geometry updates. For the fluid, we use physics-informed networks to recover velocity and pressure by fitting the observations while enforcing the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on the moving domain, which is described by an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian (ALE) map. For the geometry, a reference-domain correction and sequential registration recover the vessel shape and wall displacement. Interface traction continuity and an elastic momentum equation regularize the registration so that the recovered displacement is also physics-informed. The networks evaluate fields and physical residuals at sampled space--time points without remeshing the moving domain. Experiments on a converging channel and a patient-like aorta demonstrate reconstruction of flow and wall motion from noisy data. Ablation and parameter-sensitivity studies examine the role of structure regularization and imperfect physical coefficients. A further experiment with a three-element Windkessel outlet condition demonstrates how the framework accommodates a more physiologically realistic boundary setting.

papers.title: Comonotonic and moment matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables II
papers.abstract: In this paper, based on the concept of step-weighted distribution, we introduce a minimum-deformation approach to constructing comonotonic and moment-matching approximations for sums of lognormal random variables. The proposed approach aims to minimize the Pearson deformation of a starting comonotonic approximation subject to moment-matching constraints. We establish several results concerning the existence and uniqueness of minimum-deformation comonotonic approximations and propose a method for determining the step quantiles and weights. In particular, when the number of steps is one greater than the moment-matching order, we show that the joint optimization problem can be reduced to an optimization problem involving only the partition points. The proposed framework accommodates moment matching of any prescribed finite order, and numerical experiments demonstrate its application to approximations matching the first five moments of the original sum. The numerical results also show that minimizing the Pearson deformation does not necessarily improve the approximation accuracy of risk measures, which depends on both the starting comonotonic approximation and the choice of partition points and correction weights.

papers.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
papers.authors: Pengfei Song, Yanni Xiao, Shuangshuang Yin
papers.abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.

papers.title: Deep backward multistep high-order regression methods for high dimensional nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations
papers.authors: Qiang Han, Shaolin Ji, Zihao Xv
papers.abstract: We propose a deep backward multistep high-order regression (MHDBR) method for semilinear parabolic partial differential equations through their backward stochastic differential equation representations. The method combines multistep time discretization with regression targets formed by conditional expectations. Under explicit regularity, starting-value, forward-approximation and network-moment assumptions, we prove an error bound separating time discretization, conditional Monte Carlo sampling and neural-network approximation. The analysis assumes exact population minimization; finite-training-sample generalization and optimization errors are not included. For generators independent of the gradient variable, suitably constrained GroupSort networks and sufficiently large conditional sample sizes give order $J$ in the stated nodal $L^2$ error norm. The required network sizes depend on dimension, so this result does not establish dimension-independent complexity. We present a reproducible time-discretization test satisfying the analytical assumptions and three broader neural-network benchmarks, whose relation to the assumptions is discussed explicitly.

papers.title: A Simple Computer-Assisted Proof of the 5/6-Bound for Real-Period Pinwheel Scheduling
papers.authors: Hiroshi Fujiwara, Grzegorz Gutowski, Katsuhisa Ouchi, Alexander Wolff
papers.abstract: In pinwheel scheduling with real periods, an instance consists of $n$ tasks with real periods $1\le a_1\le a_2\le\cdots\le a_n$. The goal is to find a schedule that assigns one task to each day indefinitely such that, for every task $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every positive integer $\ell$, task $i$ occurs at least $\ell$ times in every block of $\lceil\ell a_i\rceil$ consecutive days. Given an instance $(a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n)$, its dimension is $n$, its density is $\sum_{i=1}^n1/a_i$, and its potential is $\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}1/a_i$. We prove that every real-valued instance of density at most 5/6 admits a periodic schedule of period length less than $4\cdot2^n$. For integer periods, the 5/6 density bound was a long-standing conjecture settled by Kawamura using a computer-assisted proof [STOC 2024, PNAS 2026]. Our result confirms the real-period conjecture of Fujiwara, Miyagi, and Ouchi [DMTCS 2026]. Our computer-assisted proof builds on Kawamura's ideas while using fewer explicit schedules. It combines dimension reduction by folding with nine satisfiability modulo theories (SMT) checks over linear real arithmetic. A set of 14287 explicit periodic schedules contains a schedule for every instance of dimension at most 8 and density at most 5/6, and for every instance of dimension 9 and potential at most 5/6. Folding is used to reduce every instance of larger dimension and potential at most 5/6 to an instance of dimension 9 and the same potential bound. We also prove that every real-valued instance with minimum period at least 4 and density at most 17/20=0.85 admits a periodic schedule of period length less than $19\cdot2^n$. The density bound 17/20 is tight and improves the 0.84-bound of Mishra, Rho, and Kleinberg [arXiv 2025] for integer periods. It also resolves the $a_1=4$ case of Kawamura's 2025 conjecture that integer-valued instances of density at most $1-(a_1-1)/(a_1(a_1+1))$ are schedulable.

papers.title: A Geometric Theory for Nonequilibrium Transformer Dynamics
papers.authors: Aythami Bethencourt de Le\'{o}n, Darryl D. Holm
papers.abstract: We develop a variational and geometric theory based on statistical physics for the joint evolution of Transformer attention and token representations at fixed model parameters. To this end, we introduce a free energy for the attention and model the evolution of the attention weights by its Fisher--Rao gradient flow. At fixed token representations, we prove that the softmax matrix is the unique free-energy minimiser and that every positive attention trajectory converges to it. For prescribed time-dependent representations, we show that the attention dynamics becomes linear after a change to logit variables. This result yields tracking bounds relative to the instantaneous softmax and sufficient conditions for attention to converge to a fixed matrix. Hamiltonian dynamics for the representations and their momenta are then coupled to the attention relaxation driven by the same energy. This coupling results in an energy-dissipation law. We also develop two alternative Hamiltonians incorporating the attention value map. We prove global well-posedness of the attention flow and all three coupled systems.

papers.title: Spectral Bias Reduction in Local Gated ReLU Architectures
papers.abstract:
Neural networks trained by gradient-based methods learn the low-frequency content of a target function faster than its high-frequency content. This spectral bias is well documented, but it is much less clear which architectural choices mitigate it and which cannot. We study the question for shallow ReLU models linear in their trainable parameters, where each mode is learned at a rate given by a Gram-matrix eigenvalue, and for a general symmetric bilinear form $a(\cdot,\cdot)$, so that least-squares regression ($a=$ the $L^2$ inner product) and variational or physics-informed losses ($a=$ the $H^1$ energy form) are two instances of one analysis.
  Within this framework we propose gated local ReLU dictionaries, obtained by multiplying each ReLU feature by a hat partition-of-unity weight, in the spirit of partition-of-unity finite elements and overlapping Schwarz methods. The resulting Gram matrices are block-banded for any local bilinear form, with a block-Toeplitz interior whose matrix-valued symbol governs the spectrum.
  The two forms then behave very differently. For $L^2$ regression, the symbol is bounded away from zero, the ratio is uniform in the number of windows, and the measured spread of frequency-dependent learning rates falls from $1.9\times10^{5}$ to $4.5$ at matched model size. For the $H^1$ stiffness matrix, the symbol vanishes at zero frequency: gating leaves the $\Theta(N^2)$ conditioning intact and inverts the frequency ordering instead of removing the bias. A preconditioner built from the same interior stencil will fix the spectral bias, showing that architecture alone is not enough. Experiments on $1$D regression and Poisson problems confirm the dichotomy, and the regression effect persists when the hidden-layer parameters are trained as well.

papers.title: Weighted Matroid Intersection under Minimum Rank Oracle
papers.abstract:
We consider matroid intersection under the minimum rank oracle model, in which two matroids are accessible only through an oracle that returns the minimum of the ranks of a given set in the two matroids. By Edmonds' theorem, this oracle determines the matroid intersection polytope, although it does not reveal the exchangeability graphs on which classical algorithms rely. Recent work by B\'ar\'asz, B\'erczi, Kir\'aly, Oki, Yamaguchi, and Yokoi (2025) showed that unweighted matroid intersection is polynomially solvable in this model.
  In this paper, we present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm for weighted matroid intersection in this model. The key to our algorithm is a polynomial-size extended formulation of tangent cones of common base polytopes that can be constructed using the minimum rank oracle. We also give min-max theorems in terms of the minimum rank function via 1/3-submodularity, and present a strongly polynomial-time algorithm to compute an optimal dual solution.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Riemannian Optimization on Fixed-Rank Manifolds for LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.authors: Xinjue Wang, Xiuheng Wang, Yejun Zhang, Sergiy A. Vorobyov, Esa Ollila
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization estimates descent directions from function values alone, which removes the activation storage required by backpropagation and makes it attractive for memory-efficient fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). Existing low-rank ZO methods either parameterize the additive update through Euclidean factors with a non-unique representation, or restrict each finite-difference direction to be low-rank. In this work, we propose to constrain each additive update block to a fixed-rank matrix manifold while keeping the pretrained weights frozen, so the learned update remains rank-constrained throughout fine-tuning. On this geometry, we build a Riemannian ZO gradient estimator that projects a random matrix onto the tangent space, normalizes it to correct the scale mismatch induced by projection, and further propose Zeroth-order Riemannian Gradient Descent (ZO-RGD) and its smoothed variant, ZO-RGD-S. We show that the ambient finite difference matches its retracted counterpart, the normalized estimator recovers the Riemannian gradient in expectation, and ZO-RGD converges under trajectory-regularity conditions. Experiments on LLM fine-tuning tasks show that the proposed algorithms are competitive with strong forward-only baselines across model families and tasks, with gains in several settings.

papers.title: Online Imitation Learning for Stabilizing Vlasov--Poisson Plasmas
papers.authors: Xiaofan Xia, Qin Li, Wenlong Mou
papers.abstract: We study the problem of controlling instability in the Vlasov--Poisson plasma systems, a fundamental challenge for nuclear fusion control. Motivated by the partial observability of plasma states in practice, we investigate imitation learning algorithms that learn from a fully-observable expert controller, but operate under macroscopic measurements. We theoretically establish a separation between online and offline imitation learning --- even a small behavior cloning error leads to error compounding that exponentially amplifies instability over time. By way of contrast, the online imitation learning loss can polynomially control the stability of rollout trajectories. We then propose a DAgger-style algorithm that learns the stabilizing controller under partial observability. Simulation results on a 1D Vlasov--Poisson system demonstrate that our algorithm can effectively stabilize plasma instabilities over longer time horizons than behavior cloning.

papers.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
papers.abstract: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_\lambda$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(\Omega,g,k=\lambda g)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $\lambda$ below a geometrically determined threshold $\alpha$, while vanishing $E_\lambda$ at $\lambda=\alpha$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_\lambda=0$ when $\lambda=\alpha$, then $(\Omega,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/\lambda$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

papers.title: Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron
papers.authors: Fabio Benatti, Masoud Gharahi, Giovanni Gramegna, Stefano Mancini, Vincenzo Parisi
papers.abstract: Variational quantum classifiers can generate highly structured decision boundaries through the Fourier dependence of observable expectation values on circuit parameters. We show that expressivity can come at a sharp statistical cost, by considering a quantum perceptron whose readout is the simplest periodic classifier, namely a square-wave function of the weighted inputs, and determine its typical generalization in the thermodynamic limit using a teacher-student replica-symmetric theory. Above a critical oscillation frequency, increasing the training load induces a first-order transition from weakly to strongly teacher-aligned phases, resulting in a discontinuous improvement in generalization. At fixed load, however, increasing the frequency eventually drives the equilibrium generalization error to chance level, despite perfect classification of all the training examples. Thus, the same periodic structure that enhances random-label storage can delay the onset of learning. Our results expose a quantitative tradeoff between memorization and generalization generated purely by periodic readout, and provide a benchmark for understanding Fourier-rich variational quantum classifiers.

papers.title: Optimal Byzantine-resilient Federated Learning with User-level Differential Privacy
papers.authors: Ming Xiang, Stratis Ioannidis, Edmund Yeh, Carlee Joe-Wong, Lili Su
papers.abstract: Real-world deployment of federated learning (FL) requires resilience against adversarial clients and data privacy. Byzantine fault captures the worst-case behavior of adversarial clients, while differential privacy (DP) provides statistical guarantees against privacy loss. In particular, user-level DP guards a client's entire contribution and provides more realistic protection against information leakage. Despite intensive efforts, the minimax-optimal convergence bound of Byzantine-resilient FL with user-level DP remains open. We establish an information-theoretic lower bound for any Byzantine-resilient empirical risk minimization problem under user-level DP and heterogeneous clients. We propose ByzULDP, a central DP algorithm featuring a two-level momentum across the client and server. Client-side momentum mitigates stochastic gradient variance during robust aggregation. Unlike the fault-free case, naively combining non-linear Byzantine-resilient aggregation with central DP noise can be insufficient to guarantee convergence to a bounded neighborhood of a stationary point. Our key contribution is a server-side momentum that leverages a property specific to user-level DP, where privacy sensitivity depends on how client updates are constructed, to empower convergence. ByzULDP achieves the order-optimal convergence bound for strongly-convex objectives, with vanishing error terms decaying at the optimal $O(1/T)$ and $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ rates for strongly-convex and non-convex objectives, respectively. We corroborate our analysis with numerical experiments on real-world datasets across diverse privacy budgets.

papers.title: Positivity Proofs for Third-Order Holonomic Sequences via Differences Scaled by Rational Functions
papers.abstract:
We study the positivity of sequences $f$ that satisfy a third-order holonomic recurrence $f(n+3)= P_2(n) f(n+2) + P_1(n) f(n+1) + P_0(n) f(n)$ whose coefficients $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ are rational functions in $\R(x)$. We provide a sufficient condition on $P_0$, $P_1$ and $P_2$ for the recurrence to admit a solution all but finitely many terms of which are positive, and whose positivity is robust under small perturbations of the initial values. This sufficient condition is also a necessary condition for a subclass of the recurrences. By developing the proof of this sufficient condition, for another subclass of the recurrences, we show that it is decidable whether all the terms of a given sequence are positive for any initial values outside an exceptional plane.
  It is common to construct a positivity certificate, which guarantees the positivity of a solution, to show this kind of decidability. In this paper, we construct a new type of positivity certificate via the $S$-scaled difference $f(n+1) - S(n) f(n)$ for a suitable $S \in \R(x)$. This result partially improves the work by Ibrahim and Salvy.

papers.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
papers.authors: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Yiyao Huang, Arushi Katyal, Ryan Lin, Pranav Ramakrishnan, Weiya Wang
papers.abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for Robust Blinded Sample Size Re-estimation Based on Nuisance Parameters
papers.authors: Long-Hao Xu, Lei Li, Tim Friede
papers.abstract: Blinded sample size re-estimation aims to mitigate uncertainty in nuisance parameters at the design stage while preserving the integrity of the trial. It allows the required sample size to be updated without revealing treatment assignments and thereby reduces the risk of an inappropriate sample size. Although numerous procedures have been proposed for different outcome types, a unified framework is still lacking. We therefore develop a general framework for blinded sample size re-estimation based on nuisance parameters. Within this general framework, we develop robust methods to reduce the influence of extreme observations. The proposed framework combines asymptotically linear estimators for the parameter of interest with robust Z-estimators for nuisance parameters, thereby unifying a broad class of existing procedures through different choices of estimating functions. We also propose a general principle for constructing nuisance parameters that can be estimated from blinded data. The proposed framework is supported by asymptotic theory showing that the type I error rate converges to the nominal level under regularity conditions. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed method maintains reliable type I error control across a range of settings, including contaminated data and small pilot sample sizes. Compared with existing blinded and unblinded methods, the proposed framework is more flexible and less sensitive to outliers. A clinical trial application illustrates its practical utility.

papers.title: Improving Analytic Constants via Interpretable AI-Guided Lean Proof Refinement
papers.authors: Rahul Saha, Alan Li, Anton Xue, Swarat Chaudhuri, Adam Klivans, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka
papers.abstract:
AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. Our key insight is that existing proofs often contain slack in intermediate lemmas, which can be tightened without reconstructing the entire argument. To exploit this structure, we represent proofs as partially-formalized Lean blueprints: human-interpretable dependency graphs of definitions, lemmas, and theorems. An AI agent then iteratively refines the Lean code while preserving the blueprint's dependency structure, allowing local improvements to automatically propagate to a verified final bound. This interpretable structure allows humans to inspect the agent's refinements and understand how local improvements propagate to the final theorem. For Grothendieck's constant ($\mathcal{K}_G$), we obtain $$
  \mathcal{K}_G \leq
  \frac{\pi}{2\log(1+\sqrt{2})} - 10^{-17}, $$ an explicit numerical improvement over Krivine's 1977 bound. For Korenblum's constant ($\mathcal{K}_K$), we obtain $$
  \mathcal{K}_K \geq 0.356565, $$ improving Wang's 2025 bound of $0.3554$. Our experiments demonstrate the potential of both partial formalization and iterative agentic refinement for interpretable mathematical discovery.

papers.title: Analysis of the Effect of Doppler on Direct-to-Cell: Real-World Performance and Proposed Improvements
papers.authors: Yuxi Chen, Muhammad Iqbal Rochman, Kyler McCormack, Jakob Kotz, Monisha Ghosh
papers.abstract: Direct-to-cell (DtC) satellites serve unmodified LTE phones today from low Earth orbit, where the satellite's motion creates Doppler shifts of tens of kHz. Since large offsets such as these cannot be compensated adequately by the user equipment (UE), the satellite pre-compensates the Doppler shift of each beam, but it can do so for only one reference point in the beam. A UE elsewhere in the beam still has to compensate a residual offset; previous field studies report residuals of up to 10 kHz, beyond the $\pm$7.5 kHz that the 15 kHz subcarrier spacing can resolve. In this paper we corroborate this effect with our own detailed measurements of Starlink transmissions and further correlate ineffective handover performance to inadequate residual offset compensation. We analyze the Doppler compensation problem with detailed standard-specific simulations and propose a compensation method at the UE, based on the location of the UE with respect to the beam reference point used for the Doppler compensation and the known satellite location, that improves the efficiency of handover. With UE cell-specific pre-compensation, the neighbors are identified, read correctly and handed over to in time rather than lost to radio-link failure.

papers.title: Large-Scale Hierarchical Decision-Making in Robot Control via ADMM
papers.authors: Kai Pfeiffer, Jia Wang, Gordon Owusu Boateng, Yuquan Wang, Vincent Bonnet, Abderrahmane Kheddar
papers.abstract: Sparse hierarchical nonlinear programming (SH-NLP) based on the $\ell_0$-norm provides a powerful framework for integrated, efficient hierarchical decision-making in robot kinematic control, for example in the presence of a large set of possible end-effector candidate locations. While Sequential Sparse Hierarchical Quadratic Programming (S-SHQP) with interior-point method based SHQP sub-problem solvers exploit the hierarchical, sparse structure of such problems, they are less amenable to effective warm-starting between subsequent, coherent control steps. In this work, we formulate an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) to efficiently solve related SHQP sub-problems. We introduce efficient substitutions for auxiliary variables representing $\ell_0$-norm surrogates. The solver efficiently handles separable decision functions by evaluating linear algebra expressions in the appropriate order. Results in large-scale kinematic and dynamic control show reduced computation times of up to 23.5% compared with a structure-exploiting interior-point method in low- to moderate-accuracy regimes. Furthermore, hierarchical decision-making is extended to whole-body dynamic control for humanoid walking, where the need for high-accuracy solutions is highlighted.

papers.title: Scalable Neural Safety Certification via Monotonicity
papers.authors: Amirreza Alavi, Majid Zamani, Saber Jafarpour
papers.abstract: Learning-based safety certification offers a promising route for verifying complex dynamical systems when explicit models are unavailable, but existing data-driven methods often scale poorly: they treat the system as a black box, rely on dense discretizations or Lipschitz bounds, and consequently suffer from sample complexity that grows exponentially with dimension. This paper shows that a common structural property of dynamical systems--monotonicity--can be used to break this curse of dimensionality. We develop a data-driven framework for robust safety verification and safe controller synthesis for unknown monotone systems using only simulator queries. Our main theoretical result proves that, for monotone systems with upper-closed unsafe sets, safety is completely characterized by the existence of monotone inductive barrier certificates. This structure reduces certificate verification over continuous state spaces to localized boundary checks over finitely many cells. To learn such certificates, we introduce Max-Monotone Networks, a monotone neural architecture with universal approximation guarantees for monotone functions. We then propose a training and refinement algorithm that, upon successful termination, returns formally valid neural barrier certificates and, under mild partition assumptions, requires only $O(n)$ simulator queries. Across high-dimensional benchmarks, including oscillator networks with up to $13{,}659$ states and traffic networks with $1{,}000$ states, our method certifies safety in regimes where prior approaches either do not converge or exceed memory limits. These results demonstrate that exploiting order structure can make neural safety certification both scalable and formally sound.

papers.title: Optimal Polynomial-Query Approximation for Consistent Submodular Maximization with Short Lookahead
papers.abstract: Elements arrive one at a time, and after each arrival an algorithm holds a set of at most $k$ arrived elements. Its goal is a held set whose value under a monotone submodular function is close to the best value that $k$ arrived elements can achieve. The recourse of an update is the number of elements inserted into or removed from the held set, and we require it to be bounded independently of $k$ and of the number $n$ of arrivals. With evaluations only on sets of arrived elements and polynomially many of them, the best ratio a randomized algorithm can achieve is $2-\sqrt{2}\approx0.5858$. We show that seeing future arrivals raises the best ratio for polynomially many evaluations to $1-1/e\approx0.6321$, for deterministic and for randomized algorithms; no algorithm with polynomially many evaluations exceeds $1-1/e$, even when all elements are available at once. For every $\varepsilon>0$, a deterministic algorithm that sees the next $\lceil\varepsilon k/3\rceil$ arrivals keeps a set of value at least $1-1/e-\varepsilon$ times the optimum at every time, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-3})$ elements per arrival and makes $(n+1)^{O(\varepsilon^{-2})}$ evaluations. With the whole arrival sequence known in advance, a deterministic algorithm attains the same ratio with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ changes per arrival. A randomized algorithm with the same short lookahead makes $O(n^2k)$ evaluations, changes $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ elements per arrival, and attains the same ratio in expectation at each fixed time. The main tool is a greedy algorithm with an explicit guarantee for each of its partial solutions combined with each initial segment of the known future arrivals. A second tool moves between two such solutions one element at a time while keeping the value high, and the deterministic algorithm times each move using upper bounds on the optimum from failed searches.

papers.title: Heavy tails in Gaussian-process surrogates: process-level profiling degeneracy versus observation-level identifiability
papers.authors: Neelesh S. Upadhye, Rohit Kumar Mani
papers.abstract: In this article, we study heavy-tailed alternatives to Gaussian-process surrogates, namely Student-$t$ processes, $\alpha$-stable processes and Gaussian processes with heavy-tailed noise. These are Gaussian scale mixtures, and the position of the mixing variable decides whether the tails can be learned from a single realization. For process-level mixtures with a free amplitude, the profile likelihood of the mixing law is data-free and is maximized by the Gaussian law, the plug-in predictive is a data-free transformation of the Gaussian-process predictive, and no estimator can be consistent for the mixing law over the model along one path. For observation-level mixtures with symmetric $\alpha$-stable noise, the tail index is identifiable. Further, for one-dimensional inputs under fixed-domain asymptotics with $\alpha_0<2$ and compact hyperparameter sets, a cross-fitted plug-in estimator and the Laplace marginal-likelihood estimate computed at the global posterior mode attain the efficiency bound of the model with a known regression function, also for Mat\'ern-$5/2$ sample paths. We also characterize small-sample failures of the Laplace approximation as folds of a posterior-mode branch and give a diagnostic. Finally, in a repeated Bayesian optimization study, observation-level tails reduced regret under gross outliers, as did Student-$t$ noise, and no degradation was detected under Gaussian noise.

papers.title: Chaos Growth in a Generic 2D Hamiltonian System
papers.abstract: We examine the geometric mechanism controlling the transition from local to global chaos in a generic 2D Hamiltonian system, the generalized H\'{e}non-Heiles system. Using Poincar\'e sections and invariant manifolds, we show that the chaotic fraction grows through abrupt transitions associated with the destruction of invariant barriers. We introduce an index that gives the time required for the first penetration of a local chaotic domain into the global chaos. This index increases sharply and tends to infinity as a critical energy is approached. The set of lobes generates heteroclinic connections, while multiple unstable periodic orbits exhibit a global manifold structure characterised by repeated loops and lobes. However, in special chaotic cases close to the integrable H\'{e}non-Heiles potential, where two asymptotic curves extend to infinity, the manifold topology differs qualitatively from the generic case, as the asymptotic curves no longer form closed structures surrounding the periodic orbits.

papers.title: Chatter Attack: Resource Consumption Attack for Large Language Models
papers.authors: Yibo Miao, Yichuan Cao, Xiao-Shan Gao, Yinpeng Dong
papers.abstract: LLMs are powerful but incur substantial inference cost, which can be exploited by malicious users to induce overly long outputs, increasing latency and operational expense. Prior resource consumption attacks either coerce repetition or suppress the end-of-sequence token by lowering its logit value. However, with autoregressive, sampling-based generation, the search space grows exponentially with length and small deviations or unstable trajectories can derail optimization, limiting attack effectiveness and stability. To address this issue, we introduce Chatter Attack, a novel class of resource consumption attacks that optimize adversarial prompts to induce predefined short target phrases, thereby avoiding search-space explosion while still eliciting long responses. Specifically, Chatter Attack triggers self-doubt using short doubt-inducing phrases as the target, and sustains this state throughout generation via inference attention loss and global entropy loss. To extend to black-box settings, we further propose a novel Bayesian Prompt Optimization (BPO) method, which models the objective function globally by constructing a discrete token kernel, efficiently exploring the entire search space using prior information. Extensive experiments across multiple models and datasets show that our method outperforms baselines, with maximum response length increases to 31.5$\times$, and revealing practical resource-depletion risks for real-world LLM inference services.

papers.title: Parametrizations of the solutions of Love equations and their momenta
papers.authors: Marco Faccioli, Andrea Colcelli, Danny Laghi, Yu Zhou, Giacomo Gori, Andrea Trombettoni
papers.abstract: The Love equation is a paradigmatic example of a Fredholm integral equation of great interest in mathematics and physics, where its applications range from electrostatic problems to exactly solvable models for one-dimensional systems. In this work we propose a method to approximate the normalized solutions of Love equations of the first and second kind via a parametrization obtained by Hermite interpolation at Chebyshev nodes. Following the same approach, we also obtain approximations for the second, fourth and sixth momenta of the solution of the Love equations. We focus in particular on one-dimensional quantum gases described by the Lieb-Liniger and the Gaudin-Yang models. For these models, the solutions of Love equations correspond to the normalized densities of pseudorapidities. We show that remarkably accurate results can be obtained using the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation with a number of points as low as 17+2. In the case of the Lieb-Liniger model, we also propose a very accurate closed-form estimate of the dimensionless ground state energy valid for all values of the dimensionless interaction parameter incorporating known results for small and large couplings supplemented by the Hermite-Chebyshev interpolation for intermediate couplings. As an application of this result, we compute the dimensionless local two-particle correlation function and the black soliton solutions of the Lieb-Liniger model.

papers.title: Linear Objective Problems: A Complexity Framework for Bilevel Optimization
papers.authors: Christoph Gr\"une, James B. Orlin, Lasse Wulf
papers.abstract:
Many bilevel and robust optimization problems are complete for the second level of the polynomial hierarchy, but such results are usually proven one problem at a time with problem-specific reductions. A recurring obstacle is that the lower level must select an optimal solution rather than merely a feasible one, whereas standard reductions preserve only whether a solution exists, not which solutions are optimal. We introduce linear objective problems (LOP), a framework for optimization problems whose solutions are explicit subsets of a ground set and whose objective is linear in these elements. We define tight solution-embedding reductions, which map the optimal solutions of one problem element by element onto the optimal solutions of another, without having to recognize optimal solutions, which is coNP-hard in general. This gives a notion of LOP-completeness, with Satisfiability as the canonical complete problem, even with unit weights.
  We show that many classical problems are LOP-complete, including Vertex Cover, Dominating Set, TSP, Knapsack, and Steiner Tree, and we introduce a duality that transfers LOP-completeness between minimization and maximization problems. As our main application, we prove a meta-theorem for min-max regret optimization under interval uncertainty: for every LOP-complete problem, the min-max regret version is $\Sigma_2^p$-complete. Instead of a separate proof for each nominal problem, it suffices to show that the nominal problem is LOP-complete. This recovers known results for the interval min-max regret versions of Knapsack and Maximum Benefit Set Cover and yields completeness for over 50 further problems.

papers.title: Orthogonal Updates for the Win: Towards Accelerated Adaptive Minimax Optimization
papers.authors: Zhiwei Zhai, Xinyu Wang, Wenjing Yan, Lei Ding, Ying-Jun Angela Zhang
papers.abstract: Single-loop minimax methods are appealing for modern machine learning, but standard stochastic gradient updates can be unstable and oscillatory under tightly coupled primal-dual dynamics, making performance notoriously sensitive to stepsizes. To fundamentally improve stability, we develop an orthogonal update framework tailored to minimax optimization, which applies updates along orthogonalized directions to reduce update anisotropy. However, orthogonalization reshapes the optimization geometry and makes coordinating primal-dual stepsizes even more delicate. To overcome this challenge, we develop AdaSGDA, which equips orthogonal updates with an adaptive stepsize rule driven by accumulated gradient norms.
