The geometric properties of these sets have therefore been studied intensely. In this paper we focus on the intrinsic metric properties of sets of positive reach. In particular we give an elementary proof of the fact that (closed) sets of reach at least $R$ are $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$. This fact was established earlier by Alexander and Bishop, using quite significant machinery. The fact that a space is $\operatorname{CAT}(1/R^2)$ offers many advantages, such as the uniqueness and continuity of sufficiently short geodesics, the existence of Fr{\'e}chet means and by extension the Rips based homotopy reconstruction of Hausmann is available.

papers.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
papers.abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

papers.title: Efficient high-order Discontinuous Galerkin simulations of multi-species high-enthalpy flows
papers.authors: Beatriz Fag\'a, Georgii Oblapenko, Yiyang Zhu, Daniel Doehring, Manuel Torrilhon
papers.abstract: Numerical simulation of hypersonic vehicles is an attractive approach to investigate the complex phenomena involved in such technologies. For this, second-order finite volume methods (FVM) are the established method in computational fluid dynamics, with the cost of high dissipation in affordable meshes, thus needing refined ones or adaptive mesh refinements techniques to obtain accurate results. An alternative is to make use of high-order discontinuous Galerkin methods, in particular discontinuous Galerkin spectral element method (DGSEM), once it achieves higher formal order of accuracy on element-local polynomial bases. Therefore the goal of this work is to present the numerical simulations of a two-dimensional scramjet configuration to test and verify the applicability of the DGSEM approach for a complex hypersonic flow where shock-shock interactions occur. Results revealed to be in agreement with reference FVM solvers, thus verifying the code implementation.

papers.title: Singularising quantum channels preserving kappa-additivity
papers.abstract:
We construct quantum channels by averaging unitary shift conjugations with respect to $\kappa$-additive probability measures on measurable abelian groups.
  The channels act on the duals of operator algebras generated by shifts and bounded measurable multiplication operators.
  They preserve $\kappa$-additivity of quantum states and admit a weak-$*$ integral representation on this class.
  If the averaging measure vanishes on singletons, every output state is singular.
  In the appendix, we also establish the corresponding Fubini's theorem for $\kappa$-additive measures.

papers.title: Degradation-Aware Participation of Battery Storage in Frequency Regulation Markets
papers.abstract: As data centers make the load on the power grid fluctuate faster, frequency regulation grows more valuable. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) are well suited to provide frequency regulation, but providing this service speeds up aging, especially during operation at extreme state of charge (SoC). In the PJM interconnection, the grid operator supplies a regulation signal that a participating BESS is expected to follow, within a capacity that it must bid before the signal is known. Accordingly, we decompose the degradation-aware frequency regulation problem into a bidding layer and an operations layer. For bidding, we propose an adaptive strategy, assuming perfect tracking in which the bid depends on the SoC expected at the start of the bid period by means of choosing basepoints. For operation, the BESS further protects its battery by deliberately giving up a perfect performance score, to keep its SoC away from the extremes. On the PJM regulation signal and prices of 2023, adaptive bids lengthen the battery life by $31\%$ against bidding full capacity, for $2.2\%$ of the revenue. Giving up a perfect score in operation lengthens the battery life of constant bids by $10\%$ to $27\%$, at a change in revenue of at most $0.2\%$.

papers.title: Nonlinear integral equations for stress-controlled rheology: Collocation methods for Volterra equations with functional kernels
papers.abstract: We present a class of numerical collocation methods to solve a typical inverse problem that arises in the stress-controlled rheology of complex fluids with pronounced history-dependent response, where the relation between stress and flow rate is given by an integral constitutive equation as the material law. We demonstrate the method by calculating the creep response of a nontrivial model of a shear-thinning viscoelastic fluid where a stress overshoot in rate-controlled startup flow leads to ``sudden yielding'' in stress-controlled creep. Our method is able to address the long-time behavior of the model, distinguishing the amorphous solid from the stress-induced yielded fluid, and from the in-between case of infinite deformation that never achieves a stationary shear rate (proper creep). To this end, we implement a method with flexible time-stepping, and prove uniqueness of the solution and convergence of the methods for a broad class of highly viscoelastic non-linear rheological laws in integral form.

papers.title: Near-Purity Screening and Dominant-Atom Estimation in Softmax Mixtures and Their Ensembles
papers.authors: Xin Bing, Florentina Bunea, Marten Wegkamp, Weicheng Wu
papers.abstract:
We study near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation in softmax mixtures, whose components share a common set of category features. A mixture is called $\varepsilon$-pure if one of its mixing weights is at least $1-\varepsilon$. We introduce the Trace of Latent Covariance Criterion ($\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$), a direct estimator of the trace of the covariance matrix of the latent mixing measure, constructed without estimating its atoms or weights, or knowing the number of components. Unlike existing moment-based approaches, our estimator is constructed for the softmax family and does not require knowledge or estimation of the feature distribution.
  We establish finite-sample guarantees for $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$, showing that it achieves a parametric convergence rate up to an additive approximation error of order $p^{-1/2}$, without requiring minimum separation between mixture atoms. We also study estimation of the dominant atom in near-pure mixtures by fitting a single softmax component. We prove that the resulting maximum likelihood estimator has an error bound consisting of the usual parametric term and a bias term governed by the weighted distances between the dominant and remaining atoms, revealing adaptation to the geometry of the mixture.
  Finally, we extend near-purity screening and dominant-atom estimation to ensembles of softmax mixtures with shared atoms and mixture-specific weights. We apply $\mathrm{TLC}^{2}$ separately to each ensemble member to screen for near-purity without knowing the number of components. Under additional assumptions, clustering the resulting dominant-atom estimators yields finite-sample guarantees for estimating the shared atoms. An application to the Million Song Dataset illustrates how the estimated softmax directions reveal interpretable structure in the data.

papers.title: Higher tensor network states in two spatial dimensions: fundamental theorem for open boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We introduce a class of two-dimensional tensor network states obtained by categorifying matrix product states. This procedure leads us to consider bond spaces provided by a 2-vector space associated with the 2-cells of the underlying lattice. Tensor network representations are then defined as module categories over the free monoidal category on a monoidal signature encoding the lattice geometry. We prove a fundamental theorem stating that two representations generating the same states with suitable open boundary conditions are equivalent as module categories. Finally, we introduce a notion of 2-injectivity, a categorified analogue of the injectivity condition for matrix product states.

papers.title: Quantum Robustness via Sandwiched R\'enyi Divergences
papers.abstract: If a quantum state is known only approximately, how much can the expectation of an observable change? We answer with the worst-case expectation over all states within a sandwiched R\'enyi divergence budget of a reference state, for every order $\alpha \in [1/2,\infty]$. Convex duality gives this value as a one-dimensional optimization over a sandwiched Schatten norm, running from a fidelity risk at $\alpha = 1/2$, through the entropic risk at $\alpha = 1$, to a quantum conditional value-at-risk at $\alpha = \infty$. The main result is a classicalization theorem: the quantum problem coincides with the classical one for a probability measure $\omega_\alpha$ on the spectral interval of the observable, constructed from Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure and given by Stahl's theorem at $\alpha = 1$. The Hoeffding, Bernstein and Markov--Krein bounds of classical probability thereby apply to the quantum problem, and yield Pinsker-type inequalities with Bernstein-type refinements. The measure $\omega_\alpha$ is the Born measure only at $\alpha = 1/2$; for $\alpha > 1/2$, noncommutativity of the observable with the state strictly lowers its variance below the Born variance, and with it every variance-sensitive bound: a quantum deflation.

papers.title: Clique Constraints for Exact Causal Structure Learning
papers.authors: Xiaoyu He, Pavel Ryt\'i\v{r}, Petr Ry\v{s}av\'y, Jakub Mare\v{c}ek
papers.abstract: Exact score-based causal structure learning supports explicit structural constraints and optimisation certificates, but its branch-and-cut search can be computationally demanding. We augment exact causal structure learning methods with an upper bound on the maximum clique size of the learned undirected skeleton, enforced at integer candidates through lazy cycle and clique constraints. On static linear-Gaussian Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi and scale-free DAGs, we evaluate callback order, alternative clique-cut policies, incumbent repair, fractional separation, and Big-M bounds. We report causal-recovery metrics jointly with optimality gaps, primal and dual bounds, node throughput, MIPSOL events, and callback cost. Two variants receive particular attention: B3 selects the most violated minimal (k+1)-clique inequality at each callback, whereas C3 repairs an infeasible integer candidate by deleting violating edges and refitting affected regression columns using QR-based least squares. The results do not indicate that clique constraints uniformly accelerate optimisation. However, their benefit depends on graph density, sample size, and cut-management policy, while large collections of correlated constraints can reduce node throughput. Tighter valid Big-M bounds reduced the fixed-budget optimality gap in most tested settings, without necessarily changing SHD or F1 at a fixed time limit. These findings characterize the computational trade-offs of clique-constrained exact causal learning, and identify selective separation and incumbent repair as promising directions.

papers.title: Succinct Infinite-Horizon Lyapunov and LQR Value Problems Are BQP-Complete
papers.abstract: Fundamental tasks in linear systems analysis and control require evaluating infinite-horizon output energies for autonomous systems and optimal value functions for controlled systems. These quantities are characterized by Lyapunov and algebraic Riccati equations, respectively. In this work, we study promise problems for their evaluation when the system matrices are sparse and represented succinctly by Boolean circuits specifying their nonzero entries, with input length polynomial in the logarithm of the system dimension. For dissipative autonomous systems with coordinate-vector initial states, we define the succinct Lyapunov value problem (SLV). Its extension to linear-quadratic optimal control is the succinct LQR value problem (SLQRV). We prove that SLV is $\BQP$-hard: every problem in bounded-error quantum polynomial time ($\BQP$) reduces to it in polynomial time. We then establish that the more general SLQRV problem admits a quantum algorithm running in time polynomial in the succinct input length. Since SLV is a special case of SLQRV, both problems are $\BQP$-complete. Consequently, unless bounded-error probabilistic polynomial time coincides with $\BQP$, no classical randomized algorithm can solve either problem on all promised instances in time polynomial in the succinct input length.

papers.title: A Hoare Logic for Continuous-Time Stochastic Processes
papers.abstract:
Programming language researchers have developed a wide array of tools to reason about probabilistic programs, but it remains unclear how to apply these proof techniques to continuous-time stochastic processes. To bridge this gap, we propose a verification method for properties of continuous-time stochastic processes by reasoning about them as standard programs.
  To demonstrate our approach, we define a continuous semantics for a probabilistic imperative language $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$ by taking the Kuratowski limit of the standard semantics, which collects limit points of the standard program semantics as the time-step approaches zero. Then, we present a Hoare-style logic that uses loop invariants and decreasing functions to verify properties of continuous programs. To establish soundness, we identify a broad class of assertions that are preserved from the standard semantics to the continuous semantics. To demonstrate our approach, we verify properties of ten continuous-time stochastic processes modeled in $\mathrm{pWhile}^{\mathrm{dt}}$, including variants of Brownian motion and a stochastic hybrid system.

papers.title: Unified architecture for arbitrary two-qubit gates with neutral atoms
papers.authors: Nader Mostaan, Peter Schmelcher, Rick Mukherjee
papers.abstract: We propose a unified architecture for two-qubit gates in neutral-atom quantum processors which allows the implementation of the complete set of two-qubit gates. Our approach rests on a single resource that unlocks the entire gate set: an XXZ interaction with tunable anisotropy, combined only with single-qubit operations. We introduce a Rydberg-atom realization of the tunable XXZ interaction and combine it with optimally controlled global microwave pulses to implement the B, QFT, iSWAP, and $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates, as well as a continuous gate family interpolating from CZ to iSWAP via the B gate. This work allows the implementation of any two-qubit gate natively in neutral-atom platforms, enabling flexible switching between instruction sets to reduce circuit depth and compilation overhead in quantum algorithm implementation.

papers.title: Global Green-Schwarz response on quaternionic sphere bundles
papers.abstract: Local anomaly polynomials describe local variations, but a normalized Green-Schwarz phase also depends on global background data. We explain this dependence for ten-dimensional three-sphere bundles of quaternionic lines over closed spin seven-manifolds. The backgrounds retain two specified $\mathrm{Spin}(16)$ gauge bundles and an integral differential trivialization on the base, including its boundary identifications. The trivialized class is the sum of half the first Pontryagin class of the tangent bundle and the second Chern class of the quaternionic line's underlying complex bundle. For these backgrounds, the calculation combines a generally nonzero local Green-Schwarz integral with a real eta invariant evaluated by a twelve-dimensional Atiyah-Patodi-Singer filling. Together, these terms determine an integral relative characteristic number; the additive response is one third of that number, modulo integers. When the base's third and fourth rational cohomology groups vanish, the response equals eight times the Crowley-Goette invariant, without assuming that the base is simply connected. A calibration using the actual quaternionic line bundle gives additive value one third on $\mathrm{Sp}(2)$, recovering the known third-root phase. Distinct integral String data on one fixed ten-manifold give all three phase values, showing which global background information the response can detect. The physical identifications retain their prescribed fermion data, while the separate application to integral topological modular forms and vertex operator superalgebras requires compatible integral lifts. The response calculation constructs neither a microscopic realization nor an equivalence of complete theories.

papers.title: DreamLander: A 6-DOF World Model based Reinforcement Learning Planetary Lander
papers.authors: George Nehma, Patrick Quinn, Madhur Tiwari, Camilo Riano-Rios
papers.abstract: Soft powered descent landings are becoming evermore important in the field of space exploration and scientific advancement, because of their ability to deliver mission critical payloads, both highly accurately and safely. The high efficiency restriction on planetary landings due to the severely limited fuel supply results in the need for optimal guidance trajectories and control. Model based reinforcement learning is proving to be an important tool in simplifying the highly complex process of generating optimal guidance trajectories and control. In this work, we present DreamLander, a state of the art model based reinforcement learning algorithm based on DreamerV3, to generate optimal guidance and control for a realistic 6 degree of freedom entry descent landing problem. The model based approach creates a sample efficient and highly generalizable model that can be applied to a variety of scenarios whilst maintaining a high degree of accuracy, landing within 2 meters of the designated landing zone, and with velocity norm less than 0.3 meters per second. DreamLander makes use of state sensor observations, making progress toward End-to-End solutions of the Entry Descent Landing problem.

papers.title: Topologically transitive semigroup actions of real linear fractional transformations
papers.abstract: Let $F_I=\{f:I\to I \mid f(x)=(Ax+B)/(Cx+D),\ AD-BC\neq 0\}$, where $I$ is a proper closed subinterval of $\mathbb{R}$. We describe all pairs $f,g\in F_I$ for which the action of the semigroup $\langle f,g \rangle$ generated by $f$ and $g$ is topologically transitive on $I$. It turns out that for such pairs topological transitivity, hypercyclicity, and density of every interior orbit are equivalent. Using the Hilbert metric of $I$ we show that no subsemigroup of $F_I$, with any number of generators, acts in a weakly topologically mixing way on $I$. We classify the pairs of affine maps of $\mathbb{R}$ whose semigroup action is topologically transitive, weakly topologically mixing, or hypercyclic, and we show that such an action is never $3$-transitive. In contrast, there are pairs of real linear fractional transformations whose semigroup action on $\mathbb{R}$ is topologically $3$-transitive, while no semigroup of linear fractional transformations is $4$-transitive.

papers.title: A Totient Function Inequality
papers.abstract: An unconditional inequality of the totient function is contributed to the literature. This result is associated with various problems about the distribution of prime numbers.

papers.title: The Douglas property for multiplier algebras of operators
papers.abstract: For a collection of reproducing kernels k which includes those for the Hardy space of the polydisk and ball and for the Bergman space, k is a complete Pick kernel if and only if the multiplier algebra of the Hilbert space H^2(k) associated to k has the Douglas property. Consequences for solving the operator equation AX=Y are examined.

papers.title: Triangle Tiling: The case $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$
papers.abstract:
An $N$-tiling of triangle $ABC$ by triangle $T$ (the ``tile'') is a way of writing $ABC$ as a union of $N$ copies of $T$ overlapping only at their boundaries. Let the tile $T$ have angles $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, and sides $(a,b,c)$. This paper takes up the case when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$. Then there are (as was already known) exactly five possible shapes of $ABC$ not similar to $T$: either $ABC$ is isosceles with base angles $\alpha$, $\beta$, or $\alpha+\beta$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$, or the angles of $ABC$ are $(2\alpha, \alpha, 2\beta)$. We prove that the tile is rational (the ratios of its sides are rational). We then exhibit several families of previously unknown tilings. We also exhibit, for each shape, a Diophantine equation in $N$ and the parameters of the tile that must have a solution whenever there is a tiling of some triangle of that shape.
  By means of these Diophantine equations, some conclusions about the possible values of $N$ are drawn. We prove, for example, that there is no $N$-tiling with $N$ prime when $3\alpha + 2\beta = \pi$, for three of the five shapes; that question remains open for the shape $(2\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta)$ and for isosceles triangles with base angles $\beta$. These equations also imply that for each $N$, there is a finite set of possibilities for the tile $(a,b,c)$ and the triangle $ABC$. (Usually, but not always, there is just one possible tile.) For each of the five shapes, we give a construction method that works under certain sufficient conditions, but there remain values of $N$ that satisfy our necessary conditions and for which we do not know whether a tiling exists. All results have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Sharp double logarithmic $L^\infty$ bounds for second-order Sobolev functions in dimension four
papers.abstract:
Although $W^{2,2}(\mathbb{R}^{4})$ does not embed into $L^\infty$, we prove that radial symmetry allows the $L^\infty$ norm to be controlled by the homogeneous Sobolev seminorm $\dot H^2$, at the cost of a logarithmic correction involving a stronger H\"older-type norm.
  Our main result is a sharp double-logarithmic inequality with optimal leading constant $1/(8\pi^2\alpha)$. We also establish a single-logarithmic estimate and prove the sharpness of its threshold. The optimal lower bound is derived by analysing a biharmonic obstacle problem with H\"older-type obstacle. A tailored penalization argument yields existence, uniqueness, and regularity of the minimizer, while an explicit transcendental equation for the free-boundary radius determines the sharp constant through its asymptotic behavior.
  These results provide fourth-order, four-dimensional analogues of the two-dimensional first-order inequalities of Ibrahim--Majdoub--Masmoudi (\textit{Proc.\ Amer.\ Math.\ Soc.}, 2007), with potential applications to fourth-order semilinear evolution equations with exponential nonlinearities.

papers.title: Emerging of massive gauge particles in inhomogeneous local gauge transformations
papers.abstract: A generalized theory of gauge transformations is presented on the basis of the covariant Hamiltonian formalism of field theory, for which the covariant canonical field equations are equivalent to the Euler-Lagrange field equations. Similar to the canonical transformation theory of point dynamics, the canonical transformation rules for fields are derived from generating functions. Thus---in contrast to the usual Lagrangian description---the covariant canonical transformation formalism automatically ensures the mappings to preserve the action principle, and hence to be {\em physical}. On that basis, we work out the theory of inhomogeneous local gauge transformations that generalizes the conventional local SU(N) gauge transformation theory. It is shown that massive gauge bosons naturally emerge in this description, which thus could supersede the Higgs mechanism.

papers.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.

papers.title: Trees in Random Sparse Graphs with a Given Degree Sequence
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ be the set of graphs $G(V,\, E)$ with $\left|V\right|=n$, and the degree sequence equal to $D=(d_{1},\, d_{2},\,\dots,\, d_{n})$. In addition, for $\frac{1}{2}<a<1$, we define the set of graphs with an almost given degree sequence $D$ as follows, \[ \mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}:=\cup\,\mathbb{G}^{\bar{D}}, \] where the union is over all degree sequences $\bar{D}$ such that, for $1\leq i\leq n$, we have $\left|d_{i}-\bar{d}_{i}\right|<d_{i}^{a}$.
  Now, if we chose random graphs $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ uniformly out of the sets $\mathbb{G}^{D}$ and $\mathbb{G}_{a}^{D}$, respectively, what do they look like? This has been studied when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is a dense graph, i.e. $\left|E\right|=\Theta(n^{2})$, in the sense of graphons, or when $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ is very sparse, i.e. $d_{n}^{2}=o(\left|E\right|)$. In the case of sparse graphs with an almost given degree sequence, we investigate this question, and give the finite tree subgraph structure of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{a}}\left(D\right)$ under some mild conditions. For the random graph $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{g}}\left(D\right)$ with a given degree sequence, we re-derive the finite tree structure in dense and very sparse cases to give a continuous picture.
  Moreover, for a pair of vectors $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n_{1}}\times\mathbb{Z}^{n_{2}}$, we let $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ be the random bipartite graph that is chosen uniformly out of the set $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$, where $\mathbb{G}^{D_{1},D_{2}}$ is the set of all bipartite graphs with the degree sequence $\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$. We are able to show the result for $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbf{b}}\left(D_{1},D_{2}\right)$ without any further conditions.

papers.title: Estimates for the Number of Solutions of Algebraic Diophantine Equations: From the Circle Method to the Manin Conjecture
papers.abstract: This work continues the research of the author on estimates for the number of solutions of algebraic diophantine equations by means of the circle method and develops this line in the geometric direction, towards counting integral points on log Fano varieties. It consists of two parts. Part 1 is the corrected version of the previous work. For diagonal equations $c_1x^{k_1} +...+c_sx^{k_s} = n$ with natural coefficients, upper asymptotic estimates for the number of natural solutions in the range $s \leq 2^k$, where the classical asymptotics is not applicable, are obtained by the circle method and the Hua lemma. The estimates are refined for $s = 2,3,4$ and various $k_i$; in the range $s > 2^k$ they agree with the classical ones. Part 2 develops the same line: from counting solutions of equations to counting integral points on log Fano varieties, where the circle method fails because of insuf ficient dimension. In the log case, the product in the Peyre constant diverges as a harmonic series. A method of analytic compensation is introduced that cancels the divergent term and returns the problem to the range of applicability of the standard scheme. The main result is a method for computing the Peyre log constant with guar anteed accuracy and certified intervals for the number of integral points whenever an estimate of the remainder of the asymptotics is known. The log constant is computable unconditionally, without the Manin conjecture; the conjecture is needed only to interpret it as the leading term of the asymptotics. An experimental verification for the algebraic torus and the Fermat cubic surface is presented.

papers.title: Maximal Non-commuting Sets in Certain Unipotent Upper-triangular Linear Groups
papers.authors: C. P. Anil Kumar, S. K. Prajapati
papers.abstract:
Let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a set of pairwise non-commuting elements of a group $G$. We determine $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$, where $UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q)$ is the group of $4	imes 4$ unipotent upper-triangular matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, in terms of a classical invariant of finite geometry: we prove that \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+1+
u(q), \] where $
u(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of the symplectic generalized quadrangle $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$ disjoint from a fixed line. We show that $
u(q)=q^2$ for even $q$ and $
u(q)=\mu(q)$ for odd $q$, where $\mu(q)$ is the largest size of a partial ovoid of $\mathrm{W}(3,q)$. Consequently $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3+q^2-q+1$ for even $q$, while for odd $q$ we obtain $q^3+2q-1\le \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))\le q^3+q^2-2q+2$; the upper bound rests on a self-contained proof of the inequality $\mu(q)\le q^2-q+1$. In particular $\omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))$ is not a polynomial in $q$, not even for large $q$. This corrects Theorem~$A$ of the published version of this paper, where the value $q^3+q+1+\omega(\mathcal{M})$ was claimed. We also study the non-commuting structures $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ introduced there: we prove that $\omega(\mathcal{M})=q(q-1)$ for even $q$, that $\omega(\mathcal{Q})=\mu(q)-1$ for all $q$, and that for odd $q$ a non-commuting set in $\mathcal{Q}$ consisting of almost $m$ lines exists only for $m\le 5$. Exact values for small $q$ and a list of open problems and conjectures are included. Consequently for odd $q$ \[ \omega(UU_4(\mathbb{F}_q))=q^3-q+2+\omega(\mathcal{Q}). \]

papers.title: The finite volume method on Sierpi\'nski simplices
papers.abstract: In the sequel, we extend the Strichartz average approach for the Laplacian, which uses average values of a function over basic sets, rather than pointwise ones as classically done in the literature, and goes back to the seminal work of~S.~Kusuoka and~X.~Y.~Zhou, to Sierpi\'{n}ski Simplices. To our knowledge, the finite volume method had not been applied before to fractals themselves, with their intrinsic Laplacian. We build the finite volume scheme for the heat equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions, give its consistency error, a stability condition of Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy type, obtained by means of an inclusion between the spectrum of the finite volume matrix and the one of the graph Laplacian, and prove the convergence of the scheme. Numerical results are given in the case of the Sierpi\'{n}ski Gasket and Tetrahedron, and compared with the finite difference method.

papers.title: A note on polynomial sequences modulo integers (revised version)
papers.abstract: For a real polynomial $P(x)$ we study the integer sequence $\lambda(P)=(\lfloor P(k) \rfloor)_{k\ge1}$ modulo integers. We show that for nonlinear $P$ the sequence $\lambda(P)$ is uniformly distributed (u.d.) in $\mathbb{Z}$ if and only if $P$ has an irrational coefficient other than the constant term. In fact, if all non-constant coefficients of a nonlinear $P$ are rational, then $\lambda(P)$ fails to be u.d.\ modulo every prime in a set of primes of positive density. We also study completeness: $P$ is complete modulo $m$ if $\lfloor P(x) \rfloor$ meets every residue class modulo $m$. For $P$ of even degree we prove that $\lambda(P)$ meets every residue class modulo every integer if and only if $P$ has an irrational non-constant coefficient. The same holds for every polynomial $P(x)=ax^n+c$ with $n\ge2$, and for every nonlinear $P$ with $P(x)-P(0)\in\mathbb{Z}[x]$. For linear $P$, both properties are characterized completely, and the two notions differ.

papers.title: Tiling an Equilateral Triangle
papers.abstract:
Let $ABC$ be an equilateral triangle. For certain triangles $T$ (the ``tile'') and certain $N$, it is possible to cut $ABC$ into $N$ copies of $T$. It is known that only certain shapes of $T$ are possible, but until now very little was known about the possible values of $N$. Here we prove that for $N>3$,
  $N$ cannot be prime, and study more closely the possible
  tilings when the tile has a $\pi/3$ angle.
  All theorems have been formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Plethora of cluster structures on $GL_n$
papers.authors: Misha Gekhtman, Michael Shapiro, Alek Vainshtein
papers.abstract: We continue the study of multiple cluster structures in the rings of regular functions on $GL_n$, $SL_n$ and $\operatorname{Mat}_n$ that are compatible with Poisson-Lie and Poisson-homogeneous structures. According to our initial conjecture, each class in the Belavin-Drinfeld classification of Poisson--Lie structures on a semisimple complex group $\mathcal G$ corresponds to a cluster structure in $\mathcal O(\mathcal G)$. Here we prove this conjecture for a large subset of Belavin-Drinfeld (BD) data of $A_n$ type, which includes all the previously known examples. Namely, we subdivide all possible $A_n$ type BD data into oriented and non-oriented kinds. In the oriented case, we single out BD data satisfying a certain combinatorial condition that we call aperiodicity and prove that for any BD data of this kind there exists a regular cluster structure compatible with the corresponding Poisson-Lie bracket. In fact, we extend the aperiodicity condition to pairs of oriented BD data and prove a more general result that establishes an existence of a regular cluster structure on $SL_n$ compatible with a Poisson bracket homogeneous with respect to the right and left action of two copies of $SL_n$ equipped with two different Poisson-Lie brackets. If the aperiodicity condition is not satisfied, a compatible cluster structure has to be replaced with a generalized cluster structure. We will address this situation in future publications.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the numbers $h^{0,p}(X)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be derived equivalent smooth projective varieties over the field of complex numbers. We prove that the numbers $h^{0,p}(X_1)$ and $h^{0,p}(X_2)$ are equal for any $p$.

papers.title: Ratio of tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents
papers.abstract: We consider the tiling generating functions of semi-hexagons and quartered hexagons with dents on their sides. In general, there are no simple product formulas for these generating functions. However, we show that the modification in the regions' width changes the tiling generating functions by only a simple multiplicative factor.

papers.title: $(G,\mu)$-Windows and Deformations of $(G,\mu)$-Displays
papers.abstract: Let $k_0$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, let $G$ be a smooth affine group scheme over $\mathbb{Z}_p$, and let $\mu$ be a cocharacter of $G_{W(k_0)}$ such that the set of $\mu$-weights of $\Lie G$ is a subset of $\{-1,0,1,2,\dots\}$. We prove that the groupoid of adjoint nilpotent $(G,\mu)$-displays as in \cite[Definition 1.0.1]{pappas}, \cite{lau2} and \cite[Definition 3.16]{E7} is equivalent to the groupoid of $(G,\mu)$-windows, which are the generalizations of windows as in \cite[Definition 5.1]{langer2} and \cite[Definition 3.3.1]{E7}.

papers.title: The Frobenius Problem for Generalized Repunit Numerical Semigroups
papers.authors: Manuel B. Branco, Isabel Cola\c{c}o, Ignacio Ojeda
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the numerical semigroups generated by $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots \} \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_1$ is the repunit number in base $b > 1$ of length $n > 1$ and $a_i - a_{i-1} = a\, b^{i-2},$ for every $i \geq 2$, where $a$ is a positive integer relatively prime with $a_1$. These numerical semigroups generalize the repunit numerical semigroups among many others. We show that they have interesting properties such as being homogeneous and Wilf. Moreover, we solve the Frobenius problem for this family, by giving a closed formula for the Frobenius number in terms of $a, b$ and $n$, and compute other usual invariants such as the Ap\'ery sets, the genus or the type.

papers.title: Integer factorization as subset-sum problem
papers.abstract: This paper elaborates on a sieving technique that has first been applied in 2018 for improving bounds on deterministic integer factorization. We will generalize the sieve in order to obtain a polynomial-time reduction from integer factorization to a specific instance of the multiple-choice subset-sum problem. As an application, we will improve upon special purpose factorization algorithms for integers composed of divisors with small difference. In particular, we will refine the runtime complexity of Fermat's factorization algorithm by a large subexponential factor. Our first procedure is deterministic, rigorous, easy to implement and has negligible space complexity. Our second procedure is heuristically faster than the first, but has non-negligible space complexity.

papers.title: Foliated and compactly supported isotopies of tubular neighborhoods
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a foliation with a "singular" submanifold $\Sigma$ on a smooth manifold $A$ and $p:E \to \Sigma$ be a tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in $A$. Under certain "scalability" assumptions on $\mathcal{F}$ near $\Sigma$, we prove that every leaf preserving diffeomorphism $h$ of $A$ is isotopic via a leaf preserving isotopy to a diffeomorphism which coincides with some vector bundle morphism of $E$ near $\Sigma$. This result is simultaneously a foliated, compactly supported and parametrized variant of a well known statement that every diffeomorphism $h$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ fixing the origin is isotopic to the linear isomorphism induced by its Jacobi matrix at $0$. Particular cases of such a "linearization theorem" allowed recently to compute homotopy types of leaf preserving diffeomorphism groups of polar Morse-Bott foliations on lens spaces and the twisted bundle $S^2\tilde{\times}S^1$.
  In general, that "linearization theorem" can be used to reduce the study of the homotopy type of the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $\mathcal{F}$ to an investigation of the following three groups (being independent in a certain sense): (a) diffeomorphism group of $\Sigma$, (b) the group of leaf preserving vector bundle isomorphisms of $E$, and (c) the group of leaf preserving diffeomorphisms of $A$ supported in $A\setminus \Sigma$, i.e. out of the "singularity" $\Sigma$.

papers.title: Doubly Sequenceable Groups
papers.abstract: Given a sequence ${\bf g}: g_0,\dots,g_m$ in a finite group $G$ with $g_0=1_G$, let $\bar{\bf g}:\bar g_0,\dots,\bar g_m$ be the sequence of consecutive quotients of $\bf g$, defined by $\bar g_0=1_G$ and $\bar g_i=g_{i-1}^{-1}g_i$ for $1\le i\le m$. We say that $G$ is \emph{doubly sequenceable} if there exists a sequence $\bf g$ in $G$ such that every element of $G$ appears exactly twice in each of $\bf g$ and $\bar{\bf g}$; such a sequence is \emph{cyclic} if its last term is $1_G$. We show that every group that is abelian, of odd order, sequenceable, R-sequenceable, or terraced has a cyclic double sequencing, and that a group is terraced if and only if it has a palindromic cyclic double sequencing. We show that if $H$ is a group of odd order or a sequenceable group and $K$ is an abelian group, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing. We also show that if $H$ has a cyclic double sequencing and $K$ is an abelian group with no direct summand of order $2$, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing, and we extend this to terraced groups $H$ and abelian groups $K$ with at most six direct summands of order $2$. Consequently, complete double Latin squares exist for every order, and the double sequencing conjecture holds for all groups of order at most $87$ except possibly $64$, and for all sufficiently large groups.

papers.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
papers.authors: Hari Bercovici, Yu Kitagawa, Ping Zhong
papers.abstract: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $\mu_{X_1}$ and $\mu_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $\mu_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.

papers.title: On Noetherianity of tensor modules and homology of subalgebras of vector fields
papers.authors: Boris Feigin, Alexei Kanel-Belov, Anton Khoroshkin
papers.abstract: We show that finite tensor products $\otimes_{i=1}^{r}\mathcal{T}_{\lambda}$ of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Moreover, the Hilbert series of their graded submodules are rational functions whose denominators are products of factors of the form $(1-t^m)$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2d}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U(\vir)/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.

papers.title: Convergence Analysis of an Upwind Finite-Difference Scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
papers.authors: Daisuke Inoue, Nao Hamamuki, Yuji Ito, Takahito Kashiwabara, Norikazu Saito, Hiroaki Yoshida
papers.abstract: We study the convergence of an upwind finite-difference scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on a one-dimensional periodic domain, considering both the value function and the feedback control selected by the discrete pointwise minimization. For classical value functions whose time and spatial derivatives are H\"older continuous in their respective variables, we bound the error at the grid points by a constant times the sum of the time step and spatial mesh width each raised to their common H\"older exponent. This yields first-order convergence when these derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and the meshes are refined proportionally. Under additional spatial regularity of the problem data, we also prove convergence of both one-sided difference quotients of the discrete value function to the spatial derivative of the value function: the integral over space and time of the absolute error tends to zero for each difference quotient. We further establish convergence of the discrete controls to the continuous feedback control when the continuous pointwise minimizer is unique, regardless of how the discrete minimizers are selected. These theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the accuracy of the value-function approximation and the behavior of the computed feedback controls.

papers.title: Berndt-Type Integrals and Series Associated with Ramanujan and Jacobi Elliptic Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we evaluate in closed forms two families of infinite integrals containing hyperbolic and trigonometric functions in their integrands. We call them Berndt-type integrals since he initiated the study of similar integrals. We first establish explicit evaluations of four classes of hyperbolic sums by special values of the Gamma function, by two completely different approaches, which extend those sums considered by Ramanujan and Zucker previously. We discover the first by refining two results of Ramanujan concerning some $q$-series. For the second we compare both the Fourier series expansions and the Maclaurin series expansions of a few Jacobi elliptic functions. Next, by contour integrations we convert two families of Berndt-type integrals to the above hyperbolic sums, all of which can be evaluated in closed forms. We then discover explicit formulas for one of the two families. Throughout the paper we present many examples which enable us to formulate a conjectural explicit formula for the other family of the Berndt-type integrals at the end.

papers.title: Automorphic line measures in the half-plane and the Grand Riemann Hypothesis
papers.abstract: Poincare-type series, such as Selberg's, are known to produce automorphic functions, in the hyperbolic half-plane, the decompositions of which into eigenfunctions (genuine or generalized) of the automorphic Laplacian contain all modular forms of nonholomorphic type. We introduce a one-parameter family of explicit automorphic measures supported by discrete unions of congruent lines with the same property, except for one value of the real parameter, for which they miss exactly the Eisenstein series associated to non-trivial zeros of zeta, and the Hecke eigenforms the $L$-functions associated to which vanish as $\frac{1}{2}$. The Grand Riemann Hypothesis, a special case of which needs being analyzed, is disproved

papers.title: Universally free numerical semigroups
papers.authors: Ignacio Garc\'ia Marco, Pedro A. Garc\'ia-S\'anchez, Ignacio Ojeda, Christos Tatakis
papers.abstract:
A numerical semigroup is said to be universally free if it is free for any possible arrangement of its minimal generating set. In this work, we establish that toric ideals associated with universally free numerical semigroups can be generated by their set of circuits. Additionally, we provide a characterization of universally free numerical semigroups in terms of Gr\"obner bases. Specifically, a numerical semigroup is universally free if and only if all initial ideals of its corresponding toric ideal are complete intersections. Furthermore, we establish several equalities among the toric bases of a universally free numerical semigroup.
  We provide a complete characterization of $3$-generated universally free numerical semigroups in terms of their minimal generating sets, and by proving the equality of certain toric bases. We compute exactly all the toric bases of a toric ideal defined by a 3-generated universally free numerical semigroup. Notably, we answer some questions posed by Tatakis and Thoma by demonstrating that toric ideals defined by $3$-generated universally free numerical semigroups have a set of circuits and a universal Gr\"obner basis of size 3, while the universal Markov basis and the Graver basis can be arbitrarily large. We present partial results and propose several conjectures regarding universally free numerical semigroups with more than three generators.

papers.title: Doubly Free-Boundary Rail-Yard Dimers and Annular Gaussian Fluctuations
papers.abstract: We study rail-yard dimer models with free boundaries at both ends. The double free-boundary geometry introduces infinitely many reflected Cauchy factors into partition functions and contour formulas for height Laplace observables. For admissible piecewise periodic weights satisfying the stated separation conditions, we prove a Laplace-transform law of large numbers and obtain a limit shape through weak convergence of slope measures. For $\beta=1$, under the stated regularity and nonexceptional endpoint conditions, we derive a necessary real double-root condition for the frozen boundary. We also prove Gaussian fluctuations of centered height Laplace observables, with covariance determined by an annular reflected-image kernel expressed through theta functions. Finally, we construct an exact growth-diagram sampler for finite reflected truncations and prove that their laws converge in total variation to the full Gibbs measure on every fixed rail-yard graph with finitely many columns as the truncation level tends to infinity.

papers.title: On the rigidity of Ricci shrinkers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the rigidity of the generalized cylinder $N^n \times \mathbb R^{m-n}$, or a quotient thereof, in the space of Ricci shrinkers equipped with the pointed-Gromov-Hausdorff topology. Here, $N$ is a stable Einstein manifold that has an obstruction of order $3$. The proof is based on a quantitative characterization of the rigidity of compact Ricci shrinkers, a rigidity inequality of mixed orders on generalized cylinders, and the method of contraction and extension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of the tangent flow for general compact Ricci flows under the assumption that one tangent flow is a generalized cylinder.

papers.title: An Eilenberg-Watts Theorem and Morita localization for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories
papers.abstract: Hilbert modules over a $C^*$-category were first defined by Mitchener, who also proved that they form a $C^*$-category. An Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-algebras was proved by Blecher. We follow a similar path to prove an Eilenberg-Watts theorem for Hilbert modules over $C^*$-categories and characterize equivalences of categories of Hilbert modules as being given by tensoring with imprimitivity bimodules. We employ our results to prove several equivalences of bicategories of $C^*$-algebras and $C^*$-categories, and to exhibit a Morita localization of the category of locally small $C^*$-categories.

papers.title: The Geometric Deformation of Curved $L_\infty$ Algebras and Lie Algebroids
papers.abstract: While $L_\infty$ algebras are fundamental structures in differential geometry and mathematical physics, the geometric information encoded in such structures is often implicit. We address the following question: What constitutes a geometrically meaningful deformation of an $L_\infty$ algebra arising from vector bundles, and how can such deformations classify new geometric invariants? Inspired by nonabelian extension theory of Lie algebras, we define geometric deformations of curved $L_\infty$ algebras constructed from a vector bundle $V\to M$, and demonstrate that such deformations uniquely correspond to Lie algebroid structures on $V$. Explicit computations reveal that a representative of the first Atiyah-Chern class is exact in the total Weil complex, with its primitive representing the modular class in Lie algebroid cohomology. In the case of action Lie algebroids, the leading-order Atiyah-Chern classes correspond to the equivariant Chern characters. Applications to BV theories show that the geometric deformations naturally generate Poisson sigma models. These results provide a coherent framework for deriving field theories from geometric deformations of $L_\infty$ algebras.

papers.title: On the limit of simply connected manifolds with discrete isometric cocompact group actions
papers.abstract:
We study the fundamental group of the equivariant Gromov--Hausdorff limit space \[ (M_i, p_i, G_i) \xrightarrow{eGH} (Y, p, G), \] where $\{(M_i,p_i)\}_{i\in\mathbb N}$ is a sequence of complete, connected, and simply connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with $\mathrm{Ric}\ge -(n-1)$. Here $G_i\subset \mathrm{Iso}(M_i)$ is a discrete subgroup satisfying $\mathrm{diam}(M_i/G_i)\le D$ for some fixed constant $D>0$.
  Let $G_0$ denote the identity component of $G$. Then $G_0$ is a nilpotent Lie group. Let $T^k \subseteq G_0$ be the maximal torus.
  Our main result asserts that the quotient space $Y/T^k$ is simply connected. Moreover, the fundamental group $\pi_1(Y,p)$ is generated, up to conjugation, by loops contained in $T^k$-orbits. More precisely, each generator can be represented by a loop of the form \begin{equation*} \gamma = \alpha \cdot \beta \cdot \alpha^{-1}, \end{equation*} where $\alpha$ is a curve from $p$ to some point $y \in Y$, and $\beta$ is a loop based at $y$ that lies entirely in the $T^k$-orbit of $y$.

papers.title: Hilbert number for a family of piecewise nonautonomous equations
papers.authors: J. L. Bravo, M. Fern\'andez, I. Ojeda
papers.abstract: For family $x'=(a_0+a_1\cos t+a_2\sin t)|x|+b_0+b_1\cos t+b_2\sin t$, we solve three basic problems related with its dynamics. First, we characterize when it has a center (Poincar\'e center focus problem). Second, we show that each equation has a finite number of limit cycles (finiteness problem), and finally we give a uniform upper bound for the number of limit cycles (Hilbert problem 16).

papers.title: On the depth of simplicial affine semigroup rings
papers.abstract: We recall and delve into the different characterizations of the depth of an affine semigroup ring, providing an original characterization of depth two in three and four dimensional cases which are closely related to the existence of a maximal element in certain Apery sets.

papers.title: Calligraphs and sphere realizations
papers.authors: Matteo Gallet, Georg Grasegger, Niels Lubbes, Josef Schicho
papers.abstract: We introduce a recursive procedure for computing the number of realizations of a minimally rigid graph on the sphere up to rotations. We accomplish this by combining two ingredients. The first is a framework that allows us to think of such realizations as of elements of a moduli space of stable rational curves with marked points. The second is the idea of splitting a minimally rigid graph into two subgraphs, called calligraphs, that admit one degree of freedom and that share only a single edge and a further vertex. This idea has been recently employed for realizations of graphs in the plane up to isometries. The key result is that we can associate to a calligraph a triple of natural numbers with a special property: whenever a minimally rigid graph is split into two calligraphs, the number of realizations of the former equals the product of the two triples of the latter, where this product is specified by a fixed quadratic form. These triples and quadratic form codify the fact that we express realizations as intersections of two curves on the blowup of a sphere along two pairs of complex conjugate points.

papers.title: Data-proximal null-space networks for inverse problems
papers.authors: J\"urgen Frikel, Simon G\"oppel, Markus Haltmeier
papers.abstract: Inverse problems with incomplete data are severely ill-posed and require regularization. Learned reconstructions incorporate prior information effectively, but their regularization properties are less well understood than those of classical variational methods. We propose data-proximal null-space networks, which post-process an initial reconstruction obtained by a classical regularization method and extend null-space networks by allowing learned corrections that are not restricted to the null space, while bounding their effect on the measured data by a prescribed tolerance. Combined with a convergent, possibly nonlinear regularization method, these networks yield convergent regularization methods with convergence rates and data-proximity bounds. A calmness-based analysis covers fixed networks with radial clipping even when the operator range is not closed; their correction outside the null space vanishes in the limit, so that they differ from null-space networks only at positive noise levels. For the limited-angle Radon transform, exact data consistency preserves the visible singularities of the initial reconstruction, whereas data proximity controls the visible error in a weak Sobolev norm proportional to the data norm, but not its singularities. For compactly supported objects, null-space networks act trivially, whereas data-proximal networks can still correct nearly invisible components. In limited-angle computed tomography, data-proximal networks substantially improve on null-space networks and, unlike residual networks, guarantee a prescribed bound on the data change.

papers.title: Sharp endpoint $L^p$-estimates for bilinear spherical maximal functions
papers.authors: Ankit Bhojak, Surjeet Singh Choudhary, Saurabh Shrivastava, Kalachand Shuin
papers.abstract: In this article, we address endpoint issues for the bilinear spherical maximal function. We obtain borderline restricted weak type estimates for the well studied bilinear spherical maximal function $$\mathfrak{M}(f,g)(x):=\sup_{t>0}\left|\int_{\mathbb S^{2d-1}}f(x-ty_1)g(x-ty_2)\;d\sigma(y_1,y_2)\right|,$$ in dimensions $d=1,2$ and as an application, we deduce sharp endpoint estimates for the multilinear spherical maximal function. We also prove $L^p-$estimates for the local spherical maximal function in all dimensions $d\geq 2$, thus improving the boundedness left open in the work of Jeong and Lee (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfa.2020.108629). We further study necessary conditions for the bilinear maximal function, \[\mathcal M (f,g)(x)=\sup_{t>0}\left|\int_{\mathbb S^{1}}f(x-ty)g(x+ty)\;d\sigma(y)\right|\] to be bounded from $L^{p_1}(\mathbb R^2)\times L^{p_2}(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^2)$ and prove sharp results for a bilinearized version of $\mathcal M$.

papers.title: Heat equation from a deterministic dynamics
papers.authors: Giovanni Canestrari, Carlangelo Liverani, Stefano Olla
papers.abstract: We derive the heat equation for the thermal energy under diffusive space-time scaling for a purely deterministic microscopic dynamics satisfying Newton equations perturbed by an external chaotic force acting like a magnetic field.

papers.title: Arithmetic varieties of numerical semigroups
papers.authors: Manuel B. Branco, Ignacio Ojeda, Jos\'e Carlos Rosales
papers.abstract: In this paper we present the notion of arithmetic variety for numerical semigroups. We study various aspects related to these varieties such as the smallest arithmetic that contains a set of numerical semigroups and we exhibit the root three associated with an arithmetic variety. This tree is not locally finite; however, if the Frobenius number is fixed, the tree has finitely many nodes and algorithms can be developed. All algorithms provided in this article include their (non-debugged) implementation in GAP.

papers.title: On the (In)Compatibility between Group Fairness and Individual Fairness
papers.abstract: We study the compatibility between utility-optimized statistical parity and individual fairness. While individual fairness seeks to treat similar individuals similarly, optimal statistical parity aims to provide similar treatment to individuals who share relative similarity within their respective sensitive groups. Although both fairness perspectives are desirable, they often conflict in practical applications. Our goal in this work is to analyze the existence of this conflict and its potential solution. In particular, we establish sufficient (sharp) conditions for the compatibility between the optimal (post-processing) statistical parity $L^2$ learning and the ($K$-Lipschitz or $(\epsilon,\delta)$) individual fairness requirements. When a conflict arises, we first relax the optimal statistical parity solution to the Pareto frontier, representing the optimal trade-off between $L^2$ error and statistical disparity, and then examine its compatibility with individual fairness. Our analysis identifies regions along the Pareto frontier that satisfy individual fairness constraints. Additionally, we provide individual fairness guarantees for the composition of a trained model with the optimal post-processing step, enabling practitioners to assess the compatibility of post-processed models. This provides practitioners with a principled approach to achieving Pareto-optimal statistical parity while maintaining individual fairness constraints.

papers.title: Metric Multiview Geometry---a Catalogue in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We systematically compile an exhaustive catalogue of multiview varieties and anchored multiview varieties arising from projections of points, lines, and planes in 1, 2, and 3-dimensional projective spaces. We say that two such varieties are ED-equivalent if there is a linear isomorphism between them that preserves ED-critical points. This gives rise to fourteen representatives, at most two of which are equivalent, and we determine various properties---dimension, set-theoretic equations, and multidegrees---for all varieties featured in our catalogue. In the case of points, we also present a complementary study of resectioning varieties and their singular loci. Finally, we propose conjectures for the Euclidean distance degrees of all varieties appearing in our comprehensive compilation.

papers.title: The multiples of a numerical semigroup
papers.abstract: Given two numerical semigroups $S$ and $T$ we say that $T$ is a multiple of $S$ if there exists an integer $d \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$ such that $S = \{x \in \mathbb{N} \mid d x \in T\}$. In this paper we study the family of multiples of a (fixed) numerical semigroup. We also address the open problem of finding numerical semigroups of embedding dimension $e$ without any quotient of embedding dimension less than $e$, and provide new families with this property.

papers.title: On the Drinfeld formal group
papers.abstract: We identify Drinfeld's formal group on the prismatization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$ with a formal group arising from homotopy theory, given locally by the Quillen formal group of a decompleted variant of topological periodic cyclic homology. We also prove that this formal group extends to the syntomization of $\mathrm{Spf}\,\mathbb{Z}_p$, and that it admits a certain algebraization conjectured by Drinfeld.

papers.title: Subgroup Separability of Artin Groups II
papers.abstract: In this short note, we establish a more concrete characterization of subgroup separable (LERF) Artin groups, building on a previously known criterion. Specifically, we prove an Artin group is LERF if and only if its underlying graph does not contain certain induced subgraphs, thus providing a more direct generalization of the Metaftsis-Raptis criterion for RAAGs. Consequently, we prove every LERF Artin group is coherent and obtain a graph condition for coherent Artin groups to be LERF.

papers.title: Differentiation, Taylor series, and all order spectral shift functions, for relatively bounded perturbations
papers.authors: Arup Chattopadhyay, Teun D. H. van Nuland, Chandan Pradhan
papers.abstract: Given $H$ self-adjoint, $V$ symmetric and relatively $H$-bounded, and $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{C}$ satisfying mild conditions, we show that the Gateaux derivative $$\frac{d^n}{dt^n}f(H+tV)|_{t=0}$$ exists in the operator norm topology, for every natural $n$, give a new explicit formula for this derivative in terms of multiple operator integrals, and establish useful perturbation formulas for multiple operator integrals under relatively bounded perturbations. Moreover, if the $H$-bound of $V$ is less than 1, we obtain sufficient conditions on $f$ which ensure that the Taylor expansion $$f(H+V)=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{1}{n!}\frac{d^n}{dt^n} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}$$ exists and converges absolutely in operator norm. Finally, assuming that $V(H-i)^{-p}\in\mathcal{S}^{s/p}$ for $p=1,\ldots,s$ for some $s\in\mathbb{N}$ (for instance, when $H$ is an order 1 differential operator on an $s-1$ dimensional space), we show that the Krein--Koplienko spectral shift functions $\eta_{k,H,V}$, satisfying $${Tr}\left(f(H+V)-\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{m!}\frac{d^m}{dt^m} f(H+tV)\big|_{t=0}\right)=\int_{\mathbb{R}} f^{(k)}(x)\eta_{k,H,V}(x)dx,$$ exist for every $k=1,2,3,\ldots$, independently of $s$. The latter result (which is significantly stronger than \cite{vNS22}) is completely new also in the case that $V$ is bounded. The proof is based on \cite{PSS}, combined with a generalisation of the multiple operator integral compatible with \cite{HMvN}. We discuss applications of our results to quantum physics and noncommutative geometry.

papers.title: Orbit structures and complexity in Schubert and Richardson Varieties
papers.abstract: The goal of this paper is twofold. Firstly, we provide a type-uniform formula for the torus complexity of the usual torus action on a Richardson variety, by developing the notion of algebraic dimensions of Bruhat intervals, strengthening a type $A$ result by Donten-Bury, Escobar and Portakal. In the process, we give an explicit description of the torus action on any Deodhar component as well as describe the root subgroups that comprise the component. Secondly, when a Levi subgroup in a reductive algebraic group acts on a Schubert variety, we exhibit a codimension preserving bijection between the Levi-Borel subgroup (a Borel subgroup in the Levi subgroup) orbits in the big open cell of that Schubert variety and torus orbits in the big open cell of a distinguished Schubert subvariety. This bijection has many applications including a type-uniform formula for the Levi-Borel complexity of the usual Levi-Borel subgroup action on a Schubert variety. We conclude by extending the Levi-Borel complexity results to a large class of Schubert varieties in the partial flag variety.

papers.title: Inventory Control and Storage Design via an $L^{\infty}$-control approach
papers.authors: Madhu Dhiman, Veeraruna Kavitha, Nandyala Hemachandra
papers.abstract:
Inventory control traditionally focuses on pricing and production rates, while physical storage capacity is typically fixed at the initial design stage. This paper addresses this relatively unexplored aspect by formulating a non-standard optimal control problem. The objective combines the classical integral term, capturing inventory-related costs, with an L^\infty-term, representing the maximum inventory level over the planning horizon. We first establish a relationship between the optimal pricing and production-rate policies, reducing the problem's dimensionality. Building on our earlier framework, we establish the existence of an optimal relaxed control and obtain an \epsilon-optimal pure control for the reduced problem through smooth approximation. Numerical solutions of the resulting approximate problem demonstrate a substantial reduction in required storage capacity, with a negligible loss in net revenue (less than 6%), after accounting for shortage, holding, and production costs. We also observe that increasing the weight of the L^\infty-component reduces fluctuations in the inventory trajectory.
  These findings are particularly relevant when future demand information is incomplete or unavailable. In such settings, dynamically adjusting pricing and production policies to keep inventory levels close to zero can substantially reduce storage requirements with only a negligible loss in net revenue. Our results highlight the potential of incorporating inventory-level considerations directly into operational decision-making, particularly when physical storage capacity can be designed flexibly.

papers.title: The principle of relativity in classical nonholonomic mechanics and $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine time-dependent constraints
papers.abstract: We study the principle of relativity in classical time-dependent nonholonomic Lagrangian mechanics from the perspective of moving global reference frames. We also introduce time-dependent $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine constraints, which are natural objects for the invariant formulation of nonholonomic systems with symmetries. As far as the author is aware, the Hamiltonization problem for time-dependent constraints has not yet been studied. As a first step in this direction, we consider a rolling without sliding of a balanced disc of radius $r$ over a vertical circle of a given variable radius $R(t)$. We modify the Chaplygin multiplier method and prove that the reduced system becomes Hamiltonian with respect to the new time.

papers.title: The non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the forced MHD equations
papers.abstract: We construct two distinct Leray solutions of the three-dimensional forced viscous, resistive magnetohydrodynamic equations in the whole space, with zero initial data and identical forcing. Our construction begins with a periodic axisymmetric unstable MHD mode associated with a rotating column and a nonconstant axial magnetic field. The rotating profile is also centrifugally unstable at zero magnetic field; the construction uses an unstable MHD eigenvalue and does not require magnetic destabilization of a hydrodynamically stable flow. Our spectral construction tracks a prescribed unstable MHD eigenvalue under radial truncation, the addition of small positive viscosity, and toroidal closure. The first two steps use a decomposition into a skew-adjoint principal part and compact feedback at a fixed Fourier frequency. Keeping the viscosity fixed, we bend the column into a compactly supported toroidal profile and obtain a genuine whole-space unstable eigenvalue through convergence of localized Stokes resolvents. A small-dilation limit and an exact rescaling then yield an unstable background in similarity variables. A nonlinear trajectory along its unstable direction produces the second solution. Both solutions are smooth for positive times and satisfy the energy equality. The forcing acts in both the velocity and magnetic equations.

papers.title: A Non-Markovian Approach to a Stochastic Rumor Dynamics with Cognitive Deliberation
papers.authors: Cristian F. Coletti, Denis A. Luiz
papers.abstract: We introduce a non-Markovian rumor model on a complete graph of $n$ vertices, integrating the classical interactional framework of Daley and Kendall (1964) with modern cognitive insights into misinformation. Unlike traditional Markovian models, our approach incorporates a deliberation delay -- a decision-making window where individuals evaluate information before committing to dissemination or refutation. We establish a Functional Law of Large Numbers (FLLN) and a Functional Central Limit Theorem (FCLT) to characterize the asymptotic behavior and diffusion-scaled fluctuations of the process.

papers.title: Highest weight category structures on $rep(B)$ and full exceptional collections on generalized flag varieties over $\mathbb Z$
papers.authors: Alexander Samokhin, Wilberd van der Kallen
papers.abstract: Given a split simply connected semi-simple algebraic group scheme $\mathbb G$ over $\mathbb Z$, a split maximaltorus $\mathbb T$ in $\mathbb G$and a parabolic subgroup scheme $\mathbb P\supset \mathbb T$, this paper constructs semi-orthogonal decompositions of the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb P$ with each semi-orthogonal component being equivalent to the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb G$. The semi-orthogonal components of those decompositions are stable under the monoidal action of $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ on $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$. The decompositions depend on an arbitrarily chosen total order on the Weyl group that refines the Bruhat order. The semi-orthogonal decompositions are also compatible with the Bruhat order on cosets of the Weyl group of $\mathbb P$ in the Weyl group of $\mathbb G$. Their construction builds upon the foundational results on $\mathbb B$-modules from the works of Mathieu, Polo, and van der Kallen, and upon properties of the Steinberg basis of the $\mathbb T$-equivariant $K$-theory of $\mathbb G/\mathbb B$. As a corollary, we obtain full exceptional collections in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on generalized flag schemes $\mathbb G/\mathbb P$ over $\mathbb Z$.

papers.title: Semihomogenous vector bundles, $\mathbb Q$-twisted sheaves, duality, and linear systems on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we point out the natural relation between $\mathbb Q$-twisted objects of the derived category of abelian varieties, cohomological rank functions, and semihomogeneous vector bundles. We apply this to two basic classes of objects, corresponding to each other via the Fourier-Mukai-Poincar\'e transform: positive twists of the ideal sheaf of one point and of the evaluation complexes of ample simple semihomogeneous vector bundles. This naturally leads to the introduction of $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$- graded section modules associated to line bundles on abelian varieties built by means of semihomogeneous vector bundles (containing the usual section rings). We prove a duality relation between such modules associated to dual polarizations, which is not visible at the level of the usual section rings. Other applications include formulas relating the thresholds of relevant cohomological rank functions appearing in this context. As a consequence we show a lower bound for the base point free threshold of a polarization in function of its type, and some obstructions to surjectivity of multiplication maps of global sections of certain line bundles.

papers.title: Existence of two-dimensional deep capillary solitary water waves with constant vorticity
papers.abstract: We consider two-dimensional capillary water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth. We first derive the Babenko equation that describes the profile of the solitary wave. When the velocity $c$ is close to a critical velocity, the Babenko equation can be reduced to the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation plus perturbative error. This gives the existence of small-amplitude solitary wave solutions for the water wave system with constant vorticity whose profiles are close to solutions of the stationary focusing cubic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation.

papers.title: Local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by multiplicative noises in two and three dimensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the local and global existence for the stochastic Prandtl equation in two and three dimensions, which governs the velocity field inside the boundary layer that appears in the inviscid limit of the stochastic Navier-Stokes equation with non-slip boundary condition. New problem arises when establishing the well-posedness in the stochastic regime: one can never derive a pathwise control of the energy functional which is used to describe the analytic radius of the solution in the deterministic setting. To this end, we establish higher-order estimates in the conormal Sobolev spaces in order to get rid of the dependence of the analytic radius on the unknown. Three approximate schemes are constructed for solving the stochastic Prandtl equation, and a local well-posedness is obtained in a tangentially analytic and normally Sobolev-type space. Furthermore, we study the stochastic Prandtl equation driven by a tangential random diffusion, and find that the noise regularizes the equation in the sense that in both two and three dimensions, there exists a global Gevrey-2 solution with high probability and the radius growing linearly in time.

papers.title: A phase transition for the cokernels of random band matrices over the p-adic integers
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}_n$ be an $n\times n$ Haar-uniform band matrix over $\mathbb{Z}_p$ with band width $w_n$. We prove that $\text{cok}(\mathbf{B}_n)$ has Cohen-Lenstra limiting distribution if and only if \[\lim_{n\to\infty} \left(w_n-\log_p(n)\right)=+\infty.\]

papers.title: Some invariants of totally disconnected locally compact groups: cohomology and combinatorics
papers.authors: Ilaria Castellano, Bianca Marchionna, Thomas Weigel
papers.abstract: The paper investigates two invariants for totally disconnected locally compact (t.d.l.c.) groups: the number of ends and the rational discrete cohomological dimension. Firstly, for a compactly generated t.d.l.c. group $G$, it is shown that its number of ends can be expressed in terms of the low-dimensional rational discrete cohomology of $G$, generalising a notable theorem by E. Specker to the t.d.l.c. setting. Secondly, we focus on a t.d.l.c. group $G$ acting under suitable conditions on a building $\Delta$, showing that both the number of ends and the rational cohomological dimension of $G$ are related to those of the Weyl group associated to $\Delta$. In special cases, we compare the rational discrete cohomological dimension of $G$ to its flat-rank, and in the appendix we provide examples for which these two invariants coincide. Finally, for t.d.l.c. groups with rational discrete cohomological dimension one that act properly and chamber-transitively on locally finite buildings, we explicitly construct a proper cocompact action on a tree out of the action on the building. All the results of independent interest in Coxeter theory have been included in the appendix.

papers.title: The Bruce-Roberts number of holomorphic 1-forms along complex analytic varieties
papers.authors: Pedro Barbosa, Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, V\'ictor Le\'on
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the \textit{Bruce--Roberts number} for holomorphic 1-forms relative to complex analytic varieties. Our main result shows that the Bruce--Roberts number of a 1-form $\omega$ relative to a complex analytic hypersurface $X$ with an isolated singularity can be expressed in terms of the \textit{Gom\'ez-Mont--Seade--Verjovsky index} of $\omega$ along $X$, the \textit{Milnor number} of $\omega$ and the \textit{Tjurina number} of $X$. This result allows us to recover known formulas for the Bruce--Roberts number of a holomorphic function along $X$ and to establish connections between this number, the radial index, and the local Euler obstruction of $\omega$ along $X$. Moreover, we present applications to both global and local holomorphic foliations in complex dimension two.

papers.title: On the critical points of solutions of Robin boundary problems
