We confirm this bound when $\mu>\lambda+1$ and give counterexamples to the conjecture with $\mu=\lambda$. For amply regular graphs with $\mu\ge\lambda$ and $\mu>1$, we obtain ${\rm{diam}}(G)\le 2k/\mu+1$. This proves the Qiao--Park--Koolen conjecture.
  In 1983, Terwilliger conjectured that every $(s,c,a,k)$-graph with $c>1$ is finite. We prove this conjecture when ``$s>2$, $c>2$, $(s,c)\ne(4,3)$'' and when ``$s=2$, $c>7$''. Moreover, we prove Weetman's finiteness conjecture for locally strongly regular graphs when the local parameter $\mu>1$, and disprove his stronger conjecture that every strongly regular graph is an $\mathscr{S}$-graph. We also prove that every graph whose local graphs all have rank 3 is finite, which in particular proves a conjecture of Soicher in 1992.

papers.title: Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group as defined by Barnet-Lamb et al. in [2]. In this article, we determine explicit modular local Serre weights for mod $p$ Galois representations $\bar\rho_h$ associated to eigenforms $h$ of $G$, with arbitrary weights and small slopes. As a consequence, we also determine modular global Serre weights in certain cases. We show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms corresponding to totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$--modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.

papers.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
papers.authors: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang
papers.abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.

papers.title: Complete $RO$-Graded Tambara Functor of $H\underline{\mathbb Z}$ for cyclic groups
papers.abstract: We compute the $RO$-graded Tambara functor of $H\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups to give the explicit formula for products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Besides the computation, We also develop a theory that reconstructs a genuine equivariant spectrum as the homotopy limit of a finite diagram of homotopy fixed-point spectra, Tate spectra, and only one localization spectrum at the terminal of the diagram. We call it the Tate compression theory. From it we also give a filtration for $\pi_\star(H\underline{\mathbb{Z}})$, compatible with products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms.

papers.title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
papers.authors: Frank E. Curtis, Zahra Khatti, Daniel P. Robinson
papers.abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.

papers.title: Higher-order derivatives and their applications to diffeomorphism groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply higher-order tangent bundles and higher-order derivative maps to study countable subgroups of the diffeomorphism group ${\rm Diff}(M)$ of a closed smooth manifold $M$. Using this framework, we introduce the concept of higher-order $\mu$-discreteness for subgroups $\Gamma < {\rm Diff}(M)$, and show that both the strong Novikov conjecture and the coarse Baum--Connes conjecture hold for countable groups with higher-order $\mu$-discreteness. Finally, we give examples showing that higher-order $\mu$-discreteness encompasses a strictly larger class of subgroups of $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$ than its lower-order counterpart.

papers.title: Local $Tb$ theorems with applications to the Neumann problem and caloric measure
papers.authors: Andrea Merlo, Mihalis Mourgoglou, Carmelo Puliatti
papers.abstract:
We prove a local $Tb$ theorem with testing conditions on metric balls, for possibly non-doubling measures of polynomial growth on geometrically doubling metric spaces. It resolves the maximal-truncation version of Hofmann's local $Tb$ problem for all $1<p,q\leq\infty$, without assuming antisymmetry of the Calder\'on-Zygmund kernel.
  Our theorem allows accretive systems of complex testing measures satisfying a quantitative small-set condition; these measures need not be absolutely continuous with respect to the underlying measure. Testing requires only a one-level $L^0$ bound for maximal truncations, with an alternative for balls on which the underlying measure concentrates in a set of small relative diameter. We also remove antisymmetry from the known buffered and unbuffered fixed-truncation criteria. The proof combines a mixed corona decomposition adapted to the two testing systems with two-measure $L^2$ estimates for suppressed operators. We obtain the following applications:
  - If $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$, $n\geq 2$, is a bounded domain with Ahlfors regular boundary satisfying the interior corkscrew condition, and the Neumann problem for the Laplacian in $\Omega$ is solvable with data in $L^p$ for some $1<p<\infty$, then $\partial\Omega$ is uniformly rectifiable. The proof applies the matrix-valued version of the theorem to the Cauchy-Clifford operator.
  - In the parabolic space $\mathbb{P}^n$, local time-directed $A_\infty$-type conditions on caloric and adjoint caloric measure imply $L^2(\sigma)$-boundedness of the spatial gradient of the heat single layer potential for boundary measures $\sigma$ with upper parabolic $(n+1)$-growth. This gives a parabolic counterpart of the harmonic-measure theorem of Mourgoglou and Tolsa without Ahlfors regularity, corkscrew or Harnack chain assumptions.

papers.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
papers.abstract:
The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not
  increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for
  each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal
  ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound. A connection to (generalized) Loewy length is given.

papers.title: Proper conflict-free degree-choosability of graphs with maximum average degree less than $8/3$
papers.abstract: A proper coloring $\varphi$ of a graph $G$ is called proper conflict-free if, for every non-isolated vertex $v$, some color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood $N_G(v)$. For a nonnegative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable if, for every list assignment $L$ satisfying $|L(v)|\ge d_G(v)+k$ for each $v\in V(G)$, there exists a proper conflict-free coloring $\varphi$ of $G$ with $\varphi(v)\in L(v)$ for each $v\in V(G)$. We prove that every connected graph other than the $5$-cycle $C_5$ with maximum average degree less than $8/3$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable. This improves the maximum average degree bound $18/7$ of Kashima, \v{S}krekovski and Xu, and removes the assumption $g(G)\ge7$ from the $8/3$ theorem of Qi, Song and Cao. We also show that the $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$ list-size bound is best possible for graphs with maximum average degree arbitrarily close to $8/3$ from below. As an immediate consequence, our theorem implies that every planar graph of girth at least $8$ is proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+2)$-choosable.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $\tau$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected precisely when the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules and has Cartan rank one. There are then exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra is connected. Suppose the defining partial tagged triangulation is nonempty and all its endpoints are punctures. Then the realization of the support $\tau$-tilting complex is homotopy equivalent to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Signed endpoint vectors give an explicit homotopy equivalence. Under the same endpoint hypothesis, $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates and give a surface criterion distinguishing the root sets of types $A$, $D$ and $C$. The homotopy construction also applies to Brauer graph algebras with arbitrary vertex multiplicities.

papers.title: Beyond Typical Strings: Sampling the Complexity Landscape
papers.authors: Abdurrahman Hadi Erturk, Joshua Sharkey, Nora S Martin, Kamal Dingle, Ard A Louis
papers.abstract: Uniform random sampling of strings is overwhelmingly dominated by high-complexity strings, leaving the much smaller set of low- and intermediate-complexity strings largely unexplored. Here, we adapt the nested neutral set estimator (NNSE), a Monte Carlo rare-event sampling method, to estimate the distribution P(K) of complexity values for binary strings of fixed length. NNSE allows us to explore the full complexity landscape, including exponentially rare low-complexity regions that are inaccessible to direct sampling, for string lengths up to several hundred. We apply the method to several widely used complexity measures: Lempel-Ziv 76 (LZ76), Lempel-Ziv 78 (LZ78), context tree weighting (CTW), the block decomposition method (BDM), and block entropy. We further introduce uniform complexity weighting (UCW), which gives equal weight to different complexity levels rather than to individual strings. Using NNSE to perform UCW sampling allows us to compare complexity measures across their full range in a dataset-independent way. This reveals differences in their behavior for low- and intermediate-complexity strings that are practically inaccessible to conventional uniform sampling.

papers.title: A Representation Theorem for Fractional Viscoelastic Networks
papers.authors: Andrea Giusti, Ivano Colombaro, Andrea Mentrelli, Francesco Mainardi
papers.abstract: We prove a representation theorem for finite series-parallel viscoelastic networks composed of springs and spring-pots of a common order $0<\alpha<1$. Using classical representation results for complete Bernstein and Stieltjes functions, we show that the associated complex shear modulus, expressed in an appropriately chosen auxiliary variable, admits a finite partial-fraction representation with simple poles on the negative real axis. Its reciprocal admits an analogous representation with a possible additional pole at the origin. Inverting the corresponding Laplace transforms gives finite fractional Prony representations of the relaxation modulus and creep compliance with non-negative amplitudes. These results provide a rigorous proof of a corrected version of the Mainardi-Spada conjecture for this network class. A six-element network illustrates the construction.

papers.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
papers.abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we investigate finite-time boundary collisions and interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. We first prove that finite-time boundary collisions are impossible for arbitrary nonzero vortex circulations, without any restrictions on their signs or algebraic relations. The result excludes both simultaneous boundary collapse and individual vortex approaches to the boundary, without requiring convergence of the vortex trajectories. In contrast, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse by treating the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.

papers.title: A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions
papers.abstract: P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet \(L\)-functions over \(\Q\) with conductors coprime to \(3\), with a main term of order \(Q\) and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindel\"of hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order \(Q^{\frac{5}{6}}\) in the same family, with error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)\). We explicitly evaluate the secondary coefficient and prove that it is strictly negative. We also prove unconditionally that the secondary polynomial in the squarefree second moment of the natural cubic Hecke \(L\)-functions over \(\Q(\sqrt{-3})\) has degree one and strictly positive leading coefficient, which we evaluate explicitly.

papers.title: Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains
papers.abstract: We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions as well as H\"{o}lder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations with Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.

papers.title: A $33$-polynomial proof of a three-color Rado number formula
papers.abstract: For $k\ge 3$, let $T_k(3)$ denote the least $N$ such that every $3$-coloring of $[1,N]$ contains a monochromatic solution to $x+(k-1)y=z$. The formula $T_k(3)=k^3+2k^2-2$ is already known: it follows from a Theorem of Chang, De Loera, and Wesley. Their proof uses a symbolic SAT certificate with $685$ polynomials and $9468$ solution triples. The purpose of this paper is to give an independent, explicit proof based on a much smaller certificate. We exhibit a fixed set $\Xmin$ of $33$ polynomials in $k$ and the $144$ polynomial identities $z=x+(k-1)y$ among them, and show that no $3$-coloring of $\Xmin$ avoids a monochromatic identity. The resulting case analysis has $62$ cases, depth $8$, and uses only two elementary rules; it is given in full and independently checked by a program. We also prove that $\Xmin$ is a critical subset of minimum cardinality of the $51$-element set from which it was extracted, and describe the rigid structure shared by all extremal colorings of $[1,k^3+2k^2-3]$. The lower bound is supplied by an explicit recursive coloring. In the notation $s_a(3)$ of the first author, with $a=k-1$, the formula is $s_a(3)=a^3+5a^2+7a+1$, which was conjectured before.

papers.title: Uniformization of topological MV-algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, First, we prove that for every topological MV-algebra the topology is induced by a uniformity. As a application, we obtain that every topological MV-algebra is completely regular and every \(T_0\) first countable topological MV-algebra is metrizable. Second, we study the completion of the canonical difference uniformity in topological MV-algebra. Finally, we construct some examples show that not all topological MV-algebras are canonically completable and the property of canonically completable topological MV-algebra does not imply local order convexity.

papers.title: Multi-rate high-order regularization with an order-$(p-2)$ oracle
papers.abstract:
We consider unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ whose $p$th derivative is Lipschitz continuous, with $p\geq3$, when derivative information is available only through order $p-2$. The unavailable tensors $
abla^{p-1}f$ and $
abla^pf$ are reconstructed from central finite differences of $
abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $\epsilon$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.

papers.title: On cylindrical directions of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ derived from contact with spherical cylinders
papers.abstract: We investigate the contact of regular surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with spherical cylinders $S^2(r) \times \mathbb{R}$. We introduce cylindrical directions of these surfaces, defined by the axes of spherical cylinders having degenerate contact with the surfaces, and show that these directions capture the ridge condition of projected regular surfaces under orthogonal projection along these directions.

papers.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
papers.abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.

papers.title: Model Existence and Scott's Theorem for Infinitary Real-Valued Logic: A Topological Perspective
papers.authors: Olivia Aubone, Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino
papers.abstract: In this paper we adopt a topological perspective to extend two theorems of classical infinitary logic to the infinitary logic of Keisler's general real-valued structures: the omitting types theorem and Scott's theorem. There the formulas need not be uniformly bounded, and no moduli of continuity are required, as they are in the metric extensions of the classical theorems; neither equality nor a metric is required. The omitting types theorem holds for every countable fragment, because the space of Henkin types of the fragment is \v{C}ech-complete. Scott's theorem characterizes every structure with countable sorts, among all structures, up to approximate equivalence, and the classes of this equivalence are Borel sets in the Polish space of structures on the natural numbers. With the monoid of surjections of the natural numbers in place of the group of permutations, we also prove L\'opez-Escobar's theorem for classical infinitary logic without equality.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Relaxed Multiplication in List Coloring
papers.abstract: Jiang and Zhu [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 137 (2019) 112--117] asked whether every $k$-choosable graph is $(km+1:m)$-choosable for every positive integer $m$. We show that, for all integers $k\ge3$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$ satisfying $m>8t+\epsilon$, where $\epsilon\in\{0,1\}$ and $m\equiv\epsilon\pmod2$, there is a graph with chromatic number and choice number both equal to $k$ that is not $(km+t:m)$-choosable. This answers their question negatively for every $k\ge3$ and $m\ge10$. In particular, our construction yields a $3$-choosable graph on $91$ vertices that is not $(6:2)$-choosable, answering a question of Dvo\v{r}\'ak, Hu and Sereni [Adv. Comb. (2019), Paper No.~5]. More generally, for every fixed $b\ge1$, $m\ge2$, and $t\ge0$, we construct an $(a:b)$-choosable graph that is not $(am+t:bm)$-choosable for all sufficiently large $a$, with an explicit bound on $a$. Let $F(a,b)$ be the supremum of the strong fractional choice numbers of $(a:b)$-choosable graphs. We prove that for every fixed $b\ge1$, $F(a,b)-\frac ab$ tends to infinity as $a\to\infty$.

papers.title: Kernelized Stable Fluids for simulating physically accurate solutions
papers.authors: Lennart Scholz, Aras Bacho, Houman Owhadi
papers.abstract: The Stable Fluids algorithm is a fractional step method for solving the incompressible Navier-Stokes (NS) equations in an unconditionally stable way. It was initially developed for visual effects and allows real-time simulations because of its low computational complexity. The method solves the advection step by using the method of characteristics which is implemented via linear interpolation. This results in excessive diffusion of vorticity and is one of the main reasons for the physical inaccuracy of the algorithm. We propose Kernelized Stable Fluids with Sparse Cholesky Preconditioning (KSF-Chol) in order to address this shortcoming and make the algorithm thereby suitable for engineering problems and scientific computing. The algorithm is modified by replacing the linear interpolation approach with kernel interpolation in the advection step. We accelerate the computationally expensive kernel interpolation by using sparse Cholesky preconditioning and a near-/far-field approach and optimize both methods for computations on a uniform Cartesian grid. KSF-Chol achieves per time step a near-linear computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log^d(N/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{chol}}))$ in space and time. We test KSF-Chol against reference solvers and numerical reference data on multiple 2D and 3D benchmarks and demonstrate a significantly reduced numerical diffusion as well as a competitive accuracy concerning the computation of relevant flow quantities.

papers.title: A Note on the Finite-Exceedance Dependence Principle for Sum--Maximum Asymptotic Independence
papers.abstract: Asymptotic independence between sum-type and maximum-type statistics arises repeatedly across many areas of probability and statistics, particularly in high-dimensional testing and random matrix theory. Motivated by the shared structure underlying existing proofs, which is obscured by their model-specific formulations, this note isolates a common intermediate principle. We introduce a finite-exceedance dependence principle: if the finite-exceedance dependence error vanishes at every fixed order and high-order exceedances are mildly controlled, then a finite-order Bonferroni argument yields asymptotic independence between the sum and the maximum. We further give an independent-proxy criterion for verifying this: for each finite set of exceedances, it suffices to construct an exactly independent proxy for the sum-type statistic whose approximation error is negligible in aggregate. Local deletion under dependency graphs and Gaussian regression and residualization are two examples. The framework gives modular derivations of existing sum--max independence results.

papers.title: Deterministic Principal Ideals of Dependent Random Operators
papers.abstract: We classify the algebraic principal ideals of alternating quadratic random operators under dimension-free two-sided curvature bounds. For the centered evaluation of a Hilbert two-form, an explicit covariance compensator determines the principal ideal after every fixed compact perturbation. For fixed spectral choices, the compensator is a compact linear function of the full covariance with explicit finite-dimensional approximation bounds; its class modulo the independent Gaussian ideal is intrinsic. For fixed spatial weights of rank at least two and a trace-class kernel, all attainable principal ideals form an exact order interval. Every intermediate ideal is realized by a Gaussian covariance arbitrarily close to the identity while each row retains its standard Gaussian law. For these spatial weights, trace class is also the exact kernel domain for raw evaluation under every law in the curvature class. The proof uses a conditional-residual criterion for linear operators, polarization, and finite-rank approximation. Applications include Wiener area and dependent matrices with doubly monotone variance weights. A logarithmic example separates principal ideals with identical membership in every Schatten class.

papers.title: On the lower bound for the $L^1$ norm of Liouville exponential sums. I
papers.authors: Jiangpeng Li, Yu-Chen Sun, Hui Wang
papers.abstract:
Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove Let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. We prove \[ \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)=\int_{\mathbb{T}}\left|\sum_{1\leqslant n\leqslant X}\lambda\left(n\right)\mathrm{e}\left(n\alpha\right)\right|
  \mathrm{d}\alpha
  \gg X^{\frac{1}{4}}. \] This removes the $X^\varepsilon$ loss in the previous result of Pandey and Radziwi\l\l~\cite{PandeyRadziwill2026}. In the second paper in this series, we will prove that \[ \limsup_{X \to \infty} \frac{\log \mathcal{I}_{\lambda}(X)} {\log X} \geqslant\frac{1}{3}. \]

papers.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
papers.abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every non-contractive bijection $F$ is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits: for all $a$ and $\varepsilon>0$, $0\le d(Fx,Fy)-d(x,y)<\varepsilon$ for $x$ far in the past of $a$ and all $y$. Zavarzina asked whether every such bijection of a precompact space is an isometry; the author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) answered no. Each such $F$ has a register, a quasi-pseudo-metric $\lambda^-\le d$ for which $F$ is an isometry, with round-trip distances totally bounded on orbits; after completion, $F$ acts on each orbit as a rotation of a compact monothetic group, its rigid shadow. The defect $d-\lambda^-$ from $x$ to $y$ is at most the fee of $x$ (the supremum of its defects to earlier iterates) and at least the excess of $x$'s fee over $y$'s now or at any earlier time, less their round-trip register distance; the fee never decreases forward along orbits and tends to zero backward. In this sense, every such $F$ is a toll over its rigid shadow. The fees bound the defect but do not determine it: three spirals show it can depend on $y$, vanish at a distant $y$ even when $x$ has a positive fee, and be positive toward later iterates of $x$. The toll-spiral paper asked whether every such map is conjugate to a tolled extension, a fixed toll zone over an isometric shadow, possibly with infinitely many zones. If only descents are charged, the answer is no, even up to bi-Lipschitz conjugacy; on each infinite orbit, a map is such an extension over its register exactly when its ascents carry no defect. Fees may vanish at any rate, but for zone tolls (two-valued, shift-monotone, subadditive along their routes) they reach zero at a finite depth. The general results hold on quasi-pseudo-metric spaces where every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; all but the statements listed at the end are machine-checked in Lean.

papers.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.

papers.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: We construct canonical projective birational models of normal proper integral algebraic spaces over arbitrary fields. The construction preserves the intrinsic quasi-projective core and is natural under semilinear isomorphisms. For smooth proper integral input in characteristic zero, we combine an intrinsic choice of ideals with W{\l}odarczyk's principalization to obtain a canonical tower of blowups in smooth centers ending in a smooth projective variety. Consequently, every compact connected Moishezon manifold admits a smooth projective bimeromorphic model to which all automorphisms lift compatibly. The main ingredient is a family-sum argument yielding an intrinsic finite selection of maximal tuples of boundary ideal germs; successive modifications strictly decrease the boundary-image dimension. We also construct canonical quasi-projective models for nonproper normal input and a greatest schematizing ideal for separated finite-type algebraic spaces over noetherian bases. Oda's threefold illustrates the construction.

papers.title: A Side Condition Principle With Applications
papers.abstract: We introduce a combinatorial principle $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$, for any regular cardinal $\kappa \ge \omega_2$, which asserts the existence of a family $\mathcal{Y} \subseteq [H(\kappa)]^\omega$ of elementary substructures of $H(\kappa)$ which is closed under finite intersections and satisfies that for stationarily many $N \in \mathcal{Y}$, if $M \in \mathcal{Y}$ and $M \cap \omega_1 < N \cap \omega_1$, then $M \cap N \cap \kappa \in N$. We explore the idea of defining forcings with side conditions consisting of finite subsets of such a family $\mathcal{Y}$. If $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ holds, then there exists a thin stationary subset of $[\omega_2]^\omega$, and consequently $\textsf{SC}(\omega_2)$ is independent of ZFC. Assuming that $\mu$ is a Mahlo cardinal, the L\'{e}vy collapse $\mathrm{Col}(\omega,<\mu)$ forces that $\textsf{SC}(\kappa)$ holds for all regular cardinals $\kappa \ge \omega_2$. Local instances of $\textsf{SC}$ can be forced using matrices of models or derived as consequences of square principles. We apply the principle $\textsf{SC}$ to define two kinds of forcings: a streamlined version of a strongly proper collapse, and a forcing which is strongly proper on a stationary set and adds arbitrarily many Baumgartner clubs. Finally, we prove two consistency results using forcings derived from $\textsf{SC}$ related to Aronszajn trees, the guessing model principle, strong failures of club guessing, and the higher dominating number.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: An exact unstable mode of self-similar Yang--Mills solutions in 5+1 dimensions
papers.abstract: Self-similar solutions play an important role in the formation of singularities in the Yang--Mills equations. In five space dimensions, these equations admit infinitely many self-similar solutions with an increasing number of unstable modes. It was observed numerically in [1] that all excited profiles share the least unstable eigenvalue $\lambda=5$. We explain this remarkable spectral property by an elementary construction of the corresponding eigenfunction.

papers.title: Automaticity of structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions
papers.abstract: We study structural defects in fixed points of block substitutions, building on arXiv:2604.12637 and providing its technical supplement. We develop an automata-based framework to characterize their occurrence and derive verifiable combinatorial criteria. We also introduce simplifications for the construction and analysis of these automata, including tensor-product decompositions, that clarify the mechanisms underlying structural defects and their emergence.

papers.title: A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erd\H{o}s--S\'os $(9,6)$-problem
papers.authors: Xiangliang Kong, Chong Shangguan, Xin Wang
papers.abstract: For integers $e\ge3$, let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. The lower-bound part of a longstanding conjecture of Erd\H{o}s, Frankl, and R\"odl from 1986 asserts that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, resolving the first open case not covered by the classical construction of Ruzsa and Szemer\'edi in 1976, which established $f_3(n,6,3)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$. We also establish near-quadratic lower bounds for $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ with $e=9,10,11$. We further extend the result for $e=6$ to every fixed uniformity $r\ge4$.

papers.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
papers.abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Brou\'{e}--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: The critical Cauchy boundary for Gibbs partitions
papers.abstract: We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.

papers.title: Infinitary real-valued logic and a refinement of the Kochen-Specker theorem
papers.abstract: We prove that every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables in quantum mechanics is finite, including the obstructions that rest on Gleason's hypothesis of countable additivity. Since Kochen and Specker, such obstructions have been certified by finite configurations of rays, at the level of propositional logic: once a configuration is fixed, the obstruction is the inconsistency of finitely many Boolean constraints. Compactness, the source of these configurations, cannot reach the obstructions that rest on countable additivity: in infinite dimension the finite-dimensional events admit a finitely additive noncontextual valuation, and countable additivity constrains infinitely many events at once. The tool is a theorem of infinitary real-valued logic that takes the place of compactness: every countable theory of closed conditions without models is refuted by a well-founded tree of finite contradictions, given by the winning strategies of a model existence game. Quantum probability is axiomatized by such a theory, whose standard models are exactly those of Gleason's theorem. In the strategy we construct, a hypothetical noncontextual measure is not refuted by a configuration fixed in advance: through countable additivity, the measure itself selects the four-dimensional subspace in which the measure fails. The same logic defines, in the standard models, exactly the $\sigma$-projective sets of probabilities. Statements about $\sigma$-projective sets often go beyond ZFC, as the measurability of all these sets does; our theorems are nevertheless proved in ZFC, since the only determinacy they use is that of open games.

papers.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
papers.authors: Andr\'e Tits, Pierre-Antoine Absil, No\'e Tits
papers.abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.

papers.title: The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertial Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, where each objective is a smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term and the proximal subproblem keeps a separate offset for each objective. For a two-parameter root momentum rule with trajectory-dependent coefficients, we construct a new energy function and establish an energy identity. This yields sharper convergence guarantees: boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. At the critical value $\alpha=3$, we obtain $u_0(x^N)\le \frac{2\ell R}{N(N+3)},$ together with $O(1/N)$ displacement decay, square summability, and weak Pareto convergence. The remaining little-$o$ question at $\alpha=3$ is reduced to the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy. For $1<\alpha<3$, we prove the rate $O(N^{-(\alpha-1)})$, and for every $\alpha>0$ we obtain $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A JOS1 experiment numerically validates the predicted little-$o$ separation and the rate behavior.

papers.title: A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokes-Biot problem
papers.authors: Rui Li, Hui Peng, Xiuli Wang
papers.abstract: In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.

papers.title: Nonisomorphic separable Banach spaces at Lipschitz distance one
papers.abstract: We construct nonisomorphic separable real Banach spaces whose multiplicative Lipschitz distance is one. Building on OpenAI's graph-space construction, we arrange two sequences of graph spaces into countably many blocks and form two spaces that differ by a single additional block. This block distinguishes their linear structures: one space contains a complemented copy of $\ell_1(c_0(\ell_2))$, whereas the other does not. By mapping the additional block to increasingly late positions and rearranging the remaining blocks, we obtain homeomorphisms whose Lipschitz constants and those of their inverses tend to one, while both spaces and their norms remain unchanged.

papers.title: The Logic of Emergence
papers.authors: David H. Wolpert, David C. Krakauer
papers.abstract: ``Emergence'' refers to the fact that different mathematical languages and theories seem to be required to describe scientific theories that operate at different spatial and temporal scales. Highly circumscribed, special cases of emergence have been investigated using many different formal tools, including coarse-graining (over space and / or time), renormalization, dimension reduction, broken symmetry, and various formulations of causality. Here we extend the mathematics of model theory to unify and extend these earlier investigations. As a preliminary application of our framework, we investigate canonical examples of emergence, including the emergence of genetics from chemistry, of psychology from neurobiology, and of different forms of collective behavior from the laws governing their constituent parts. By exploiting the power of model theory we also uncover many aspects of emergence that were previously obscured. In particular, we uncover some of the rich hierarchical structure that relates different scientific fields. For example, we show that scientific fields can be related via a collection of multiple partial orders, all defined over the same set. On the other hand, under an alternative relation among scientific fields, one which allows cycles, we show that it is possible that the set of all of scientific fields must collapse into a single scientific field. Going forward, these investigations point to the formal tools that might need to be developed in order to arrive at a deeper understanding of this emergent hierarchy of scientific reality.

papers.title: Technical Report: Partially Asynchronous Distributed Optimization on Riemannian Manifolds
papers.authors: Adam Pooley, William Warke, Matthew T. Hale
papers.abstract: There is a large body of work on distributed optimization for problems in Euclidean space. However, many existing algorithms and analyses do not directly transfer to problems defined on manifolds. Therefore, in this paper we propose a distributed asynchronous optimization algorithm for problems on Riemannian manifolds. The algorithm we develop is a parallelized form of Riemannian block coordinate descent in which all agents can compute and communicate asynchronously. We assume only "partial asynchrony", namely that all delays in computations and communications obey some finite bound, and we omit the common assumptions of convexity of the objective and compactness of the manifold. Under mild conditions, we prove that agents' iterates drive the Riemannian gradient of the objective to zero, and we derive a rate of convergence for the norm of the gradient. In simulations, we compare to a synchronous baseline algorithm under varying communication delays and numbers of agents. In example problems, we empirically show that our algorithm converges up to 8.5 times faster and attains up to 24 times lower suboptimality over a finite horizon.

papers.title: A family of symmetric counterexamples to the bent sum decomposition conjecture
papers.authors: M\'at\'e R\'obert Kepes, Anita Kercs\'o-Moln\'ar, Andr\'as Viczi\'an
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an infinite family of counterexamples to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions. The conjecture states that every Boolean function in an even number of variables $n$ of algebraic degree at most $n/2$ can be written as the sum of two bent functions. We show that for every $n=2^k\geq 8$, the symmetric function $F_n=1+\sigma_2+\sigma_4+\sigma_6+\cdots+\sigma_{n/2}$ has degree $n/2$ and cannot be written as a sum of at most two bent functions. Here $\sigma_j$ is the elementary symmetric Boolean polynomial of degree $j$. Furthermore, we show that the eight-variable member of this family can be represented as the sum of exactly three bent functions. Using the connection between bent-sum decompositions and derivatives of bent functions, we also obtain an infinite family of balanced Boolean functions that cannot be derivatives of bent functions.

papers.title: Validity of the Behrens--Fisher solution
papers.abstract: The Behrens--Fisher fiducial interval for the difference of two normal means is known from the numerical work of Robinson (1976) to be conservative, but a proof has been lacking. The results here prove that the fiducial interval for any linear combination of $k$ normal means has coverage probability at least its nominal level for all values of the unknown variances. Taraldsen (2026) explains this in more detail using the original data of Behrens (1926). The proof presented in the following rests on a novel plug-in inequality: if a threshold function controls a scaled sum of pivots pointwise in the scale vector, then it also controls the sum with the observed scales plugged in, provided the location errors satisfy a concentration condition formulated through a weighted geometric mean. Independent normal errors satisfy the condition.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the martingale property of stochastic exponentials driven by multi-dimensional diffusions
papers.abstract: We give necessary and sufficient coefficient conditions for stochastic exponentials driven by multidimensional diffusions to be true martingales. The classical reduction to non-exit of the diffusion with Girsanov-shifted drift separates the analysis into smooth boundary points, infinity, and nonsmooth boundary pieces. On smooth domains, under regularity and non-explosion hypotheses, martingality is equivalent to nonpositivity of the shifted Fichera drift, provided an explicit local condition holds where that drift vanishes and the stochastic integrand is unbounded. At infinity, Feller's test gives exact criteria when a scalar function of the diffusion reduces to a one-dimensional diffusion up to a time change with rate comparable to a positive function of the scalar coordinate. General radial and projection tests supply sufficient conditions. Applications give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions for inverse-CIR and $4/2$ models with correlated factors and singular stochastic integrands, including critical equality cases. The coupled non-affine examples go beyond direct scalar Feller tests and affine Riccati criteria, and exhibit boundary exits not decided by tests at infinity. Further exact criteria cover logarithmic boundary singularities, weighted distances, and an absorbed factor. The martingale conditions also yield uniqueness criteria for associated valuation equations.

papers.title: Minimum-Time Interceptor Selection and Obstacle-Avoiding Path Planning for Heterogeneous UAVs
papers.abstract: Selecting the most suitable unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to intercept a moving target is challenging when multiple vehicles have different speeds, initial headings, turning capabilities and launch delays, particularly in environments containing obstacles. This paper develops a computationally efficient framework that integrates minimum-time interceptor selection with obstacle-avoiding path planning for heterogeneous UAVs. The interception problem for each UAV is formulated as a minimum-time optimal control problem and solved numerically using an arc-parameterised nonlinear programming model based on Dubins-type paths. The candidate trajectories consist of minimum-radius circular arcs, straight-line segments and tangential obstacle-boundary arcs, with exact geometric distance constraints imposed to ensure obstacle avoidance along the entire path. To improve computational efficiency, a closed-form lower bound on interception time is incorporated into a bound-and-select algorithm that eliminates UAVs unable to improve the best verified feasible interception time. The proposed pruning strategy preserves the best computed interception decision obtained through full enumeration while reducing computational effort. Numerical experiments investigate the effects of target speed, UAV turning radius, launch delay and obstacle configuration. Across 20 randomly generated scenarios involving up to eight UAVs, the proposed approach reduces average computational time by approximately 85$\%$ for eight-vehicle teams without changing the selected interceptor or its computed interception time. The proposed approach provides an efficient method for selecting a single UAV and generating feasible Dubins-type interception trajectories in obstacle-constrained environments.

papers.title: Gaps in the Most Frequent Sizes of Integer Sumsets
papers.authors: Saad A. Awan, Steven J. Miller, Linh Nguyen, Steven Senger, Elvis Wong
papers.abstract: Nathanson observed that, for four-element sets $A$ of integers, the most frequent sizes of the iterated sumset $hA$ are separated by triangular numbers. Senger proved this and suggested an analogue for larger sets. We establish this pattern for $k$-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,q\}$, for every fixed $k\geq3$, where $h\geq2$ is either fixed or grows slower than $q^{1/(2k-1)}$. As $q\to\infty$, almost every such set has the largest possible $h$-fold sumset, and almost every exception has one of $h-1$ explicit smaller sizes. The differences between consecutive sizes among these $h$ values are consecutive $(k-2)$-dimensional simplex numbers.

papers.title: A true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independence of PA
papers.abstract: We give a true $\Pi^0_1$ sentence $\varphi$ which is independent of Peano Arithmetic. Moreover, if $\widehat{\phi}$ denotes its interpretation on $\omega$ as a sentence of set theory, then $\widehat{\phi}$ is a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence independent of ZFC.

papers.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
papers.authors: K. Sudarshan Kumar, Boniface Nkonga, Praveen Chandrashekar
papers.abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models under gravitational force, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.

papers.title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $\kappa\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $\kappa$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $\kappa$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.

papers.title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
papers.authors: Jiamei Li, Caihua Luo, Xu Song, Yilin Zeng
papers.abstract: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.

papers.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
papers.abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.

papers.title: Shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces
papers.abstract: We describe the shifted Lagrangian geometry of curves in Radko surfaces, through their global integrations and their homotopy Poisson algebras. We construct the adjoint symplectic groupoid of the surface explicitly, show that admissible curves integrate to embedded Lagrangian subgroupoids, which are 1-shifted Lagrangians, and characterize when their shifted intersections are clean. For a component of the degeneracy locus, a canonical Hamiltonian flow on its shifted self-intersection recovers the modular period. On the infinitesimal side, the homotopy Poisson algebra of a connected admissible curve not contained in the degeneracy locus is $L_\infty$-isomorphic to its underlying cochain complex, and its $L_\infty$-isomorphism class is determined by the total contact multiplicity. The brackets of arity at least two can be removed by a change of tubular neighbourhood exactly when all contacts are transverse. At tangential contacts, the binary bracket retains the modular vector field. We establish this distinction using a general characterization of the $L_\infty$-isomorphisms induced by changes of tubular neighbourhood, valid for arbitrary coisotropic submanifolds.

papers.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
papers.authors: Francisco J. Mu\~noz, Juan Carlos Nu\~no, Luca Meacci
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a discrete-time model in which the population is updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. The model is a Markov chain whose large-population limit is a map $F_\tau$; Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, $F_\tau$ goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the computed window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. One-stage contagion ($p=1$), $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos in our scans. In all tests the chaotic attractor was unique up to coexistence with simpler attractors, with one positive Lyapunov exponent. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle with troughs of $10^{-44}$--$10^{-164}$: the round structure does not create the oscillation but turns it into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus not an artefact of discretising a stable state, but a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating.

papers.title: The singular Gaussian scaling limit for a tagged particle in the infinite-dimensional Dyson model at $\beta=2$
papers.abstract: We prove a logarithmic central limit theorem for a tagged particle in infinite-dimensional Dyson Brownian motion at inverse temperature $\beta=2$, starting from the sine$_2$ point process. The fluctuation is of order $\sqrt{\log t}$, which is subdiffusive and substantially slower than the polynomial fluctuations of classical short-range interacting particle systems, reflecting the rigidity induced by long-range logarithmic repulsion. We further identify the scaling limit as the singular Gaussian field corresponding to the zero-Hurst parameter, which provides a realisation of the singular Gaussian field as a scaling limit of a tagged particle raised by D\"urr, Goldstein and Lebowitz (Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 38 (1985)).

papers.title: $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$- and $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-invariant multidifferential operators
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension of the space of $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$-invariant (n)-ary differential operators on weighted densities for arbitrary weights, including the singular cases in which the usual elimination procedure breaks down. The proof relies on the strong Lefschetz property established by Stanley \cite{s} and Watanabe \cite{w}. We also investigate the corresponding problem in the super case.

papers.title: h-dichotomies via uniform noncriticality and expansiveness for noninvertible evolution families
papers.abstract: We establish characterizations of h-dichotomies for noninvertible evolution families acting on Banach spaces, in terms of appropriate notions of expansiveness and uniform noncriticality. Our results extend the corresponding characterizations previously obtained for invertible evolution families. To the best of our knowledge, no such characterizations have previously been established for general noninvertible evolution families. A key difference is that noninvertibility makes the structure of the stable spaces more delicate: in our positive-half-line result, finite codimension must be imposed at every time, rather than only at the initial time. We show by an example that the latter, weaker condition is insufficient. We also study evolution families on the negative half-line, using duality to obtain corresponding characterizations in terms of dual expansiveness and dual uniform noncriticality. General growth rates are treated by a time-rescaling argument.

papers.title: Sharp condition for Superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation
papers.authors: Xia Huang, Yuan Li, Yixing Pu
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp condition for local superharmonicity of positive singular solutions to the critical polyharmonic equation $(-\Delta)^m u=u^{\frac{n+2m}{n-2m}}$, where $m\geq2$ is an integer and $n>2m$. For a solution in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at zero, local superharmonicity holds if and only if \(\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)>0\). The threshold is sharp. In the biharmonic case $m=2$, for every $n\geq5$, we construct smooth positive solutions of $\Delta^2u=u^{\frac{n+4}{n-4}}$ in a punctured ball with a nonremovable singularity at $0$, satisfying $\liminf_{x\to0}u(x)=0$ and $\limsup_{x\to0}u(x)=+\infty$, while $-\Delta u$ converges to a finite negative limit along a fixed ray. The construction relies on an infinite array of concentrating bubbles arranged on concentric polygons, with a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction controlling their interactions against a vanishing background.

papers.title: Recurrent and rigid multipliers on commutative Banach algebras. The Fourier algebra
papers.authors: Mar\'ia J. Beltr\'an-Meneu, Jorge Galindo, Enrique Jord\'a
papers.abstract: We study recurrence, rigidity and uniform rigidity of multipliers on semisimple commutative Banach algebras. For a power-bounded multiplier $T$ on a Tauberian, self-adjoint algebra $\mathfrak{A}$, we show that $T$ satisfies each of these properties if and only if the multiplication operator on $C_0(\Delta(\mathfrak{A}))$ induced by the Gelfand transform of $T$ does. One consequence of our analysis is that, if $\Delta(\mathfrak{A})$ is $\sigma$-compact, then recurrence implies rigidity for such multipliers. We examine in detail the multipliers of the Fourier algebra $A(G)$. In particular, we show that recurrence of a multiplier of $A(G)$ is equivalent to recurrence of the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ when the connected components of $G$ are open. For multipliers that are not power bounded, a flexible construction based on chains of compact subgroups of a locally compact abelian group $G$ produces multipliers of $A(G)$ that are rigid but not uniformly rigid, and multipliers that are recurrent but not rigid, such that in each case the corresponding multiplier on $C_0(G)$ is uniformly rigid. Via the Fourier-Stieltjes transform, these results describe the recurrence and rigidity properties of convolution operators on $L^1(G)$.

papers.title: Mathematical analysis and vectorized FEM implementation of logarithmic strain space framework for finite strains: a case study on elastoplasticity
papers.authors: Miroslav Frost, Martin Kru\v{z}\'ik, Alexej Moskovka, Jan Valdman
papers.abstract: We investigate the mathematical and computational aspects of the logarithmic strain space framework for finite-strain models in nonlinear continuum mechanics, focusing on the classical von Mises elastoplastic model with linear kinematic hardening. To overcome the lack of coercivity and lower-semicontinuity in the quadratic Hencky energy, we introduce higher-gradient regularization and prove the existence of energetic solutions for rate-independent quasistatic evolution under time-dependent Dirichlet loading. Complementarily, we develop a vectorized MATLAB finite-element implementation of the framework leveraging page-wise matrix functions and operations, and our custom vectorization library. Computational benchmarks show that local tensor operations are significantly accelerated, the logarithmic-strain approach does not substantially increase computational costs, and the implementation robustly handles large rotations and deformations.

papers.title: Geometric folding and maximal asymptotic variance
papers.abstract: Based on the recent breakthroughs by OpenAI and consequently by Binder-Ivrii-Prause-Smirnov, we develop a finite-scale folding method for the nonlinearity of a schlicht function, based on a signed critical-point count for superharmonic potentials and a quantitative target cutoff. Furthermore, we use a cylindrical root transform to reduce the logarithmic cost of access to the point at infinity. Combined with a Littlewood-Paley formula as well as dilation, the method yields the maximal asymptotic variance bound $\Sigma_{\max}^2\le1$ for the unrestricted schlicht class of normalized univalent functions.

papers.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization
papers.abstract: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.

papers.title: On the Monotonicity of Information Measures
papers.abstract: We study the monotonicity of information measures, functions that assign a value to each statistical experiment, with respect to the Blackwell and Lehmann orders. We show that such monotonicity can be characterized by local, first-order conditions. Under natural invariance properties, a measure is Blackwell monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of signal replacements, and Lehmann monotone if and only if it decreases in the direction of reverse signal replacements, which replace signals with higher ones only in low states or with lower ones only in high states. We translate both conditions into the space of posterior beliefs and apply them to likelihood-separable and posterior-separable measures, showing in particular that the entropy cost is Lehmann monotone. Among posterior-separable measures, we further identify a Lehmann monotone subclass, posterior-mean-ratio measures, that characterizes the Lehmann order.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
papers.authors: Zhen Qin, Casey Jameson, Alireza Goldar, Michael B. Wakin, Zhexuan Gong, Zhihui Zhu
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.

papers.title: Graph Fourier Neural Kernels: Learning Full PDE Trajectories Across Geometries and Anisotropic Parameter Fields
papers.authors: Shane E. Loeffler, Zan Ahmad, Shiyi Chen, Syed Yusuf Ali, Carolyna Yamamoto, Kensuke Sakata, Dan M. Popescu, Alana Yee, Yash Lal, Natalia Trayanova, Mauro Maggioni
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulations of time-dependent nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) are expensive to repeat across families of domains and parameter fields, a cost that recurs in design optimization, uncertainty quantification, and computational medicine. Most neural-operator surrogates require each domain to be mapped onto a common grid or reference shape, and few predict the full time course. We introduce Graph Fourier Neural Kernels (G-FuNK), a neural operator for second-order semilinear PDEs with a diffusive principal part that transfers across geometries and anisotropic diffusion tensors without coordinate maps or diffeomorphisms. A weighted graph and its Laplacian supply a spectral basis that encodes geometry and anisotropy. Shared layers act in this basis, at a cost linear in mesh size after one partial eigendecomposition per geometry, and a neural ODE integrator propagates the learned generator to full spatiotemporal trajectories on unseen domains. Across anisotropic heat flow, stiff reaction-diffusion, FitzHugh-Nagumo, and patient-specific left-atrial electrophysiology on CT-derived surfaces, G-FuNK reproduces held-out trajectories with relative $L^2$ error between 0.046 and 0.160. Its accuracy is comparable to that of a geometry-aware Fourier neural operator on regular domains, and its predictions are unchanged when a rectangular domain is rotated. On left atria, whose venous and valvular openings prevent mapping onto a reference shape, it predicts an 85-ms trajectory in under half a second, against about 5 minutes for finite elements, with a mean activation-time error of 1.73 ms. Accuracy depends on graph construction and is highest when the learned generator is integrated at its training time step.

papers.title: Neural Window Decoding of Spatially Coupled LDPC Codes: Exploiting Window Structure for Learning and Adaptation
papers.authors: Dae-Young Yun, Hee-Youl Kwak, Sang-Hyo Kim, Yongjune Kim, Jong-Seon No
papers.abstract: We propose a neural window decoder (NWD) for spatially coupled low-density parity-check (SC-LDPC) codes. The proposed methods adapt neural min-sum decoding to the structure and sequential operation of window decoding. First, target-oriented training restricts the loss to the variable nodes whose decisions are required at each window stage. Second, learned damping factors identify check-node updates that can reuse messages from the preceding iteration. Finally, adaptive weight switching selects weights trained for unreliable inherited information when a previous-window failure is detected. For a length-$20{,}000$ $(3,6)$-regular SC-LDPC code, the target-oriented NWD achieves performance comparable to sum-product window decoding while using min-sum updates. On the reduced target graph, scheduling based on regularized damping factors yields an estimated computational cost 48\% lower than that of full-graph weighted min-sum decoding, while maintaining comparable decoding performance. Adaptive weight switching improves decoding performance by 35\% at 3.0 dB relative to plain weights. These learning methods exploit the properties of window decoding to improve the reliability and computational efficiency of SC-LDPC convolutional codes.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Markov-Switching Ordinary Differential Processes
papers.authors: Katherine Tsai, Mladen Kolar, Sanmi Koyejo
papers.abstract: Complex systems often evolve in continuous time but are observed only at discrete time points with measurement noise. When the interactions can change across unobserved states, recovering both the state transitions and the differential equations is important for mechanistic insight and for identifying time-varying directed graphs. However, this recovery is challenging in high dimensions. In this paper, we study estimation and graph recovery for high-dimensional Markov-switching ordinary differential equation models from noisy discrete observations. We model the switching between states by a latent continuous-time Markov chain, and within each state the drift is a sparse additive function with unknown nonlinear components. We approximate each component by a finite basis expansion and estimate the parameters under group sparsity. Our procedure estimates the latent trajectories by wavelet smoothing and then runs a penalized surrogate expectation-maximization algorithm. Under stationarity and geometric $\beta$-mixing, given a sufficiently accurate estimated trajectory and other local regularity conditions, we show that the algorithm converges geometrically to a neighborhood of the true parameters. Finally, in an application to resting-state fMRI data, the procedure identifies multiple connectivity states, whose occupation times we compare descriptively between the children with combined-type ADHD and the typically developing children used in the fit.

papers.title: Exploring specialization and sensitivity of convolutional neural networks under simultaneous image augmentations
papers.authors: Pavel Kharyuk, Sergey Matveev, Ivan Oseledets
papers.abstract: Drawing parallels with the way biological networks are studied, the authors adapt the treatment--control paradigm to explainable artificial intelligence research and enrich it through multi-parametric input alterations. A framework for investigating internal inference impacted by input data augmentations is proposed to address the real-world scenario with multiple simultaneously applied treatments instead of observing a single effect. The internal changes in network operation are reflected in activation changes measured by variance, which can be decomposed into components related to each augmentation by employing Sobol indices and Shapley values. To facilitate distinguishing model-related specifics from the self-interactions of augmentations, an auxiliary variable responsible for their permutations has been incorporated into the analysis. The resulting quantities enable one to visualize sensitivity to different variables and use them as features for further analysis and processing, including guided masking of activations. In addition, a method for single-class sensitivity analysis is introduced through a pipeline that involves class selection according to their match with the prediction bias generated by targeted damaging of the activations. Three convolutional networks, namely AlexNet, VGG11, and ResNet18, have been evaluated via the designed framework, with two vision transformers, ViT-b-16 and Swin-t, partially complementing the findings. Two sets of augmentations, consisting of five and seven distinct input transformations applied simultaneously, have been utilized as sources of variance in the image domain. Relying on the observed parallels, the authors assume that the developed framework can potentially be transferred to the study of biological neural networks in complex environments, as well as enhance the design of autonomous decision-making systems.

papers.title: On the Depth of Monotone ReLU Neural Networks and ICNNs
papers.authors: Egor Bakaev, Florestan Brunck, Christoph Hertrich, Daniel Reichman, Amir Yehudayoff
papers.abstract: We study two models of $\mathsf{ReLU}$ neural networks: monotone networks ($\mathsf{ReLU}^+$) and input convex neural networks ($\mathsf{ICNN}$). Our focus is on expressivity, mostly in terms of depth, and our motivation is to gain a better understanding of the depth required to exactly represent functions using neural networks with ReLU activations, a subject that has received a lot of attention lately. We prove several lower bounds on the depth required to represent functions by monotone ReLU networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$. For the maximum function $\mathsf{MAX}_n$ computing the maximum of $n$ real numbers, we show that $\mathsf{ReLU}^+$ networks cannot compute $\mathsf{MAX}_n$, or even approximate it. We prove a sharp lower bound of $n-1$ on the $\mathsf{ICNN}$ depth complexity of $\mathsf{MAX}_n$. We also prove depth separations between $\mathsf{ReLU}$ networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$s; for every $k$, there is a depth-$2$ $\mathsf{ReLU}$ network of size $O(k^2)$ that cannot be simulated by a depth-$k$ $\mathsf{ICNN}$.
